• Full Pro Fabric features: SQL/Redis persistence on Fabric runtime, login reserve cache wiring on Fabric, visitor mode on Fabric, advanced performance.yml toggles on Fabric. These ship to BBB Pro and do not gate the Modrinth lite publish.
  • bStats on Fabric (tracked in MULTI_PLATFORM_PLAN.md, row metrics = new Metrics(this, 30865)). Possible but not yet wired: no official bstats-fabric artifact, so do it via a shaded/community bStats Metrics/MetricsBase copy or a small custom submitter to the bStats v2 data endpoint on an RTP.scheduler async timer, registering RTP's chart catalogue through metrics-api (MetricsSnapshot / FabricMetricsBinding). rtp-fabric-only; D-005 gated. Not a Modrinth-publish blocker.
  • Forge / NeoForge support (Phase 5+ per MULTI_PLATFORM_PLAN.md, out of scope until Fabric stabilizes).
  • Cross-server proxy support on Fabric (independent axis per MULTI_SERVER_PLAN.md).

docs.title: Ordering recommendation
docs.text:
Run phases sequentially: B (safety blockers) -> C (feature sweep) -> D (smoke test) -> E (publish surface + docs).

Within Phase C, the items are mostly independent except C1 which is foundational; do C1 first, then C2-C7 in any order. C5 (effects/events) is the most likely to surface real bugs because it has the most existing partial work.

Within Phase B, B2 is trivial and can be done first as a warm-up. B1 is the substantive safety fix.

docs.title: Resume protocol
docs.text:
This file follows the AGENTS.md Checklist-Based State Tracking contract. On resume:

  1. Read the latest <UPDATE> for context.
  2. Re-read this file.
  3. Re-verify the last [x] item still holds (file unchanged, test still green, build still clean).
  4. Continue from the first [ ] item.

When all boxes are ticked and Phase E is complete, delete this file (per the scratch-doc protocol; promote any durable findings to docs/dev/ first).

docs.title: Modrinth Listing Optimization - Working Notes
docs.text:
Status: scratch / working notes (gitignored under docs/dev/scratch/). Source conversation: 2026-05-19, migration from SpigotMC to Modrinth. Author: drafted by Junie at user request; not canonical until promoted to docs/marketing/ or an ADR.

This document distills the six Gemini-suggested marketing tactics into a repo-specific action plan. Each item is filtered against what actually exists in this codebase (modules, ADRs, build pipeline) so the recommendations are concrete, not generic.

docs.title: TL;DR ranking (by return-on-effort)
docs.text:
1. Automated Modrinth releases via GitHub Actions (point 4) - recurring downloads, zero ongoing cost.
  2. Modrinth README rewrite emphasizing architecture + diagrams (points 1 + 2) - one-time write, biggest first-impression delta.
  3. SpigotMC funnel banner edit (point 5) - 10-minute edit to two .bbcode files.
  4. Support-expectations section on the Modrinth page (point 3) - short, sets SLA boundaries.
  5. Hold the platform-compatibility claims to what is actually stable (point 6) - Fabric stays off the supported list until Phase 4 closes.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Correct direction. Modrinth's audience skews toward Paper/Folia admins who read READMEs and care about MSPT. The differentiators in this repo are real, not marketing fluff:

  • Archimedean spiral 1D mapping - ADR-001. Bounded worst-case attempts, O(1) coordinate generation, no unbounded reroll loop.
  • L1 / L2 / L3 cache tiering (keptLocations / unkeptLocations / backlogLocations) - ADR-028. Most competitors pick on-demand.
  • Anvil NBT pre-filter - ADR-016. Biome/material checks without loading chunks.
  • Count-bound pipeline on Folia (vs Time-Bound on Spigot/Paper) - preserves region-thread budgets.
  • MemoryTracker lifecycle for chunk tickets and pipeline tasks - release on every exit path (S-002).
  • Zero synchronous chunk I/O on the main thread (S-005) verified by ReqRtpS005ChunkLoadingTest and related guards.

docs.title: Caveat
docs.text: Do not trash "legacy plugins with quadtrees." That tone reads as marketing on a technical audience and invites pedantic rebuttals. State the trade-off honestly instead - the spiral is not strictly faster than a quadtree for every query, it is a different shape of trade-off (bounded distribution, cheap 1D index, no rejection sampling).

docs.title: Concrete next step
docs.text:
Draft docs/marketing/MODRINTH_README.md distilled from docs/dev/CONCEPTS.md plus ADR-001 / ADR-016 / ADR-028. Audience: admins evaluating in under 60 seconds, not contributors.

Sketch outline:

  1. One-line value prop ("Async-only random teleport for Paper, Folia, and Bukkit, with pre-verified location cache and bounded spiral coverage").
  2. Bullet list of measurable claims (no synchronous chunk loads; pre-verified pool; count-bound on Folia).
  3. Three-image gallery (see point 2).
  4. Config sample (the simplest possible).
  5. Links to deep docs (docs/dev/INDEX.md) for the technical reader.
  6. Support expectations (see point 3).

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: Agree. Low cost, high payoff. Modrinth renders embedded images from the project gallery and from raw GitHub URLs.

docs.title: Assets to produce
docs.text:
• Spiral coverage plot (uniform distribution over a bounded annulus). The repo already has Python Test Scripts/Circle Curve/ which presumably emits something close.
  • Pipeline diagram (shape -> chunk -> vert -> biome -> safety) annotated with which stages are async on which platform.
  • Cache-tier diagram (L1 hot / L2 cold / L3 backlog) - translates ADR-028 into something an admin grasps in one look.

Static PNGs only. No animated SVGs, no clever interactive widgets.

docs.title: Concrete next step
docs.text: docs/marketing/img/ directory, three PNGs, referenced by relative path from the future Modrinth README and by raw-GitHub URL from the Modrinth listing.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Agree on the principle (set expectations explicitly), disagree that a Discord is required. GitHub Issues already exists, SUPPORT.md already exists.

What is missing is a one-paragraph "how to report a bug" on the Modrinth page itself with explicit "best-effort, no SLA" language. The Discord-vs-no-Discord question is a personal-bandwidth decision, not a strategic one - adding a Discord obligates moderation.

docs.title: Do not link from the Modrinth page
docs.text:
• docs/dev/POTENTIAL_BUGS.md - internal stay-on-task policy, not user-facing.
  • .junie/AGENTS.md - internal contributor / agent contract.

docs.title: Do link
docs.text:
• SUPPORT.md
  • CHANGELOG.md
  • docs/dev/INDEX.md (signals seriousness to technical evaluators without writing fresh marketing copy)

docs.title: Known-limitations section
docs.text:
Worth being upfront about. Per docs/dev/MULTI_PLATFORM_PLAN.md:

  • Fabric (rtp-fabric) is the current frontier and unstable; do not claim Fabric support on the Modrinth page yet (see point 6).
  • Forge / NeoForge: out of scope until Fabric stabilizes (Phase 4).
  • Velocity / BungeeCord: planned via rtp-proxy per ADR-036, Phase 1 unblocked, not yet user-installable.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Highest-ROI item on the list. Aligns with how Modrinth's discovery works (Recently Updated feed, follower notifications). The blocker is not tooling; the discipline already exists:

  • CHANGELOG Hygiene rule in .junie/AGENTS.md enforces net-delta-from-released-tag - exactly the hygiene that makes frequent releases safe.
  • Jenkinsfile already builds; adding a GitHub Actions release path does not displace it.
  • The lite-assembly variant (ADR-024) gives two artifacts per release - more surface area on the Modrinth page.

docs.title: Concrete next step
docs.text:
.github/workflows/release.yml triggered on v* tag push:

  1. Run .\gradlew build (full multi-module, per the AGENTS.md Final Full Build rule).
  2. Upload main jar and lite jar via modrinth/minotaur@v2.
  3. Pull the matching CHANGELOG section as the Modrinth release notes (already in net-delta form, so this is correct by construction).
  4. Tag the Modrinth release with the loaders the build actually supports (paper, folia, bukkit; not fabric - see point 6) and the MC versions matching rtp-bukkit-v* / rtp-paper-v* / rtp-folia-v* submodules.

Secrets required: MODRINTH_TOKEN. Out of scope for this scratch doc to author the workflow - captured here as the next deliverable.

docs.title: Release cadence policy (proposed)
docs.text:
• Patch / beta releases on every meaningful bugfix or single-issue change that passes the full build.
  • Minor releases when a feature lands behind a config flag.
  • Major releases reserved for breaking API changes (rtp-api surface) - these need release notes plus a migration paragraph.

Avoid the "save up features for a big release" anti-pattern Gemini called out. The CHANGELOG hygiene already supports small-frequent.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text: Agree tactically. SEO point is real: SpigotMC outranks Modrinth for legacy queries, and the existing docs/FRONT_PAGE.bbcode plus docs/FRONT_PAGE_LITE.bbcode are ready to retarget.

docs.title: Do
docs.text:
• Add a prominent banner at the top of both .bbcode files: "Latest builds, Folia tags, and beta channels live on Modrinth: ." Keep the language welcoming, not aggressive.
  • Keep the latest stable on Spigot so existing users do not lose access.
  • Push betas, Folia-tagged builds, and the lite variant to Modrinth only. That asymmetry is the natural funnel - people who want the new thing learn where to look.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Fully cripple Spigot downloads. That creates support load from confused users who cannot find anything and damages reputation.
  • Edit FRONT_PAGE.bbcode while also changing semantic content; keep the funnel edit isolated for an auditable diff.

docs.title: Concrete next step
docs.text:
Two-file edit, ~10 minutes, low risk:

  • docs/FRONT_PAGE.bbcode
  • docs/FRONT_PAGE_LITE.bbcode

Both files are user-facing marketing copy; per .junie/AGENTS.md Markdown Encoding Hygiene, use ASCII punctuation (no em dashes) and verify no mojibake before submit.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Already in progress; do not over-promise. Current state per repo:

  • Bukkit / Paper / Folia: first-class, all green.
  • Fabric (rtp-fabric): active frontier, unstable. Known blockers per MULTI_PLATFORM_PLAN.md:
  • S-005 violation in FabricWorld.getChunkAt.
  • Null stub in FabricServerAccessor.getLocationGenerator.
  • Unresolved Loom dependency.
  • Velocity / BungeeCord: Phase 0 complete (ADR-036), Phase 1 unblocked, no user-installable artifact yet.
  • Forge / NeoForge: out of scope until Fabric stabilizes (Phase 4).

docs.title: Pterodactyl auto-pull
docs.text: Real lever and worth optimising for. Pterodactyl eggs query Modrinth's API by project_id and resolve the latest version matching the egg's declared loader and MC version. Implication: the more accurate the loader / MC-version tags on each Modrinth release, the more automated installs happen. This is purely a tagging discipline question, not a code question.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• List Fabric as "supported" on the Modrinth page until Phase 4 closes. Listing an unstable platform damages exactly the technical-admin reputation that point 1 is trying to build.
  • Mirror the rtp-proxy artifacts to Modrinth before Phase 1+ is user-installable. Mark them as planned only.

docs.title: Items Gemini did not surface that matter more
docs.text:
• Modrinth loader / version tags are the actual discoverability lever. Tag every release with the exact MC versions and loaders. Admins filter the project search by these; the README is secondary.
  • The lite jar is a marketing asset, not just a technical one. "Drop-in, no config, small footprint" framing on Modrinth captures a different audience than the full feature set. Make the lite jar a separate "version" on the Modrinth project rather than a buried download.
  • The existing docs/dev/ tree is a moat. It is unusually thorough for a Minecraft plugin. A one-line "Full developer documentation: " on the Modrinth page signals seriousness to the admin demographic point 1 targets, with zero new writing.
  • Locale parity is a quiet selling point. The locale TSV pipeline and LocaleParityTest guarantee that shipped locales never silently fall back to English - worth one bullet on the Modrinth page for international audiences ("ships with N locales, parity-enforced").
  • Don't gate on a Modrinth project description rewrite. The Modrinth README and the GitHub README can stay separate. The GitHub README is for contributors; the Modrinth README is for admins. Tailor each to its audience.

docs.title: Open questions for the user
docs.text:
1. Discord channel: create one or not? Defaults to "not" unless the user wants the moderation load.
  2. Modrinth project URL / slug already reserved?
  3. Who holds the MODRINTH_TOKEN and is willing to add it as a GitHub Actions secret?
  4. Spigot resource: keep it active indefinitely, or sunset after N releases on Modrinth?
  5. Do we want the lite jar promoted as a "version" on the same Modrinth project, or its own project?

docs.title: Next deliverable shortlist
docs.text:
If the user picks any one of these, switch to [CODE] mode and execute:

  • A - Draft .github/workflows/release.yml (Minotaur upload on tag push).
  • B - Draft docs/marketing/MODRINTH_README.md (admin-facing, distilled from docs/dev/CONCEPTS.md + ADRs).
  • C - Edit docs/FRONT_PAGE.bbcode and docs/FRONT_PAGE_LITE.bbcode to add the Modrinth funnel banner.
  • D - Generate the three marketing PNGs into docs/marketing/img/.
  • E - Add a "Known Limitations" + "Support" section to whichever README ships to Modrinth.

Recommended order: A, then B + D together, then C, then E. Each step is independently submittable and independently revertible.

docs.title: Plan: Resolve English Bleed in Shipped Locales
docs.text: Working note. Delete once the remediation campaign is complete.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Many baseline keys across messages.yml, safety.yml, performance.yml, config.yml, logging.yml, integrations.yml, economy.yml, and metrics.yml have been added or rewritten over time and the reconcile step (scripts/reconcile-locale-csvs.ps1) correctly seeded the new rows from the English baseline. Step 4 of the Locale Config TSV Pipeline in .junie/AGENTS.md (the translation step) has been repeatedly skipped, leaving the seeded English values in the locale TSVs and therefore in lang/<locale>/<file>.yml. The "Generalized Menu Framework" section in messages.yml is one acute case; the broader symptom is much larger.

docs.title: Current Bleed (as of this snapshot)
docs.text:
Counts below are rows in scripts/out/locale-<lang>.tsv whose value column is byte-identical to the matching English baseline value (i.e. an unmistakable un-translated row). Joins on (filename, parent_path, base_key, index). Empty values and rows with no English baseline are excluded.

Per locale (% is English/non-empty):

pl   369 nonempty   349 still English   94.6%
de   361 nonempty   268 still English   74.2%
fr   361 nonempty   262 still English   72.6%
cat  232 nonempty   156 still English   67.2%   (note: cat is Internet-Cat dialect, not a Romance lang)
nl   238 nonempty   155 still English   65.1%
ja   232 nonempty   145 still English   62.5%
ko   232 nonempty   145 still English   62.5%
zh   232 nonempty   145 still English   62.5%
pt   230 nonempty   132 still English   57.4%
es   232 nonempty   131 still English   56.5%
ru   230 nonempty   127 still English   55.2%
it   238 nonempty   128 still English   53.8%

By file (summed across all locales):

messages.yml           925
safety.yml             386
performance.yml        224
config.yml             188
logging.yml            168
integrations.yml       108
economy.yml             84
metrics.yml             60

Total bleed: ~2143 rows. Note: cat should be Cat-dialect-translated, not skipped; see Domain Analogies & Aliases in .junie/AGENTS.md.

docs.title: Constraints (must hold)
docs.text:
1. No hand-edits to lang/<locale>/*.yml or *.lang.yml. The TSV pipeline is the source of truth. Hand-edits will be wiped on the next reconcile.
  2. One locale at a time beats one ten-locale shot for quality (TRANSLATION_GUIDE.md §8).
  3. Mask placeholders, color codes, doc-tags before machine-translating:
  4. [placeholder] segments (e.g. [player], [command], [type], [values]).
  5. Color codes: &a, &l, etc., and hex #RRGGBB sequences.
  6. Section markers §.
  7. Doc-tags: @type, @range, @unit, @default, @options (these must remain verbatim in comments).
  8. URLs, version banners, file names.
  9. UTF-8, no BOM, LF line endings. Existing TSVs contain pre-existing mojibake (e.g. MenÃ¼ instead of Menü in locale-de.tsv). Fix mojibake on rows you touch, do not sweep otherwise (per Markdown Encoding Hygiene).
  10. @type/@range/@unit/@default/@options lines in preceding_comment must not be translated. Only the prose around them.
  11. Pre-existing native translations are precious. Do not overwrite a non-English value just because it differs from the baseline. The audit specifically looks for value == English-baseline.

docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
Translation will happen out-of-band in a separate AI session (user preference: faster interface). To make that safe and resumable, we need three deterministic helpers around the existing TSV pipeline:

  1. Auditor: enumerate every row whose value is byte-identical to the English baseline value, exporting a small focused TSV per (locale, file) — the Bleed Manifest.
  2. Bundle Exporter: package one locale's Bleed Manifest as a self-contained input file for an external AI session. Format: a markdown document containing the English baseline value, the comment block, the base_key/parent_path/index coordinates, and an empty # locale_value: field for the translator to fill. Placeholders/color codes pre-masked with sentinels <<P0>>, <<P1>>, …; a sentinel legend is printed at the top so the translator does not corrupt them.
  3. Bundle Importer: read the translator's filled bundle back, unmask sentinels, validate that every placeholder/color code was preserved, and patch the corresponding rows in scripts/out/locale-<lang>.tsv in place. Validation rules:
  4. Same set of [placeholder] tokens.
  5. Same set of &x color codes and hex codes (order-insensitive).
  6. Same trailing/leading whitespace policy as the baseline value.
  7. Non-empty locale_value (empty = leave row English, mark # TODO(i18n):).
  8. Mojibake check: refuse to import rows containing â€, Â, Ã, âœ, âŒ, ðŸ, or \uFFFD.

After bundle import for a locale: - Run .\scripts\reconcile-locale-csvs.ps1 (sanity round-trip). - Run .\scripts\locale-files-from-csv.ps1 to regenerate lang/<locale>/*.yml. - Run .\gradlew :rtp-plugin:test --tests "*LocaleParityTest*". - Run .\gradlew build.

docs.title: Sequencing (one locale per PR, large-bleed first)
docs.text:
Priority order picks worst-bleed-first while keeping each PR independently reviewable:

  1. pl (94.6%, 349 rows) — biggest payoff.
  2. de (74.2%, 268 rows).
  3. fr (72.6%, 262 rows).
  4. cat (67.2%, 156 rows) — Cat-dialect, needs the cat-themed vocabulary from .junie/AGENTS.md Domain Analogies & Aliases row. Cannot be machine-translated as a natural language.
  5. nl (65.1%, 155 rows).
  6. ja / ko / zh (62.5%, 145 rows each) — non-Latin scripts; placeholder masking is critical.
  7. pt (57.4%, 132 rows).
  8. es (56.5%, 131 rows) — also has ReqRtpF013SpanishLocaleContentTest content guards; do not break them.
  9. ru (55.2%, 127 rows).
  10. it (53.8%, 128 rows).

Each locale: one branch, one PR, one LocaleParityTest + full build before submitting.

docs.title: Out-of-Scope for This Plan
docs.text:
• Sweeping the existing mojibake in non-touched rows. Record incidental hits in POTENTIAL_BUGS.md per Stay-On-Task Policy. Touched-row mojibake is fixed by the import validator.
  • Adding new baseline keys. If the user wants a new key, they go through the normal Locale Config TSV Pipeline and add the row in the same change; this plan is about catching up on already-merged baseline keys.
  • The shape/<x>.lang.yml and vert/<x>.lang.yml rename-map files. They live in the locale TSV directly and follow the same workflow but are not currently part of the bleed audit (their values are short identifier strings, not prose).

docs.title: Deliverables for This Session
docs.text:
Below the line, the auditor + bundle scripts and a sample bundle for pl (largest bleed) to validate the end-to-end loop. The scripts are idempotent and operate purely on scripts/out/*.tsv; no lang/ edits.

  • scripts/audit-locale-bleed.ps1 — audit only, prints summary and writes scripts/out/bleed-<lang>.tsv.
  • scripts/export-translation-bundle.ps1 -Locale <lang> — emits scripts/out/bundle-<lang>.md.
  • scripts/import-translation-bundle.ps1 -Locale <lang> — reads back scripts/out/bundle-<lang>.md (or another path), validates, patches scripts/out/locale-<lang>.tsv.

docs.title: PLAN - Plugin-Message Network Transport implementation
docs.text:
Status: In progress - Slices A-H landed; Slice G complete (liteJarStructureCheck now excludes/forbids the proxy/common/transport/{redis,sql}/ subtrees that were leaking into lite and asserts the plugin-message binding/resolver present; check passes) and Slice H complete (Velocity audit: the BungeeCord vocabulary is handled natively by Velocity core, no proxy code needed; finding recorded in rtp-proxy-ADR-016); Slice B item 7 (Bukkit shim) + Slice D item 19 landed so the tier-1 transport is live on Bukkit/Paper/Folia; Slice I (docs/CHANGELOG sync + final gate), the command-tree wiring of NetworkRegionParameter, and the deferred Fabric/NeoForge shims (item 8) remain (see per-slice boxes + the progress note below).

Progress note (2026-06-12): Slice A (shared BackendHeartbeatCodec, Redis+SQL repointed), Slice B item 6/9 (NetworkBridge seam + inline FakeNetworkBridge), Slice C (PluginMessageNetworkBinding + tests), a minimal item 19 (RTP.networkBridgeFactory hook + plugin-message/auto cases in NetworkModeBootstrap.openTransport, auto resolves silently to disabled with no proxy bridge), and the Slice D state machine (ProxyAutoDetector items 16-18 + the NetworkBridge.requestTopology()/registerTopology()/Topology active-handshake default methods, ProxyAutoDetectorTest 5/5, item 20) are implemented and verified by .\gradlew build. Still open: the Bukkit NetworkBridge shim (Slice B item 7) and the full bootstrap wiring that constructs/pumps ProxyAutoDetector and resolves auto to plugin-message on ENABLED (item 19 full), NetworkRegionParameter (E), network.yml schema + locale pipeline (F), lite-jar audit extension (G), Velocity channel handling (H), and the docs/CHANGELOG sync (I). Progress note (2026-06-13, Option 1 - topology-seeded candidates): Symptom "only /rtp region=default works on a lobby" root-caused to the single-player plugin-message gossip limitation: a player-empty backend cannot carry its heartbeat, so the heartbeat-fed NetworkSnapshot (the sole source for PeerRegionRegistry.peerEntries()/isReachableHardPin) stays empty on the lite tier and every server:region destination is rejected/unsuggested. Owner (leaf) chose Option 1: seed cross-server destinations from the proxy's GetServers topology (only needs the local server's own player connection). Implemented in PeerRegionRegistry (new setTopologyPeerSupplier/setAssumedRegionSupplier; peerEntries() surfaces server:default for proxy-advertised peers lacking a heartbeat, isReachableHardPin accepts topology-known servers under "unknown -> accept" while a live killSwitch or a concrete heartbeat region set still wins) and wired in NetworkModeBootstrap from ProxyAutoDetector.peerServerIds(). New PeerRegionRegistryTest topology cases + existing suites green; full .\gradlew build green. (Blank /rtp lobby dispatch via pickMostKept() still needs real heartbeat metrics and is out of this fix's scope.)

Date: 2026-06-12 Owner: leaf (repo owner) Implements: approved proposal docs/dev/scratch/PROPOSAL-plugin-message-network-default.md; contract ADR platforms/rtp-proxy/docs/adr/rtp-proxy-ADR-016-plugin-message-default-transport.md; amendments to ADR-036, ADR-024, MULTI_SERVER_PLAN.md. Reuses (no SPI change): NetworkTransport, BackendHeartbeat, NetworkSnapshot, BackendSelector in rtp-proxy-common; BackendHeartbeat flat-field encode/decode currently private in RedisNetworkStateBinding.

Build order is dependency-first: a slice never depends on a later slice. Each slice ends green (its own tests pass) before the next starts; the final full build (.\gradlew build) is the last gate before submit. Every slice is independently revertible.

docs.title: 0. Anchored seams (verified in the codebase)
docs.text:
• rtp-core -> NetworkModeBootstrap.openTransport(type, intervalMs, transportSec, verifier, schemaVersion) is the single switch that constructs a NetworkTransport from transport.type. It currently handles in-memory / sql / redis. This is where plugin-message and auto plug in.
  • rtp-proxy-common -> NetworkBindings.open(cfg, dataSource) is the proxy-side factory mirror of the same switch (used by the Velocity/Bungee adapters). Keep the two switches in sync.
  • InMemoryNetworkStateBinding implements NetworkTransport is the reference peer to mirror: methods publishBackendHeartbeat, readSnapshot, subscribeBackendHeartbeats, claim/release/redeem/findReservation/reapExpired/listActiveForServer, publishProxyHeartbeat, close.
  • RedisNetworkStateBinding.encodeBackend(BackendHeartbeat) (+ the matching decode) is private; SqlNetworkStateBinding already duplicates the same field order. Both must move to a shared codec before tier-1 can reuse it (Slice A).
  • transport.type is parsed by NetworkConfig (proxy side) and read from RtpYamlSection in NetworkModeBootstrap (backend side).

docs.title: Slice A - Extract a shared BackendHeartbeat codec (no behaviour change)
docs.text:
Goal: one encoder/decoder shared by Redis, SQL, and the new plugin-message tier, so all tiers carry an identical field set (proposal §9.1).

  • [x] 1. Add BackendHeartbeatCodec in rtp-proxy-common (...transport.codec), with encode(BackendHeartbeat): String / decode(String): BackendHeartbeat, lifted verbatim from RedisNetworkStateBinding.encodeBackend/decode (preserve exact field order - the HMAC in Redis signs over it).
  • [x] 2. Repoint RedisNetworkStateBinding to call the shared codec; delete its private copies. Keep the HMAC layer wrapping the codec output unchanged (codec must stay HMAC-agnostic).
  • [x] 3. Repoint SqlNetworkStateBinding (line ~543, "order matches RedisNetworkStateBinding.encodeBackend") to the shared codec.
  • [x] 4. Tests: a BackendHeartbeatCodecRoundTripTest (encode->decode identity for a fully-populated BackendHeartbeat, incl. empty/optional fields); run existing RedisNetworkStateBinding* and SqlNetworkStateBinding* suites to prove no regression.
  • [x] 5. .\gradlew :rtp-proxy-common:test green.

Risk: field-order drift breaks the Redis HMAC. Mitigation: codec is byte-identical to the old private method; round-trip + existing Redis signed-snapshot test guard it.

docs.title: Slice B - NetworkBridge seam (rtp-core) + per-platform send/receive shim
docs.text:
Goal: the raw "send these bytes on bungeecord:main over player P's connection / receive bytes" primitive, the only platform-specific surface (proposal §3, decision §9.2). Not Bukkit-only.

  • [x] 6. Define NetworkBridge interface in rtp-core (...common.network.pluginmessage):
  • void sendViaPlayer(UUID carrier, String subChannel, byte[] payload) (Forward/Connect framing built above this, see Slice C),
  • void registerInbound(Consumer<byte[]> sink),
  • Optional<UUID> anyOnlinePlayer() (carrier selection),
  • ProxyProbe passiveProbe() returning { armed: boolean } from spigot.yml/paper-global.yml,
  • boolean isAvailable() (platform actually wired).
  • [x] 7. Bukkit shim BukkitNetworkBridge in rtp-bukkit-common: register bungeecord:main outgoing + incoming via Messenger, sendPluginMessage on a Player, read paper-global.yml/spigot.yml for the passive probe. Wire it into the Bukkit network bootstrap path. Done: BukkitNetworkBridge frames Forward (sub-channel RTPNet) / Connect / GetServer(s), decodes inbound via a PluginMessageListener, and the passive probe reads spigot.yml settings.bungeecord + paper-global.yml proxies.{bungee-cord,velocity}.enabled. Installed via RTP.networkBridgeFactory in AbstractServerAccessor.start(Object) (alongside the ADR-049 sampler factory), so the existing plugin-message/auto cases in openTransport now resolve to a live binding. sendPluginMessage is called directly (netty-queued, off-thread safe); a Folia region-thread-affine send refinement remains an optional follow-up.
  • [ ] 8. (Deferred, not this turn) Fabric/NeoForge shims: leave a documented TODO + a no-op NetworkBridge fallback so auto resolves to disabled cleanly where no shim is installed. Capture the deferral in the plan's Notes, not as a silent gap.
  • [x] 9. Tests: a FakeNetworkBridge test double (in-JVM loopback, inline in PluginMessageNetworkBindingTest) so Slices C-E test without a live server.

Risk: carrier-player dependence (proposal §6.1). Mitigation: anyOnlinePlayer() returns Optional; absence is a normal "cannot broadcast yet" state, not an error.

docs.title: Slice C - PluginMessageNetworkBinding implements NetworkTransport (rtp-core, behind NetworkBridge)
docs.text:
Goal: the tier-1 binding (proposal §3). Peer of InMemoryNetworkStateBinding; no rtp-proxy-common SPI change.

  • [x] 10. New PluginMessageNetworkBinding (rtp-core ...common.network.pluginmessage) taking a NetworkBridge + heartbeatTicks/staleTimeoutMillis config.
  • [x] 11. publishBackendHeartbeat(row) -> BackendHeartbeatCodec.encode(row) -> bridge.sendViaPlayer(carrier, "Forward"/"ForwardToPlayer", framed), throttled to heartbeatTicks (default 200) via RTP.scheduler.runTaskTimerAsynchronously (no raw threads - guideline Scheduler Usage).
  • [x] 12. subscribeBackendHeartbeats(sink) / readSnapshot() -> maintain ConcurrentHashMap<serverId, (BackendHeartbeat, lastSeenMillis)>; expire on staleTimeoutMillis (default 1500); decode inbound via the shared codec; build NetworkSnapshot from live entries; invoke sink on change.
  • [x] 13. Move framing helper: Connect <serverId> / ConnectOther <player> <serverId> builders (used by the dispatcher's connect step, not by the binding's reservation methods).
  • [x] 14. claim/redeem/release/reapExpired/findReservation/listActiveForServer -> best-effort / no-op returning resolved empties (proposal §3, ADR-016 mapping table). Document each as "non-durable; destination decides on arrival; player re-issues on miss".
  • [x] 15. Tests (ReqRtpNet* named, traceable): heartbeat publish->gossip->snapshot round-trip over FakeNetworkBridge; TTL expiry marks a peer stale; no-op reservation methods never throw and never mint a token; carrier-absent publish is a silent skip not an error (S-004: logged at FINE, not swallowed exception).

docs.title: Slice D - auto resolver + state machine (rtp-core)
docs.text:
Goal: transport.type: auto -> proxy auto-detect (proposal §4, decision §9.5 re-probe).

  • [x] 16. ProxyAutoDetector (rtp-core) implementing the state machine UNKNOWN -> ARMED (passive probe true) -> PROBING (first join: GetServer/GetServers) -> ENABLED (reply within handshakeTimeoutMillis) | DISABLED (standalone). Heartbeat gossip starts only in ENABLED.
  • [x] 17. GetServer reply populates this backend's own proxy serverId; GetServers populates the discovered peer-name set (via the new NetworkBridge.requestTopology()/registerTopology() default-method handshake + Topology record). No hand-typed servers: list.
  • [x] 18. Re-probe hooks: onCarrierAvailable() re-probes from both ARMED and DISABLED, so a standalone server that later joins a proxy picks the network up on the next player join without a restart.
  • [x] 19. Extend NetworkModeBootstrap.openTransport: add case "plugin-message" -> new PluginMessageNetworkBinding(bridge, ...); add case "auto" -> run ProxyAutoDetector; resolve to plugin-message when ENABLED, else a disabled/no-op binding when standalone. Mirror the same two cases in NetworkBindings.open for proxy-side parity. Done: the auto case now builds a ProxyAutoDetector sharing the binding's NetworkBridge, runs evaluatePassive() (DISABLED -> silent null/standalone), opens the plugin-message tier when armed, and retains the detector; boot() pumps onCarrierAvailable() (carrier-gated active GetServer/GetServers handshake + re-probe) and tick() on RTP.scheduler at the heartbeat cadence, cancelled in shutdown(). Proxy-side mirror: NetworkBindings.open now recognises plugin-message/auto and degrades to the in-memory binding with a clear "backend-only tier" note (the real binding lives in rtp-core; a proxy has no plugin-message bridge), instead of throwing "unrecognised type".
  • [x] 20. Tests: ProxyAutoDetectorTest (5/5) covers each transition, handshake timeout -> DISABLED, re-probe on reconnect, unavailable bridge, and late-reply-ignored, driven by a manual clock + loopback bridge double. (openTransport/NetworkBindings.open class-resolution assertions deferred with the full bootstrap wiring below.)

docs.title: Slice E - NetworkRegionParameter (commands-api / command layer)
docs.text:
Goal: cross-server region tab-complete + validation with the "unknown -> accept" rule (proposal §7, §6.2).

  • [x] 21. RegionAvailabilityProvider seam (rtp-core ...common.network) with tri-state Availability + UNKNOWN_ALL; snapshot-backed SnapshotRegionAvailabilityProvider reads the same cached NetworkSnapshot as PeerRegionRegistry (transport-agnostic).
  • [x] 22. NetworkRegionParameter (rtp-core ...commands.parameters): values() = local regions + live server:region entries; isRelevant rejects only on a positive KNOWN_UNAVAILABLE verdict and accepts on UNKNOWN/stale (the load-bearing rule). isSuggestionRelevant strict (only KNOWN_AVAILABLE).
  • [x] 23. Followed the commands-api suggestion-vs-validation split (isRelevant vs isSuggestionRelevant); value form is server:region (no free positional). (Command-tree wiring of the parameter deferred with the bootstrap/Bukkit-shim wiring below.)
  • [x] 24. Tests: NetworkRegionAvailabilityTest (8/8) - provider verdicts incl. kill-switch exclusion; parameter known-available (suggest+validate), known-unavailable (no suggest, still reject), unknown server (no suggest, accept-at-execute), empty snapshot (accept-all).

docs.title: Slice F - network.yml schema + locale pipeline
docs.text:
Goal: ship the trimmed lite schema (proposal §5) through the mandated locale TSV pipeline (guideline Locale Config TSV Pipeline).

Edit the baseline rtp-plugin/src/main/resources/network.yml only: add transport.type: auto (+ plugin-message/inMemory/disabled to the documented enum), transport.pluginMessage.{channel, heartbeatTicks, staleTimeoutMillis}, and the optional servers.<name>.{permission, display-name, hide-when-unavailable, allow-when-unavailable} policy overlay (no host/port, no required list). New comment/config-token rows seeded English first-pass (guideline §4 acceptable; translators fill later).

Extend liteJarStructureCheck: assert absent RedisNetworkStateBinding, SqlNetworkStateBinding, and JDBC/Jedis/Lettuce driver classes; assert present (permitted) PluginMessageNetworkBinding + the auto resolver. Confirm the plugin-message tier pulls in no JDBC/Redis driver transitively. docs.title: Slice H - Velocity channel handling (decision §9.4: implement if absent)
docs.text:
Goal: ensure the proxy honors GetServer/GetServers/Connect/Forward on modern Velocity (proposal §9.4). BungeeCord is layered later, not this turn.

  • [x] 30. Audit rtp-proxy-velocity for the modern namespaced channel registration + the GetServers/topology handshake; add whatever is missing. Done (no code change required): the audit found rtp-proxy-velocity registers/handles no plugin-message channel at all - it operates purely at the SPI/transport level (Redis/SQL/in-memory state, dispatcher, ServerPreConnectEvent redeem). Modern Velocity honors the full BungeeCord vocabulary (Connect/ConnectOther/GetServer/GetServers/Forward/ForwardToPlayer) via its own built-in handler on bungeecord:main, gated by bungee-plugin-message-channel = true in velocity.toml (the default). The backend BukkitNetworkBridge (Slice B item 7) speaks to that native handler directly and receives replies/forwards on its registered incoming bungeecord:main channel, so nothing was missing on the proxy side. Recorded the finding in rtp-proxy-ADR-016 (Velocity audit (2026-06-13)). The optional proxy companion that holds the channel open without player presence remains a future enhancement, not a tier-1 requirement.
  • [x] 31. Tests where feasible (unit over the framing); the live 2-proxy/2-backend devstack round-trip is acceptance, tracked but not blocking the unit gates. N/A this turn: no proxy-side framing exists to unit-test (Velocity handles the vocabulary natively); the backend-side framing in BukkitNetworkBridge is thin platform glue (would need MockBukkit) and its contract is already covered by PluginMessageNetworkBindingTest via FakeNetworkBridge. The live devstack round-trip stays a separate acceptance turn (plan open item 2).

docs.title: Proposal: De-canonicalize CommandsAPI.parameterDelimiter after the : -> = migration
docs.text: Status: draft (awaiting D-005 approval) Origin: chat 2026-05-20, follow-up to the command-syntax migration from : to =.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: With : retired as the parameter delimiter, the configurability layer in commands-api is dead weight: the character is no longer data, it is a fixed grammar token. The codebase still pays the cost of an abstraction whose only historical purpose was to let the delimiter vary.

docs.title: What's currently in the way
docs.text:
• CommandsAPI.parameterDelimiter is a mutable public static char = '='. Mirror field: multiParameterDelimiter = ','.
  • ~20 call sites in commands-api/.../TreeCommand.java use String.valueOf(CommandsAPI.parameterDelimiter) to feed split / contains / indexOf / lastIndexOf.
  • Three helpers (containsParamDelimiter, indexOfParamDelimiter, splitOnParamDelimiter) wrap one-line String.indexOf('=') calls.
  • BukkitValueCoercer.legacyColorFromDelimitedString is @SuppressWarnings("unused") and self-describes as the legacy path.
  • REQ-API-F-005 is still phrased as if the delimiter were configurable.

docs.title: Proposal (phased)
docs.text:
Phase 1 - safe, mechanical, single PR. No public API removal.

  • Make parameterDelimiter and multiParameterDelimiter public static final.
  • Inside commands-api itself, replace String.valueOf(CommandsAPI.parameterDelimiter) with "=" literals at the ~20 sites; prefer char overloads of indexOf / split where the API permits.
  • Inline containsParamDelimiter and indexOfParamDelimiter. Keep splitOnParamDelimiter as the one named grammar primitive.
  • Delete BukkitValueCoercer.legacyColorFromDelimitedString.
  • Re-word REQ-API-F-005 to absolute state: "The parameter delimiter shall be =."
  • Affected modules: commands-api, effects-api. No rtp-core changes.
  • Cross-module callers (effects-api etc.) keep the named-constant reference (cheap, documents intent).

Phase 2 - only after Phase 1 lands and an addon survey confirms no consumers.

  • @Deprecated(forRemoval=true) on parameterDelimiter / multiParameterDelimiter, with Javadoc pointing to the literal.
  • Hold one major.

Phase 3 - defer to next major.

  • Remove the fields entirely.

docs.title: Risks / trade-offs
docs.text:
• Addon binary compat. parameterDelimiter is on the public commands-api surface and read transitively via effects-api. final is safe; removal is not.
  • Locale / messages.yml strings. BaseRTPCmd already builds parameterName + "=" + parameterValue. Sweep user-facing help strings for any residual name:value framing before merging.
  • Traceability. REQ-API-F-005 row in TRACEABILITY.md needs a re-check when the requirement text moves.
  • Don't over-rotate. A static final char PARAM_DELIMITER = '='; is still a useful named constant (for the Brigadier bridge and for grep-ability). The thing worth deleting is the configurability, not the name.

docs.title: Verification plan
docs.text:
• :commands-api:test, :rtp-core:test, :rtp-plugin:test --tests "*Tree*", full .\gradlew build.
  • Brigadier suggestion smoke (tab-complete still appends =).
  • LocaleParityTest (no message-text drift).

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• The reg: value-side sigil in TreeCommand.expandRegexToken. That is a sub-token marker inside the value half, not a separator, and the freed : is actually one of the upsides of the migration.
  • minecraft:-prefix stripping in BukkitValueCoercer.resolveViaRegistry / resolveSound. Tracked as a separate decanonicalization opportunity (see follow-up chat 2026-05-20).

docs.title: PROPOSAL: @options-driven finite-value pickers in the in-game config editor
docs.text: Status: APPROVED (D-005, approved 2026-08-14). ADR-064 amended to record the runtime directive consumer and the @source: shape/@source: vert registries. Discovered-during: issue "under rtp admin and associated config editor, use a menu for a set of predetermined values for something like shape.name as arbitrary input is confusing" Author: Junie (with project lead) Related: builds on PROPOSAL-config-menu-shape-vert-intuitive.md (APPROVED 2026-08-14) whose Part 2 (finite shape.name picker) was deferred; ADR-064 (config-comment summary line as menu hover); docs/dev/CONFIG_COMMENT_STYLE.md (machine-readable enumeration tags); ADR-035 / ADR-044 (menu framework).

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
In the in-game /rtp config (and rtp admin) book/chat menu, every editable config key routes to the same free-text anvil prompt. For keys with a finite, predetermined value set this is confusing and error-prone:

  • database.type accepts only yaml / sqlite / mysql / postgresql, but the editor lets the operator type anything.
  • shape.name / vert.name are type discriminators (CIRCLE / SQUARE / ...) whose value selects which sibling sub-parameters are valid; free text invites typos that silently revert to the default.
  • Many other keys are already finite: network.yml transport.type, regionCollision.policy, the load-balancer curve types and metric inputs; config.yml menu.renderer; the metrics Folia aggregation modes; etc.

Arbitrary input on a finite-domain key can never produce a valid result other than one of the known options, so a picker is strictly better UX and eliminates a class of "why didn't my change take?" support issues.

docs.title: 2. Confirmed design (agreed in discussion)
docs.text:
• Drive the finite value set from the existing @options config-comment directive. CONFIG_COMMENT_STYLE.md / ADR-064 already define # @type: enum + # @options: [...] (YAML-flow) directive lines in the block comment above each key, explicitly "for the menu system". database.yml and several others already ship them. No new metadata format is introduced.
  • Zero new file I/O. The comment text is already resident in memory: ConfigParser.getYamlRoot() returns the cached RtpYamlConfig (populated once at load/reload via loadWithComments), and RtpYamlSection.getComment(key) reads it with no disk access - exactly the path resolveConfigHover already uses for hover text at menu-open time. Parsing @options reuses that already-fetched comment string.
  • Free text stays the default. A key with no directives (or an unparseable @options) falls back to the current free-text anvil prompt - never breaks the menu.
  • This subsumes the deferred shape/vert .name picker. Rather than bespoke .name routing, shape/vert expose their finite type set via @source: shape / @source: vert (a registry-backed variant) so the same generic picker path serves them.

docs.title: 3. Affected classes / modules
docs.text:
• rtp-core new ConfigDirectives (small parser): given a key's block comment string, extract @type, @options (List), @range, @source. YAML-flow values parsed with the existing SnakeYAML loader, guarded so malformed lines degrade to "no directives".
  • rtp-core CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildConfigFile - at row-emit time, parse directives from the comment already fetched for hover; when a finite domain is present (@options, or @source for registry-backed sets), emit a picker-opening action instead of the plain free-text OpenConfigKey.
  • rtp-core CommandTreeMenuBuilder - add a generic buildOptionsPicker(fileName, key, options, current) (one row per option, current value starred, Back row, paginated), generalizing the existing buildShapeVertTypePicker. buildShapeVertTypePicker is either retired in favor of it or re-expressed as the @source: shape/vert case.
  • rtp-core MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchOpenConfigKey - before the PromptAnvilInput fallback, resolve the target key's directives; if a finite domain is declared, render the options picker via the renderer; otherwise keep the current free-text anvil path. Each option row stages key=value through the existing cart/write path (no SubConfigCmd merge change).
  • rtp-plugin resources - add @type/@options (or @source) directive lines to the block comments of finite keys that lack them (e.g. shape/vert, any finite key not yet annotated), mirrored into every lang/<locale>/<file>.yml per Locale Parity Maintenance (directives are language-neutral, copied verbatim).

docs.title: 4. Intended before/after
docs.text:
Before (database.type row, menu): 

database.type: sqlite      <- click opens a blank/free-text anvil; any string accepted

After (menu view; disk unchanged until applied): 

database.type: sqlite      <- click opens a finite picker
   -> yaml
   -> * sqlite   (current, starred)
   -> mysql
   -> postgresql

shape.name after (via @source: shape): 

shape.name: CIRCLE         <- finite picker sourced from RTP.factoryMap shape keyset
   -> * CIRCLE
   -> SQUARE

docs.title: 5. @options vs @source (design point for approval)
docs.text:
CONFIG_COMMENT_STYLE.md makes @options and @source mutually exclusive:

  • @options: [...] - fixed list literally in the comment. Best for stable enums (database.type, regionCollision.policy, curve types).
  • @source: <registry> - values come from a runtime registry (material, biome, world, tag). Best for sets that vary at runtime.

Shape/vert type names come from RTP.factoryMap (registered shapes/verts can vary), so a hardcoded @options list could drift from the actual registry. Recommendation: introduce @source: shape and @source: vert as new registry keywords and route them through the existing finite-value machinery (ShapeParameter.values() / VertParameter.values(), i.e. the same source buildParamPicker already uses for world/region/biome). This keeps shape/vert authoritative and avoids list drift.

docs.title: 6. Requirements / ADRs touched
docs.text:
• ADR-064 / CONFIG_COMMENT_STYLE.md - first runtime consumer of the directive tags. No format change; may add shape/vert as recognized @source registries (doc update in CONFIG_COMMENT_STYLE.md §@source).
  • REQ-RTP-F-013 (configurable user-facing messages) - any new picker labels/headers go through messages.yml + locale parity.
  • Book Menu Color Contrast (.junie/AGENTS.md) - picker rows use parchment-safe colors (no &e/&6/&f); reuse the existing &2 value-row convention.
  • Locale Parity Maintenance - directive lines added to baseline comments are mirrored into every shipped locale's <file>.yml.

docs.title: 7. Risks / trade-offs
docs.text:
• Parse robustness: a malformed @options/@range line must never break the menu - guard the SnakeYAML parse in try/catch (mirrors resolveConfigHover) and fall back to free text.
  • Annotation coverage: keys without directives keep free text; rollout is incremental (annotate finite keys over time). No behavior regression for un-annotated keys.
  • Per-open parse cost: negligible (in-memory string scan + one flow-list parse). Optional optimization: parse directives once at load/reload and cache a Map<key, ConfigDirectives> beside the cached YAML root; deferred as a micro-optimization, not required for correctness.
  • @source growth: adding shape/vert as registries slightly widens the @source vocabulary; contained to the directive parser + doc.

docs.title: 8. Verification plan
docs.text:
• Unit: new ConfigDirectives parser tests (valid @options, @range, @source, malformed lines, no-directive → empty).
  • Unit: extend MenuConfigSubtreeBuildersTest / add coverage that a key with @options emits a picker action (not free text) and that an un-annotated key still emits the free-text route.
  • Unit: buildOptionsPicker page shape (Back row, one row per option, current starred, pagination).
  • Dispatch: MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchOpenConfigKey routes an @options key to the picker and an un-annotated key to PromptAnvilInput.
  • LocaleParityTest for any new messages.yml keys and for the added directive comments.
  • Final full ./gradlew build.

docs.title: 9. Open questions for approval
docs.text:
1. Approve the generic @options/@source-driven picker (section 3-4) as the mechanism, replacing the deferred bespoke shape.name routing?
  2. Approve introducing @source: shape / @source: vert (section 5) so shape/vert stay registry-authoritative instead of a hardcoded @options list?
  3. Scope: implement the parser + picker + dispatch + annotate an initial set of finite keys (database.type, shape/vert, regionCollision.policy, curve/renderer types) this pass, and annotate the remaining finite keys incrementally - acceptable?
  4. Directive caching (section 7): baseline per-open parse now, or add the load-time Map<key, ConfigDirectives> cache in the same pass?

docs.title: PROPOSAL: intuitive in-game editing of shape/vert (and other type-bearing blocks)
docs.text: Status: APPROVED (D-005, 2026-08-14). Parts 1 (display resolve) and 3 (silent-fallback fix) implemented this session; the finite shape.name type-picker wiring (Part 2 of the menu work) is explicitly deferred to a follow-up per the user ("not necessarily this session ... use a menu for a set of predetermined values for something like shape.name"). Discovered-during: issue "issues are arising with ingame config editing with @config showing up and default inputs unclear" Author: Junie (with project lead)

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
Editing shape (and vert) through the in-game /rtp config book menu is confusing in three distinct ways:

  1. The @config inheritance token leaks into the menu. Region/world files ship shape: "@config" (ADR-073) as an intended, file-only inheritance token. The menu reads the raw parser data and renders it as the scalar shape: @config, presenting an internal token as if it were the editable value. @config is legitimate in files but should never be shown or typed in-game.
  2. shape/vert are edited as open-ended free text. Clicking the key opens a free-text anvil prompt prefilled with the raw stored value. shape is not a scalar - it is a type-bearing block whose name discriminator (CIRCLE, SQUARE, ...) selects which sibling sub-parameters (radius, centerX, ...) are valid.
  3. A valid type name silently reverts to the default. Typing SQUARE reverts to CIRCLE with no error. Root cause: the shape/vert write -> reload round-trip resolves an unmatched name through Factory.getOrDefault, which silently substitutes the DEFAULT.YML/first entry instead of reporting a bad value.

docs.title: 2. Confirmed design (agreed in discussion)
docs.text:
• Do not render the block key shape/vert as a scalar row. Expand it into its member rows, with the name leaf as the finite selector that drives the sibling sub-parameter rows.
  • Resolve @config for display only. The menu shows the effective (inherited) value; an untouched inherited key is left as @config on disk. Only keys the operator actually changes are materialized (materialize-only-changed-keys), preserving live inheritance for everything else. This matches ADR-073 intent.

docs.title: 3. Affected classes / modules
docs.text:
• rtp-core CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildConfigFile - resolve @config for the expanded/flattened view; route the .name leaf to the finite picker.
  • rtp-core CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildShapeVertTypePicker / buildShapeVertSubParams - already built; wire them in as the behavior of the .name leaf.
  • rtp-core MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchOpenConfigKey - detect a .name leaf of a type-bearing block and route to the type picker instead of PromptAnvilInput.
  • rtp-core ConfigParser / RegionConfigLoader - ensure the menu-visible data presents shape/vert as a resolved section/FactoryValue (so the existing flattenNestedConfigValue/factoryValueToMap path expands it) without materializing the on-disk token.
  • rtp-core Factory.getOrDefault callers on the shape/vert write path (SubConfigCmd) - stop silently defaulting; surface msgBadParameter on an unmatched name.

docs.title: 4. Intended before/after
docs.text:
Before (region file regions.yml, default entry): 

shape: @config          <- menu shows literal "@config"; click opens free text

After (menu view; disk unchanged until edited): 

shape.name: CIRCLE      <- finite picker (CIRCLE / SQUARE / ...), starred current, resolved from @config
shape.radius: 1000      <- typed sub-rows, derived from the selected type
shape.centerX: 0
...
Disk after the operator changes only shape.name to SQUARE: the shape block materializes as a concrete section; all other still-inherited keys keep their @config token.

docs.title: 5. Requirements / ADRs touched
docs.text:
• ADR-073 (config inheritance @<file> tokens) - amendment: clarify that the menu resolves the token for display, and that a write materializes only the edited block/keys while preserving the token for untouched keys. (Write side already largely implements this in ConfigParser.set, lines ~1541-1559.)
  • REQ-RTP-F-013 (configurable user-facing messages) - any new menu labels go through messages.yml + locale parity.
  • Book Menu Color Contrast (.junie/AGENTS.md) - no &e/&6/&f on parchment.

docs.title: 6. Risks / trade-offs
docs.text:
• Inheritance semantics: materialize-only-changed-keys keeps inheritance live for untouched keys; confirmed as the desired behavior.
  • Generalization: the .name-leaf-as-selector pattern is written generically so any future type-bearing block benefits, but scope here is limited to shape/vert.
  • Silent-fallback fix also affects the CLI path (/rtp config regions set shape SQUARE); a reproduction test is planned before the fix so we pin the exact fallback point.

docs.title: 7. Verification plan
docs.text:
• Unit: extend MenuShapeVertExpansionTest / MenuConfigSubtreeBuildersTest for the resolved-@config expansion and finite .name picker.
  • Round-trip regression: new test driving set shape SQUARE -> reload -> assert SQUARE (guards the silent-fallback bug).
  • LocaleParityTest for any new messages.yml keys.
  • Final full ./gradlew build.

docs.title: 8. Open questions for approval
docs.text:
1. Approve implementing sections 3-4 as scoped (shape/vert only, generic .name mechanism)?
  2. Approve the ADR-073 amendment wording in section 5?
  3. Any objection to surfacing msgBadParameter (instead of silent default) on an unmatched shape/vert name on the CLI path?

docs.title: PROPOSAL - /rtp config <file> view as an interactive book
docs.text:
Status: Design complete (v3.7, 2026-05-18). Pre-D-005, awaiting user review before checklist promotion. All Q1-Q13 + v3.6 refinements (3.2 / 3.4.ii / 3.5) + v3.7 implementation defaults (permission, locale keys, TTL, empty-file, shape/vert value source) answered. No open (?) items remain.

Final design summary (head of file, read this first): - 3-page curated config subtree (selector -> per-file key list -> per-key picker), rooted on the /rtp menu front page (later: under an admin panel). - Reuses buildParamPicker verbatim. No refactor. List keys inherit via existing ListCmd. - 3 new MenuAction variants: OpenConfigSelector, OpenConfigFile, OpenConfigKey. - Shape/vert sub-parameters: two-step page (pick type -> sub-param page), stateless writes (rely on parser-stored type as discriminator, matching SubConfigCmd:122 defaulting). - Write grammar: direct parameterValues on SubConfigCmd (no set verb); list edits via ListCmd. - Raw YAML view preserved as opt-in ViewRawSubConfigCmd. - Concurrent stale-view problem ignored (~5s natural refresh). - Command-tree path-walker demoted to a "Browse all commands" fallback row.

Decisions log (chronological, for traceability): - First pass (Q1-Q6): Q1 reuse buildParamPicker; Q2 synthesize through normal command path; Q3 list keys get click-to-remove + anvil-add; Q4 raw YAML opt-in; Q5 ignore stale views; Q6 dedicated config subtree, path-walker as fallback. - Second pass (Q7-Q11): Q7 separate MenuAction variants (revised to 3 in v3); Q8 dropped (no buildParamPicker refactor needed); Q9 list edits already routed through ListCmd; Q10 shape/vert sub-params surface via factory getData(); Q11 entry point is /rtp menu root. - Third pass (Q12-Q13): Q12 two-step page for shape/vert (v3.2a); Q13 stateless sub-param writes (relies on parser-stored type discriminator).

Decisions from user (2026-05-18, first pass): - Q1 -> reuse buildParamPicker. The existing param-picker (allowed-values rows + a PromptAnvilInput "type a value" tail row) is the click target for each key, not a bare anvil prefill. This is a richer flow than draft v1 assumed and means a config key click descends into a picker page rather than opening anvil directly. - Q2 -> synthesize /rtp config <file> set <key> <value>. Output is already logged server-side; no need for a direct write path. - Q3 -> list/map keys get a sub-page with click-to-remove rows + an add row that opens the anvil. I.e. list keys are not skipped; they get their own multi-row editor. - Q4 -> raw-YAML view stays as an opt-in subcommand (view raw or similar). - Q5 -> ignore stale-view problem. Users re-open within the natural 5-second window. - Q6 -> reject route (a), adopt route (b). Path-walking through the reflected command tree was tried in Stage A and produced suboptimal UX. Instead: dedicated menu pages (config-file selector -> per-file view) with command path-walking demoted to a fallback row for anything not surfaced on the front page or admin panel.

This v2 supersedes draft v1 at sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 and the affected-modules table in 4.

Effective issue (user, 2026-05-18 10:58):

working on the menu system, I want to reduce config updates to the view page as a book page and clickable (click event) anvil input view with suggested values for each clicked subparameter then return to book view with updated value

User clarification (2026-05-18):

currently the view option prints to chat and closes the book and does not make any lines clickable

So the goal is to replace the current chat-dump behavior of view with a book page whose value lines are clickable, each click opening the existing anvil-prefill flow, and returning to the book afterward.

docs.title: 1. Current state (what is already built)
docs.text:
The anvil-prefill round-trip the user wants is not new - it already exists for the param-picker pages of the generalized menu (ADR-045). The pieces are:

  • MenuAction.PromptAnvilInput(parentPath, paramName, prefill) in rtp-api - the sealed token type for "open an anvil GUI, prefilled, write the typed value back as the parameter".
  • CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildParamPicker(...) in rtp-core (line ~489) - emits a PromptAnvilInput row as the "type a value" entry on every param-picker page.
  • BookMenuRenderer in rtp-paper-common - renders a MenuModel as a written book; serializes PromptAnvilInput (and the other server-resolved actions) as /rtp menu token:<t> click events. Covered by BookMenuRendererTest.
  • MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchPromptAnvilInput in rtp-core - server-side handler that opens the anvil GUI on Paper/Folia, accepts the entered text, applies it as a config write, and (per ADR-045) returns the player to the originating page.
  • Token mint/TTL is governed by MenuTokenRegistry; book renderer guarantees exactly one mint per PromptAnvilInput fragment.

Implication: the user's flow ("book page -> click value -> anvil with prefill -> return to book with new value") is already implemented end-to-end for menu-driven set operations. The only thing wired the old way is view, which bypasses the menu pipeline entirely and writes to chat.

docs.title: 2. The gap (ViewSubConfigCmd today)
docs.text:
rtp-core/.../commands/config/ViewSubConfigCmd.java (104 lines):

  • Reads the raw on-disk YAML file via Files.readAllLines(...).
  • Streams up to MAX_LINES = 1000 lines to the caller via RTP.serverAccessor.sendMessage(...) as plain chat.
  • No click events, no book, no model object, no participation in MenuTokenRegistry, no path-tracking.
  • Registered from SubConfigCmd:373 (addSubCommand(new ViewSubConfigCmd(this, configParser))).

The current output is also disjoint from the structured config model: it shows raw YAML text, including comments, whitespace, and any hand-edits, rather than typed keys with current values. That means even if we made lines clickable in chat, the click target would be "edit this raw line" rather than "edit this parameter", which is the wrong abstraction for the anvil flow (which expects a (parentPath, paramName) pair).

docs.title: 3.1 Reuse, do not parallel-build
docs.text:
The view page is a menu page. Build it through the same pipeline:

  • view no longer streams raw YAML lines. Instead it constructs a MenuModel whose rows are the parameters of the underlying ConfigParser<E> (one row per enum key in E), each row carrying:
  • Label: <paramName>: <currentValue> (color-coded by type, e.g. green for default-equal, yellow for overridden).
  • Hover: the YAML comment block for that key (already extracted by SubConfigCmd.descriptionFromComment).
  • Click action: MenuAction.PromptAnvilInput(parentPath = ["config", "<file>"], paramName = "<key>", prefill = "<currentValue>") - i.e. the identical token type the param-picker already emits.
  • The renderer is the existing BookMenuRenderer. No new renderer.
  • The redeem path is the existing MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchPromptAnvilInput. No new redeem arm.
  • After anvil-submit, the user lands back on the same view page via the existing "return to originating page" branch of dispatchPromptAnvilInput (ADR-045). The page is rebuilt fresh, so the new value is visible immediately.

This means the only new code is the page-builder for "render this ConfigParser as a MenuModel", plus the wiring that swaps ViewSubConfigCmd's body from chat-dump to "open menu page".

docs.title: 3.2 Where the new page-builder lives
docs.text:
CommandTreeMenuBuilder is the right home, but the natural extension point depends on whether we treat config <file> view as:

  • (a) a synthetic node in the reflected TreeCommand tree, so OpenMenu(["config", "<file>", "view"]) Just Works through the existing dispatchOpen path-walker, or
  • (b) a special-cased page identified by a dedicated MenuAction.OpenConfigView(fileName) variant.

I lean (a) because: - It piggybacks on the path-walking infrastructure Stage A already built (MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchOpen, CHECKLIST-menu-navigation.md). - It avoids adding a sealed variant just for one entry point, which would also require a token-registry round-trip update in BookMenuRenderer. - The reflected tree already exposes config -> <file> -> view, so OpenMenu reaching that path is natural; we just intercept the page-builder when the leaf is view.

Mechanism: in CommandTreeMenuBuilder.build(..., assembledPath), when the resolved node is the view subcommand of a SubConfigCmd, dispatch to a new buildConfigView(parentSubConfigCmd, ...) instead of the generic leaf renderer. SubConfigCmd already holds a FactoryValue<?> (the typed config), so the page-builder can iterate keys directly without reading the file.

docs.title: 3.3 Where the new entry-point lives
docs.text:
Two integration points (both small):

  • /rtp config <file> view invoked directly (chat / Brigadier): ViewSubConfigCmd.onCommand no longer reads the file; instead it dispatches an OpenMenu(["config", "<file>", "view"]) through the same code path the menu redeem uses. Effectively: view becomes a one-line "open me as a book".
  • /rtp menu navigation: the view subcommand row in the existing menu already exists (Stage A made TreeCommand children navigable); no change needed - clicking it descends into the new page.

docs.title: 3.4 Suggested-values source for anvil prefill
docs.text:
The user mentioned "suggested values for each clicked subparameter". The existing PromptAnvilInput carries a single prefill string, not a list of suggestions, because anvil GUIs only have one input slot. Two interpretations:

  • (?) Q1: Does "suggested values" mean
  • (i) just the current value prefilled (which is what PromptAnvilInput.prefill already does), or
  • (ii) a tab-complete-style suggestion list shown above/before the anvil opens (e.g. as a separate intermediate page for enum-typed keys: shape, vert, biomes-with-allowed-values), with a "type custom" fallback?

If (ii), the right move is to mirror what CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildParamPicker already does for enumerable params: render a value-picker sub-page first (rows = allowed values via safeValues(...)), with the final row being a PromptAnvilInput for free-form override. This is already implemented for command parameters; we'd reuse it for config keys by extracting a small "values for this typed key" helper.

For now this draft assumes interpretation (i) is the minimum viable feature and (ii) is a follow-up. Please confirm.

docs.title: 3.5 Write-back semantics
docs.text:
dispatchPromptAnvilInput today translates the anvil-typed string into a parameter update for the command parented by parentPath. For config keys, the equivalent is configParser.setFromString(key, typedValue) (or whatever the parser exposes - need to verify the exact API). The user-visible operation should be the same as /rtp config <file> set <key> <value> - and indeed the cleanest implementation is to have the redeem path synthesize and run that command, so all existing validation, audit logging, S-004 attribution, and RTP.serverAccessor.sendMessage(updatedMsg) confirmation in SubConfigCmd.onCommand Just Work.

(?) Q2: Are we comfortable having the redeem path round-trip through /rtp config <file> set <key> <value> (cleanest, reuses all validation/logging), or do you want a direct configParser write (faster, but duplicates validation)?

docs.title: 3.6 Pagination
docs.text:
A ConfigParser typically has 10-40 keys; written books hold ~14 lines per page. The existing BookMenuRenderer already paginates via ChangePage. No new pagination logic - we just split the row list across pages the same way param-picker pages do.

The current MAX_LINES = 1000 chat cap becomes irrelevant; it can be deleted.

docs.title: 4. Affected classes / modules (per D-005)
docs.text:
Module File Change rtp-core commands/config/ViewSubConfigCmd.java Replace onCommand body: read file -> open menu page at ["config", "<file>", "view"]. Delete the MAX_LINES chat-streaming path. rtp-core commands/menu/CommandTreeMenuBuilder.java Add buildConfigView(SubConfigCmd parent, UUID callerId, ..., List<String> assembledPath). Wire from build(...) when the resolved node is a view leaf under a SubConfigCmd. rtp-core (test) commands/menu/MenuConfigViewTest.java (new) Each key in a ConfigParser emits exactly one row with a PromptAnvilInput token carrying the current value as prefill; pagination matches book-page capacity; permission gating mirrors rtp.config. rtp-api menu/MenuAction.java No change if we adopt route (a) above. Add OpenConfigView only if user prefers route (b). rtp-plugin messages.yml + every lang/<locale>/messages.yml + messages.lang.yml New keys: configViewTitle, configViewRowFormat (or reuse existing menu format keys). Per locale parity rule, runs through the TSV pipeline (see AGENTS.md), not hand-edited. rtp-paper-common (test) menu/BookMenuRendererTest.java Add a test asserting a config-view MenuModel renders with the same PromptAnvilInput token semantics as a param-picker.

Out of scope of this proposal: - Fabric rendering of the book page. The book + anvil GUI flow is Bukkit-family only today (per MenuAction javadoc). Fabric falls back to the chat renderer; that path can stay unchanged. - Multi-file "config index" book (a top-level book listing all config files with click-to-view). The user only mentioned the per-file view page; if they want an index too, separate proposal. - Editing of structured / list-valued keys (e.g. worlds, biome allow-lists). The anvil flow is single-line-string by construction; complex types will need either a sub-picker page or a follow-up proposal. (?) Q3: how should list-valued and map-valued keys be handled - skip them with a "(complex, use /rtp config <file> set directly)" row, or render them as nested sub-pages?

docs.title: 5. REQ-* / ADR references
docs.text:
• ADR-045 (docs/adr/ADR-045-rtp-docs-menu-consumer.md) - the menu consumer protocol this proposal piggybacks on. No new ADR is required if we adopt route (a); the existing dispatch semantics already cover this use case.
  • REQ-RTP-F-013 - all new user-facing strings (page title, row format, anvil prompt) must be configurable via messages.yml and locale-mirrored via the TSV pipeline.
  • REQ-RTP-S-004 - the redeem path already audit-logs invalid tokens; the new page-builder must not introduce any silent-discard paths. Reusing SubConfigCmd.onCommand's existing write logic (route Q2 = "round-trip through set") satisfies this for free.
  • S-005 - the page-builder runs on whatever thread the menu redeem dispatched it on; no chunk I/O is involved, so trivially satisfied. The current view already runs RTP.scheduler.runTaskAsynchronously for file reads, which becomes irrelevant once we stop touching the file.

docs.title: 6. Risks and trade-offs
docs.text:
• Loss of raw-YAML-with-comments visibility. Today, view shows the literal file including comments and any hand-edits. The new view shows typed parameters and their current values, which is the more useful abstraction for editing - but it hides the comment block (except in tooltips) and any keys present in the file but not in the parser's enum (i.e. unknown / deprecated keys). Mitigation: keep a hidden / opt-in view raw subcommand that preserves today's behavior, or add a ? row at the top of the book that opens a chat dump. (?) Q4 - do you want raw-YAML access preserved at all?
  • Anvil only accepts ~50 characters. Long string values (e.g. URLs, long biome lists) will not fit. For those, the anvil flow degrades; the fallback should be to surface /rtp config <file> set <key> ... as a SuggestInput row instead of PromptAnvilInput. The existing param-picker already has this fork; reuse it.
  • Concurrent edits. Two players viewing the same file, one edits a key, the other's book shows stale values until they re-open. (?) Q5 - acceptable? The redeem path could broadcast a "your view book is stale" message to other viewers, but that needs a per-file viewer registry.
  • No ADR change needed. If route (a) holds, this is purely additive within Stage A semantics. The risk of needing a superseding ADR is low but non-zero - we should walk the proposal past ADR-045's "Open question" section once before final approval.

docs.title: 7. Open questions (consolidated)
docs.text:
• Q1. "Suggested values" = current-value prefill only, or a value-picker sub-page for enum keys with prefill-fallback?
  • Q2. Write-back via synthesized /rtp config <file> set <key> <value> (reuses all validation/logging), or direct configParser write?
  • Q3. List-valued / map-valued keys - skip, sub-page, or "open in chat for now" fallback?
  • Q4. Preserve raw-YAML chat view as a view raw opt-in, or drop it entirely?
  • Q5. Stale-view problem under concurrent edits - ignore, broadcast a notice, or build a viewer registry?
  • Q6. Route (a) OpenMenu path-walker vs. route (b) new MenuAction.OpenConfigView variant - I lean (a), confirm?

docs.title: 8. Next steps (only after answers to the open questions)
docs.text:
1. Answer Q1-Q6, narrow the proposal.
  2. Promote this file to CHECKLIST-config-view-as-book.md once approved (per AGENTS.md Checklist-Based State Tracking).
  3. Implement the page-builder + ViewSubConfigCmd rewrite as a single, small [CODE] slice.
  4. Locale parity via the TSV pipeline for any new messages.yml keys.
  5. LocaleParityTest + scoped tests + .\gradlew build per AGENTS.md Final Full Build.

docs.title: v2 - reshaped design after user answers (2026-05-18)
docs.text: The Q1/Q3/Q6 answers materially change the architecture from v1. Replaying the design with those decisions:

docs.title: v2.1 New mental model: a dedicated config-menu subtree, not a reflected-tree page
docs.text:
User rejected route (a) (reflected TreeCommand path-walking) on the basis that Stage A's experience showed it produces poor UX. The new shape is:

  • A first-class menu subtree rooted at a curated config entry on the menu front page / admin panel. This is hand-authored, not derived by reflection over the command tree.
  • Page 1: config-file selector. Rows = one per known ConfigParser (messages, performance, safety, economy, effects, logging, regions, worlds, ...). Each row clicks to Page 2 for that file.
  • Page 2: per-file key list. Rows = one per parser key, label <paramName>: <currentValue>. Each row clicks to Page 3 for that key.
  • Page 3: per-key picker. This is buildParamPicker reused verbatim (Q1). Allowed-values rows for typed/enumerable keys, plus the existing PromptAnvilInput "type a value" tail. List-valued keys get a variant (see v2.4 below).
  • Back rows at every level (Stage A MenuAction.OpenMenu semantics still work; only the entry point of the subtree is curated, not the internal navigation).
  • The command path-walker (route a) survives as a fallback row on the front page / admin panel: "Browse all commands" -> the reflected tree as today. This preserves the discoverability of obscure subcommands without forcing them onto the curated path.

docs.title: v2.2 New MenuAction variants (Q6 decision implies this)
docs.text:
Because we're not path-walking the reflected tree for config, we need dedicated tokens for the curated entry points so BookMenuRenderer / MenuRedeemSubcommand can identify them without parsing strings:

  • MenuAction.OpenConfigSelector - no payload; opens the file-selector page.
  • MenuAction.OpenConfigFile(String fileName) - opens the per-file key list for fileName (matches a ConfigParser.name).
  • MenuAction.OpenConfigKey(String fileName, String paramName) - opens the per-key picker (delegates internally to buildParamPicker with a synthesized parent + key descriptor).
  • MenuAction.OpenConfigListEntry(String fileName, String paramName, int index) - opens the click-to-remove confirm or no-op acknowledgement for list-valued keys (Q3).

Each gets a small dispatchOpenConfig* arm in MenuRedeemSubcommand. All four follow the same server-resolved-token contract as the existing OpenMenu / PromptAnvilInput, so BookMenuRenderer round-trips them as /rtp menu token:<t> click events with no new transport logic.

(?) Q7: Are four new variants acceptable, or would you rather collapse to a single OpenConfigPage(fileName?, paramName?, listIndex?) discriminated by nullness? Four is cleaner pattern-matching; one is fewer sealed-type rows to maintain. I lean four.

docs.title: v2.3 Write-back unchanged (Q2 confirmed)
docs.text:
Both the picker rows (for enumerable values) and the anvil "type a value" submit route synthesize /rtp config <file> set <key> <value> and dispatch it through the normal command path. No new write path. All existing validation, audit logging, and the RTP.serverAccessor.sendMessage(updatedMsg) confirmation in SubConfigCmd.onCommand are inherited.

The only nuance: buildParamPicker today writes back to a command parameter, not a config key. So either: - v2.3a. Generalize buildParamPicker's write-back binding so the same builder can target "set this command param" or "set this config key" depending on a WriteBackBinding strategy passed in. Cleanest abstraction; small surface change. - v2.3b. Copy buildParamPicker into a sibling buildConfigKeyPicker that hardcodes the config-set synthesizer. More duplication, less risk of regressing the command-param path.

(?) Q8: v2.3a (refactor buildParamPicker to accept a write-back binding) vs v2.3b (sibling builder, copy-paste)? I lean v2.3a but only mildly - the duplication in v2.3b is bounded.

docs.title: v2.4 List/map key editor (Q3 expanded)
docs.text:
For a list-valued key (worlds, biome lists, allow-lists), Page 3 changes shape:

  • Rows = one per current list entry, each labeled <entry> with a click action that submits /rtp config <file> set <key> remove <entry> (or equivalent - need to verify SubConfigCmd's actual list-edit grammar, (?) Q9).
  • Footer row: [+ add] -> PromptAnvilInput with empty prefill. Anvil submit synthesizes /rtp config <file> set <key> add <typedValue>.
  • After either action the redeem path returns the player to the same Page 3, which is rebuilt fresh and shows the updated list.

For map-valued keys (rare; if any exist - (?) Q10: do any current config keys use map values that the user-facing UI needs to edit?): treat each entry as a (subkey, subvalue) pair and render two click targets per row. This is a follow-up; not blocking v2.

docs.title: v2.5 Affected modules (replaces v1 section 4)
docs.text:
Module File Change rtp-api menu/MenuAction.java Add four sealed variants: OpenConfigSelector, OpenConfigFile, OpenConfigKey, OpenConfigListEntry (or a single OpenConfigPage, pending Q7). Same defensive-copy / equals / hashCode pattern as PromptAnvilInput. Update MenuModelSurfaceTest permitted-types list. rtp-api (test) menu/MenuModelSurfaceTest.java Permitted-types assertion + defensive-copy tests for each new variant. rtp-core commands/menu/CommandTreeMenuBuilder.java Add buildConfigSelector, buildConfigFile, buildConfigKey. buildConfigKey either delegates to a refactored buildParamPicker (Q8 = v2.3a) or to a new sibling (Q8 = v2.3b). rtp-core commands/menu/MenuRedeemSubcommand.java Four new dispatchOpenConfig* arms (or one, pending Q7). Each rebuilds the target page and sends it to the player as a fresh book. rtp-core commands/config/ViewSubConfigCmd.java Rewrite onCommand body: open the per-file menu page directly (no token mint needed when invoked from a command - we can build the model in-process and hand it to the active renderer). The existing chat-dump becomes a view raw subcommand (Q4). rtp-core commands/config/ViewRawSubConfigCmd.java (new) Holds the old file-read + chat-stream logic from ViewSubConfigCmd. Registered as a child of view. Permission gated. rtp-core (test) commands/menu/MenuConfigSubtreeTest.java (new) (1) selector page lists every registered ConfigParser; (2) per-file page renders one row per key with OpenConfigKey token; (3) per-key page delegates correctly to picker; (4) list-keys render add-row + per-entry remove rows. rtp-paper-common (test) menu/BookMenuRendererTest.java New tests: each OpenConfig* variant round-trips through /rtp menu token:<t>, with one mint per fragment. rtp-plugin messages.yml baseline + locale TSV pipeline New keys: configSelectorTitle, configFileRowFormat, configKeyRowFormat, configListAddRow, configListRemoveHover, configViewRawHint. Go through the TSV pipeline per AGENTS.md Locale Config TSV Pipeline, not hand-edited.
