SubConfigCmd:373 (registration of ViewSubConfigCmd) is the only registration change; the new entry point is added under the existing wiring, not replacing it.

docs.title: v2.6 Front-page / admin-panel wiring (deferred but worth flagging)
docs.text: The user said "config selection then view" lives on the front page or admin panel. I don't yet know the canonical location of that front page in the menu tree - it might be the root of /rtp menu, or a separate /rtp admin menu builder. (?) Q11: which existing menu page should get the new OpenConfigSelector row? Pointing me at the builder is enough; I don't need it documented exhaustively.

docs.title: v2.7 New open questions (Q7-Q11)
docs.text:
• Q7. Four MenuAction variants or one discriminated OpenConfigPage?
  • Q8. Refactor buildParamPicker to accept a WriteBackBinding (v2.3a), or copy-paste into buildConfigKeyPicker (v2.3b)?
  • Q9. Confirm the /rtp config <file> set <key> add/remove <value> grammar for list-typed keys - does SubConfigCmd already accept these verbs, or do they need to be added?
  • Q10. Do any current config keys have map values that the in-game UI needs to edit, or are all of them either scalar or list?
  • Q11. Which existing menu page hosts the new OpenConfigSelector row - the /rtp menu root, an admin panel, or both?

docs.title: v2.8 Implementation order (once v2 questions are answered)
docs.text:
1. Q7-Q11 answered.
  2. New MenuAction variants land first (smallest surface, easiest to review, no behavior change yet).
  3. New CommandTreeMenuBuilder builders + tests next, still without the redeem path wired - just verify the model is correct in isolation.
  4. MenuRedeemSubcommand dispatch arms + ViewSubConfigCmd rewrite + ViewRawSubConfigCmd extraction.
  5. BookMenuRenderer round-trip tests.
  6. Locale TSV pipeline pass for the new messages.yml keys.
  7. LocaleParityTest + scoped tests + .\gradlew build.

Each step independently verifiable; the checklist (once promoted) will mirror this order.

docs.title: v3 - corrected after reading SubConfigCmd.addParameters (2026-05-18)
docs.text: The Q9 answer pushed me to read the actual write grammar. v2's assumptions about set <key> <value> and "refactor buildParamPicker" are both wrong. Ground truth:

docs.title: v3.1 What actually exists in SubConfigCmd
docs.text:
• SubConfigCmd.onCommand consumes parameterValues: Map<String, List<String>> directly. There is no set verb. The write form is /rtp config <file> <key>:<value> <key>:<value> ... — every config key is a top-level commands-api parameter on the SubConfigCmd itself.
  • addParameters() walks the parser's EnumMap and, per typed value, registers a tailored CommandParameter (line 366-448): BooleanParameter, IntegerParameter, FloatParameter, WorldParameter, RegionParameter, ShapeParameter, VertParameter, or an inline CommandParameter (for raw strings). Sections that aren't shape/vert are recursed via addSectionParameters. Each of these already exposes .values() and a description, which is exactly what buildParamPicker consumes.
  • List-typed keys (block-foo, biome-foo, anything instanceof List) get a dedicated ListCmd subcommand (line 446), with its own ListAddParameter and ListRemoveParameter files at commands/config/list/. So Q9's add/remove semantics already exist — under /rtp config <file> <listKey> add <value> / ... remove <value>, dispatched through ListCmd, not through the parent set/SubConfigCmd.
  • shape / vert sub-parameters (Q10): when the key is shape or vert, the registered parameter is ShapeParameter / VertParameter whose .values() returns factory-registered type names (SQUARE, CIRCLE, JUMP, LINEAR, ...). Selecting a type name activates extra sub-parameters via the factory.get(name).getData() call in onCommand (line 159+). Those sub-parameters are then also valid keys in the same parameterValues map. So the "select a type, get new sub-parameters" UX is already encoded in the data; it just needs the renderer to ask the factory for the activated sub-parameters after a type is picked.

docs.title: v3.2 Implications
docs.text:
Q8 is moot. No WriteBackBinding abstraction needed. buildParamPicker already targets a TreeCommand + CommandParameter pair. The config-key picker is just buildParamPicker(theSubConfigCmdInstance, <keyName>) — verbatim, no refactor. This is a big simplification.

Q9 grammar corrected. List edits go through ListCmd. The Page 3 editor for a list key doesn't synthesize anything novel — it just opens the ListCmd page (which is also already a TreeCommand that buildParamPicker can render). ListAddParameter exposes the anvil-target free-form entry; ListRemoveParameter exposes the current entries as .values().

Q10 (shape/vert sub-params) needs a small extension to buildParamPicker. Today the builder shows the .values() of a single parameter. For shape/vert, after the user picks a value the remaining sub-parameters of that activated type need to surface as further rows. Options:

  • v3.2a. Two-step page: Page 3a "pick shape type" -> Page 3b "configure sub-parameters of this shape type". 3b is built by querying RTP.factoryMap.get(RTP.factoryNames.shape).get(typeName).getData() for the EnumMap of sub-params, and rendering each as its own row that opens its own picker. This composes cleanly with the existing 3-page subtree.
  • v3.2b. Inline expansion: clicking shape in Page 2 opens a Page 3 that combines the type picker and the activated type's sub-parameters on the same page (multi-section book page). Denser but trickier to lay out.

I lean v3.2a (composes, no special-case rendering, matches user's "config selection -> view" mental model). (?) Q12 to confirm.

Q11 confirmed: new OpenConfigSelector row lands on the current /rtp menu root page. Future admin-panel nesting is non-blocking — we just keep OpenConfigSelector as an action and re-host the row when the admin panel exists.

docs.title: v3.3 Revised affected modules (replaces v2.5)
docs.text:
Module File Change vs v2 rtp-api menu/MenuAction.java Same as v2: four new OpenConfig* variants (Q7 confirmed). rtp-core commands/menu/CommandTreeMenuBuilder.java buildConfigSelector (file list), buildConfigFile (delegates to existing buildParamPicker(theSubConfigCmd, key) for each key). No buildParamPicker refactor. Add small extension for shape/vert: after a value pick, query the factory's getData() and render sub-param rows. rtp-core commands/menu/MenuRedeemSubcommand.java Three new dispatch arms (OpenConfigSelector, OpenConfigFile, OpenConfigKey). OpenConfigListEntry is not needed because list editing routes through ListCmd's existing parameters via buildParamPicker. Drop that variant from v2 (revise Q7 answer: three variants, not four). rtp-core commands/config/ViewSubConfigCmd.java Body becomes "open OpenConfigFile(this.name)". Old chat-dump body moves to ViewRawSubConfigCmd. rtp-core commands/config/ViewRawSubConfigCmd.java (new) Holds the old Files.readAllLines + chat-stream logic. rtp-core (test) commands/menu/MenuConfigSubtreeTest.java (new) Selector / file / key page assertions. For shape/vert, assert the post-pick sub-parameter rows are rendered. For list keys, assert delegation to ListCmd's parameter rows. rtp-api (test) menu/MenuModelSurfaceTest.java Permitted-types + defensive-copy for the three new variants. rtp-paper-common (test) menu/BookMenuRendererTest.java Token round-trip for OpenConfigSelector/OpenConfigFile/OpenConfigKey. rtp-plugin messages.yml + TSV pipeline Same as v2: configSelectorTitle, configFileRowFormat, configKeyRowFormat, configViewRawHint. Remove v2's configListAddRow/configListRemoveHover from this slice — they belong to a separate "ListCmd as a menu page" task if one is needed, since ListCmd rendering is already covered by buildParamPicker for free.

Net effect of v3 vs v2: less new code, no buildParamPicker refactor, one fewer MenuAction variant, list-key UX inherited from existing ListCmd. Shape/vert sub-parameter expansion is the only genuinely new builder logic, and it's a small factory-driven getData() walk.

docs.title: v3.4 New / surviving open questions
docs.text:
• Q7 (revised). Still "MenuAction variants are good" per user, but three variants now (OpenConfigSelector, OpenConfigFile, OpenConfigKey), not four. Confirm.
  • Q8. DROPPED. Not needed.
  • Q9. RESOLVED. List edits go through ListCmd, already wired.
  • Q10. PARTIALLY RESOLVED. Shape/vert sub-parameter expansion is the work; only Q12 remains.
  • Q11. RESOLVED. /rtp menu root.
  • Q12 (new). Shape/vert sub-parameter rendering: v3.2a two-step page (pick type, then configure sub-params) vs v3.2b combined page. I lean v3.2a.
  • Q13 (new). When the user clicks a shape/vert sub-parameter, the write needs to send both the type name and the sub-parameter value in the same parameterValues map (because the type acts as a discriminator for which sub-parameters are valid). Is it acceptable to have the menu remember the type selection in the menu token state and re-send it on each sub-param write, or should we treat each sub-param write as a standalone command (relying on the parser's current state to fill the type)? I lean the latter (stateless writes, matches the current parameterValues.putIfAbsent("vert", ...) defaulting at line 122).

docs.title: v3.5 Revised implementation order
docs.text:
1. Answer Q7 (revised to 3) + Q12 + Q13.
  2. Add three new MenuAction variants (OpenConfigSelector, OpenConfigFile, OpenConfigKey) + tests.
  3. CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildConfigSelector + buildConfigFile, both as thin layers over buildParamPicker. Tests against a fake ConfigParser.
  4. Shape/vert sub-parameter expansion in buildParamPicker (the only non-trivial builder change). Tests for RegionKeys.shape + RegionKeys.vert.
  5. MenuRedeemSubcommand three new dispatch arms.
  6. ViewSubConfigCmd rewrite + ViewRawSubConfigCmd extraction + registration.
  7. OpenConfigSelector row added to the /rtp menu root page.
  8. Locale TSV pipeline for the new messages.yml keys.
  9. LocaleParityTest + scoped tests + .\gradlew build.

Each step independently verifiable; the resulting checklist will follow this exact ordering.

docs.title: v3.6 - refinements from user (2026-05-18, post-v3 review)
docs.text: Three follow-up clarifications addressed against v3.5. None invalidate the v3 design; they tighten three specific points.

docs.title: v3.6.1 (re §3.2) view opens the book directly — not "synthetic"
docs.text:
v3 framed ViewSubConfigCmd.onCommand as "synthesize an OpenConfigFile dispatch". User clarifies: /rtp config <file> (with no further verb) already implies view in the command grammar; we can let view be the book entry point with no synthetic indirection.

Concrete change vs v3.3 row for ViewSubConfigCmd:

  • ViewSubConfigCmd.onCommand builds the per-file page in-process by calling CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildConfigFile(parentSubConfigCmd, callerId, ...) and hands the resulting MenuModel to the active renderer (book on Paper/Folia, chat fallback elsewhere). No token mint is needed for the entry transition because the player isn't clicking through a serialized token — they typed the command.
  • The OpenConfigFile MenuAction variant still exists and is still used for the click path from the selector page (Page 1 -> Page 2). The two entry points converge on the same buildConfigFile builder.
  • "Synthetic command synthesis" (/rtp config <file> view issued internally) is not how the book opens — that was a v1/v2 framing that v3 partially carried over. The book opens by direct builder invocation; the command path and the click path both call the same builder.

Net effect: one fewer indirection layer, same observable behavior, same tests apply.

docs.title: v3.6.2 (re §3.4 Q1) Adopt interpretation (ii) — value-picker sub-page for enum-typed keys
docs.text:
v1 Q1 had two readings of "suggested values": - (i) current value as anvil prefill only; - (ii) a value-picker sub-page (allowed values as rows) with an anvil "type a value" tail row as fallback.

User selects (ii). This is already exactly what buildParamPicker produces (safeValues(...) rows + trailing PromptAnvilInput), so v3's "reuse buildParamPicker verbatim" plan is unchanged. Recording this as a definitive answer (rather than an assumption) so the checklist step for buildConfigFile doesn't drift back to a bare-anvil prefill shortcut.

Implication for shape/vert (v3.2a two-step): Page 3a is the type picker — its allowed values come from ShapeParameter.values() / VertParameter.values() (factory-registered type names), with an anvil tail for typos / unknown types. Page 3b is the sub-parameter list — each sub-parameter row is itself a buildParamPicker page, so the value-picker semantics nest naturally.

Implication for raw-string keys (no enumerable values): safeValues(...) returns empty, so the page degrades to the single PromptAnvilInput row with the current value prefilled. This matches v1 (i) behavior exactly for that subset — (i) is the empty-.values() special case of (ii), not a separate mode.

docs.title: v3.6.3 (re §3.5) Book must reflect the updated value after a write
docs.text:
v3 didn't pin down what the player sees after submitting an anvil edit. User: the book must, at minimum, show the updated value after the write, even if making the change durable (config reload, on-disk persistence) is deferred to an explicit later reload.

Contract:

  1. After a successful write (any path: enum row click, anvil submit, list add/remove via ListCmd), the redeem handler rebuilds the originating page fresh from the live ConfigParser state and resends it to the player. The freshly built MenuModel reflects the new value in the row label (<paramName>: <newValue>).
  2. "Live ConfigParser state" = whatever getConfigValue(key, default) returns immediately after SubConfigCmd.onCommand finishes its write. SubConfigCmd already mutates the in-memory parser before its async write completes (configParser.set(...) calls precede the file flush), so the rebuilt page reads the post-write value without waiting for I/O.
  3. Durability is separate. If the design chooses to defer on-disk persistence to a later /rtp reload (which is a valid choice — SubConfigCmd already writes through, but a future variant could batch), the in-memory parser still reflects the change, so the rebuilt book is still correct. The user-visible commitment is "the book shows your edit"; on-disk timing is an implementation detail.
  4. Concurrent stale views (v1 Q5) remain ignored — other players' open books still need ~5s natural refresh. v3.6.3 only governs the acting player's own book.

Implementation note: this is already the v3 redeem semantics for list keys ("rebuilt fresh after each edit", v2.4). v3.6.3 generalizes it: every MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchOpenConfig* arm that follows a write rebuilds the originating page from live parser state before sending. Add an explicit test:

  • MenuConfigSubtreeTest.rebuildAfterWrite_reflectsNewValue: write a key via the redeem path, immediately rebuild the per-file page, assert the row label contains the new value (not the pre-write value).

docs.title: v3.6.4 No new open questions
docs.text:
All three points are answers, not new questions. v3.5's implementation order is unchanged; the test list grows by one (rebuildAfterWrite_reflectsNewValue) and the ViewSubConfigCmd rewrite description (step 6) simplifies to "direct buildConfigFile invocation, no synthetic command".

Design is now ready for D-005 approval -> checklist promotion. No further questions outstanding.

docs.title: v3.7 - implementation defaults (2026-05-18, user-answered latent items)
docs.text: Five latent items surfaced after v3.6 review that were defaultable but not pinned. User answered each; recording verbatim so the checklist doesn't re-derive them.

docs.title: v3.7.1 Permission gating
docs.text:
• Gate the config selector row and all OpenConfigSelector/OpenConfigFile/OpenConfigKey redeem arms on the existing rtp.config.view command permission (the same node that already gates /rtp config).
  • Hide the row for senders lacking the permission (do not render it greyed-out). Mirrors how SubConfigCmd itself rejects.
  • When the future admin panel exists, the row migrates under it; the permission node stays the same.

docs.title: v3.7.2 messages.yml keys
docs.text:
• More configurability is preferred over fewer keys. Final key surface (replaces v3.3's row):
  • configSelectorTitle, configSelectorBackRow
  • configFileTitle (per-file page header, takes file name placeholder), configFileBackRow, configFileEmptyHint (shown when the file is blank, see v3.7.4)
  • configKeyRowFormat (label format: <paramName>: <currentValue>), configKeyHoverFormat (hover description)
  • configTypePickerTitle (shape/vert step 3a header), configSubParamPageTitle (shape/vert step 3b header)
  • configViewRawHint (footer row that opens ViewRawSubConfigCmd)
  • configValueUnsetPlaceholder (display when getConfigValue(...) returns null/default)
  • All keys go through the TSV pipeline (see AGENTS.md Locale Config TSV Pipeline). Step 8 of v3.5 is updated: edit messages.yml baseline, run locale-files-to-csv.ps1 -> reconcile-locale-csvs.ps1, translate seeded rows in scripts/out/locale-*.tsv, run locale-files-from-csv.ps1, then LocaleParityTest.

docs.title: v3.7.3 Token TTL
docs.text:
• All three new variants (OpenConfigSelector, OpenConfigFile, OpenConfigKey) mint tokens with a 1-hour TTL in MenuTokenRegistry.
  • Existing PromptAnvilInput tokens emitted from within these pages keep their default TTL (ADR-045) - only the OpenConfig* tokens get the longer lifetime, since users may park on a selector or per-file page.
  • Cut back later if we observe leaked tokens or memory pressure; until then 1 hour is the policy.

docs.title: v3.7.4 Empty / unreadable config files
docs.text:
• Config files are dynamically detected via RTP.configs; the only realistic edge case is a blank but extant file (the parser yields no keys).
  • For that case, buildConfigFile renders a file-accurate empty page: file-name title row + configFileEmptyHint row + back button. No "(unavailable)" or greyed treatment needed.
  • Deleted files are regenerated by the reload pipeline before the menu is opened, so a missing file is not a state the menu needs to handle.

docs.title: v3.7.5 Shape / vert sub-parameter rendering source
docs.text:
• Q13's stateless-write decision stands: the parser's stored shape/vert type discriminates which sub-parameters are valid.
  • For rendering the type picker (Page 3a) and the post-pick sub-parameter list (Page 3b), reuse the existing tab-complete value-source functions that the commands-api uses for these parameters. Specifically:
  • Type picker rows come from the same function ShapeParameter / VertParameter already exposes for tab-completion (factory-registered names).
  • Sub-parameter rows come from the activated factory's getData() (already used by SubConfigCmd.onCommand).
  • This means no new value-enumeration code for shape/vert - the menu builder calls the same enumerators the command tab-complete already calls. Orphaned sub-params from a previous type are left in place (parser ignores them under the new type, cheapest correct behavior).

docs.title: v3.7.6 No new open questions
docs.text:
All five items are now defaults of record. v3.5's nine-step implementation order is unchanged; step 8 (locale TSV pipeline) is expanded to cover the larger key surface from v3.7.2, and step 4 (shape/vert expansion) is clarified to reuse existing tab-complete value-source functions per v3.7.5.

Design is fully ready for D-005 approval -> checklist promotion.

docs.title: PROPOSAL — config-view book: ConfigSection flattening + List edit semantics
docs.text:
Status: draft (design-only, awaiting user re-review before coding) Author: Junie (this session) Companion docs: - PROPOSAL-config-view-as-book.md (the parent proposal; steps 1-8 of CHECKLIST-config-view-as-book.md are shipped) - CHECKLIST-config-view-as-book.md (resumable checklist; this proposal adds steps 10-11)

User answers locked this session (used as the contract below): - A(i): shape, vert, and any future named region sub-config keep their dedicated submenu (two-step type-then-subparams page already shipped in step 4). Other nested YAML sections coexist by flattening to prefix.key rows on the per-file page. - A(ii): flatten for display only; the write-back path reverses the dotted name back to the nested YAML write that SubConfigCmd already accepts. No new wire format. - B(iii): the value picker for a List parameter shows the raw current contents of that list section only; not tag-expanded (so #minecraft:logs stays as #minecraft:logs, not its 6 leaf biomes). - B(iv): write convention is <paramName>:<value> adds, <paramName>:-<value> removes — matches the early-testing minus-sign syntax SubConfigCmd already accepts. To be re-verified in code before step 11 lands.

docs.title: 1. Symptom recap (what the user reported)
docs.text:
"we currently literally infer 'map' but often it's a configuration section"

In CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildConfigFile, every enum constant of the file's ConfigParser<E> becomes one row. When that constant's current value is a RtpYamlSection (e.g. regions/default.yml#shape, regions/default.yml#vert, or any future nested section like a per-mode tuning block), the row label degrades to <KEY>: [object Object]-ish and the click action is OpenConfigKey(file, paramName) which routes to buildParamPicker. buildParamPicker then has no CommandParameter for the nested leaves (they live on a different TreeCommand node) so the page is the empty "back + header + type fallback" — a dead-end.

"And the biome list is not printed with the currently written options to possibly remove"

In CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildParamPicker, the value rows come from safeSuggestions(param, callerId) -> CommandParameter.relevantValues(uuid), which returns the valid universe (every biome the server knows, in this case). The currently-configured list (safety.yml#biomes) is invisible — the user can add but can't see what to remove.

docs.title: 2. Design — Part A: ConfigSection flattening to prefix.key
2.1 Detection
docs.text:
For each enum constant K of the file's ConfigParser<E>, the builder fetches parser.getConfigValue(K, null) and inspects the return type:

  • RtpYamlSection instance:
  • If K is RegionKeys.shape or RegionKeys.vert (or any future entry on a curated allowlist — see §2.4): render a single row labeled "<K>: <currentTypeName>" whose click action stays OpenConfigKey(file, K.name()). The existing step-4 MenuConfigSubtreeBuilder.buildSubParamPage two-step page handles this case. No change to that path.
  • Otherwise (generic nested section): flatten one row per child key. Label "<K>.<childKey>: <value>", click action OpenConfigKey(file, K.name() + "." + childKey) (the dotted name flows through the SAM unchanged). Order: insertion order from the section (deterministic per YAML load).
  • List<?> (e.g. safety.yml#biomes): one row labeled "<K> (<size> entries)", click action OpenConfigKey(file, K.name()). The redeem dispatch routes to a new picker variant (Part B) instead of the flat buildParamPicker.
  • Scalar (String/Number/Boolean/Enum-name): unchanged — one row "<K>: <value>" with OpenConfigKey(file, K.name()).
  • null: unchanged — "<K>: <unset>".

docs.title: 2.2 Write-back reversal (dotted -> nested)
docs.text:
The dispatch arm for OpenConfigKey(file, dottedName) splits on the first .:

  • No dot (teleportDelay): existing flat path — buildParamPicker(subConfigCmd, ..., ["config", file, "set"], paramName).
  • One dot (shape.radius for a non-curated section, or any flattened child): rewrites the picker's value-click action so that clicking value V for dotted key prefix.child emits /rtp config <file> set <prefix>.<child>:<V> — which SubConfigCmd.onCommand already accepts (it treats parameterValues keys verbatim and the YAML writer interprets the dot as section/key navigation, pending verification at step 11 kick-off; see §2.5).
  • For nested-section flattening, the CommandParameter lookup uses the dotted form directly on the parent SubConfigCmd. If no such parameter is registered, the picker falls back to: free-form anvil input only (no suggestion rows). This is acceptable for generic sections where the suggestion universe isn't enumerable.

docs.title: 2.3 Curated two-step allow-list
docs.text:
The set of (file, key) pairs that opt out of generic flattening and into the existing shape/vert two-step page:

File Key Discriminator field Notes regions shape name Already wired (step 4) regions vert name Already wired (step 4) (future) (future) name Add a row here when the curated submenu is needed.

Detection rule: the curated allow-list is a Set<String> of dotted file-qualified keys (e.g. {"regions.shape", "regions.vert"}) on MenuConfigSubtreeBuilder (or on RTPCmdBukkit's anonymous impl). All other sections flatten.

docs.title: 2.4 Auto-update on name change
docs.text: Per the user's confirmation: "shape and vert and any future region sub-config use names and auto-update their keys when their name is updated". This is already the contract of the step-4 two-step page (Q4-2 from the locked design): writing name:CIRCLE switches the active type, and on the next render the sub-param page re-reads the parser and shows CIRCLE's subParams(typeName) keys — the rename happens for free because the menu re-asks the builder for a fresh model. No new code needed.

docs.title: 2.5 Verification needed before coding
docs.text: • Confirm SubConfigCmd.onCommand accepts a dotted parameter name in parameterValues and writes it through to nested YAML. Looking at lines 90-203 of SubConfigCmd.java the merge path is keyed verbatim on parameterValues map keys, so a dotted key likely lands as a top-level YAML key (which is wrong — we need it to land as prefix: child: value). If that's the case, the dispatch arm needs to split the dotted name before invoking the command, passing prefix: as the segment and child:<value> as the leaf — i.e. emit /rtp config <file> set <prefix> <child>:<V> where <prefix> is a sub-subcommand. This is the open verification step before step 10 implementation.

docs.title: 3. Design — Part B: List parameter editing
3.1 New picker variant
docs.text: A new MenuAction sealed variant or a new buildListEditor method on CommandTreeMenuBuilder. Option chosen: new builder method, reuse existing OpenConfigKey action with a typed dispatch in MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchOpenConfigKey (detect param.getData() instanceof List and route to buildListEditor). No new sealed variant. Rationale: the action surface stays at 11 variants; the per-key dispatch arm already exists.

docs.title: 3.2 Page layout
docs.text:
For OpenConfigKey(file, listKey) where the current value is a List<?>:

  1. Back row → OpenConfigFile(file).
  2. Header row → "editing list: <file>.<listKey> (<size> entries)".
  3. Current-contents section (new): one row per entry in the current list value. Label "&c- &0<entry>" (red minus, black entry — parchment-readable). Click action: OpenMenu(["config", file, "set", listKey + ":-" + entry]) — emits the minus-sign remove syntax. One entry shown raw, no tag expansion per B(iii).
  4. "Add new value" header (non-clickable separator).
  5. Add-rows (existing relevantValues minus the current entries — so the user doesn't see "add OCEAN" when OCEAN is already in the list). Label "&a+ &0<value>". Click: OpenMenu(["config", file, "set", listKey + ":" + value]).
  6. Anvil "type a value to add" row (preserves the free-form add path).

Pagination: same scheme as buildConfigFile/buildParamPicker — 12 rows/page including back+header. Current entries and add-entries share the paging budget so a 200-biome list pages naturally.

docs.title: 3.3 Write-back verification
docs.text: The SubConfigCmd merge path handling of listKey:-value is the other open verification step before step 11 codes. The user recalled implementing it in early testing; I need to grep for - handling in SubConfigCmd or its parsers before assuming. Fallback if not present: add a small adapter in SubConfigCmd.onCommand that interprets a leading - as remove from the current list (3-5 line patch).

docs.title: 3.4 Tests
docs.text:
• buildListEditor happy path: current=[OCEAN, DESERT], available=[OCEAN, DESERT, PLAINS] → page shows 2 remove rows + 1 add row + anvil row.
  • Empty current list: 0 remove rows + all available as add rows.
  • Pagination at >12 combined entries.
  • Null/empty-arg rejection.

docs.title: 4. New checklist steps
docs.text:
Append to CHECKLIST-config-view-as-book.md:

  • Step 10. Config-section flattening (Part A).
  • 10a. Verify SubConfigCmd.onCommand write-back semantics for dotted vs split parameter names (the §2.5 open question). If split is needed, document the segment layout.
  • 10b. Extend CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildConfigFile with per-key type detection (RtpYamlSection / List / scalar) and flatten non-curated sections to prefix.key rows.
  • 10c. Extend MenuConfigSubtreeBuilder (and RTPCmdBukkit's impl) with the curated allow-list Set<String> field; dispatch consults it to choose two-step vs flatten.
  • 10d. Extend dispatchOpenConfigKey to split dotted paramName and route to the verified write segment shape.
  • 10e. Tests: new MenuConfigFileFlatteningTest covering scalar/list/section/curated-section detection; existing tests stay green.

  • 10f. Locale: new messages.yml baseline keys configFlatKeyRowFormat ("[prefix].[child]: [value]") and configListSummaryRowFormat ("[key] ([size] entries)"); run the locale TSV pipeline.

  • Step 11. List editor (Part B).

  • 11a. Verify SubConfigCmd minus-sign remove handling on a list parameter. Add the 3-5 line adapter if missing.
  • 11b. New CommandTreeMenuBuilder.buildListEditor(callerId, file, listKey, currentEntries, availableEntries, writeCommandPath) per §3.2.
  • 11c. Route dispatchOpenConfigKey to buildListEditor when the resolved CommandParameter's current value is a List.
  • 11d. Tests: new MenuListEditorTest per §3.4.

  • 11e. Locale: new keys configListEditorTitle, configListRemoveRowFormat ("&c- &0[entry]"), configListAddRowFormat ("&a+ &0[value]"), configListAddHeader. Run the locale TSV pipeline.

  • Step 12. Final full build gate. Re-run the deferred .\gradlew build from CHECKLIST step 9 once steps 10-11 are merged.

docs.title: 5. Risks and follow-ups
docs.text:
• Risk: deeply-nested sections (a section inside a section, e.g. region.shape.tuning.factor). The current flattening proposal handles one level of dotting. Deeper nesting would need recursive flattening (shape.tuning.factor). Defer until a real config introduces it.
  • Risk: list of complex objects (e.g. a list of maps for waypoints). Today, no shipped config has this shape. If/when one appears, the list editor would need to recursively open a section editor for each entry. Defer.
  • Risk: locale parity drift with two new locale key surfaces (steps 10f + 11e together = ~7 new baseline keys, multiplied across ~12 locales). Lessons from step 8 apply — run the TSV pipeline once at the end, not per-step.
  • Follow-up (out of scope): a WriteBackBinding strategy abstraction to consolidate the various write-shape variants (flat, dotted, list-add, list-remove, named subsection). Worth doing once all three of (flatten, list-edit, future map-edit) ship — premature today.

docs.title: 6. Locked decisions (for the next session resuming)
docs.text:
• Coexist: keep step-4 two-step shape/vert page; flatten everything else.
  • Display-only flatten, reverse to native write on click.
  • Show raw current list contents only (no tag expansion).
  • Use the minus-sign convention for list remove (listKey:-value).
  • Design-only this session; coding lands as steps 10 + 11 in a follow-up.

docs.title: PROPOSAL: GUI-author SPI (menu data + teleport intent) for third-party inventory GUIs
docs.text:
Status: Proposal (this file). Author: Junie, 2026-05-29 (revised 2026-05-30). Captures the design conversation between the user and Junie so the implementation can resume in a later session without re-deriving any decision. No code lands in the session that produced this file. Rule D-005: this proposal must be approved before any code is written.

Revision 2026-05-30 - prior-art reconciliation: The teleport-intent entry point this proposal originally called requestTeleport(...) already exists in rtp-api as RTPAPI.teleport(UUID, RtpTarget) -> CompletableFuture<RTPResult> (plus cancel, queueDepth, isWarmingUp), shipped and tested as Phase 1 of CHECKLIST-rtp-api-devux.md (RtpApiTeleportSurfaceTest, TeleportDataTest). RtpTarget and RTPResult value types also already exist in rtp-api. This proposal is therefore narrowed: the mutating intent call is done; what remains is the read/metrics/chart surface plus the unstable rtp-core hooks. Do not re-author a requestTeleport(...) - reuse RTPAPI.teleport(...). (Note: the core-internal Region/RegionQueueManager.requestTeleport(UUID) is unrelated waitlist enrollment, ADR-043, not a public API.)

docs.title: 1. One-paragraph summary
docs.text: RTP ships a book-first interactive menu framework (ADR-035), maps-api for chart/MSPT rendering onto map items, and metrics-api for runtime-health snapshots. A native inventory (chest) GUI was evaluated and found to carry a poor cost/risk ratio: books already cover destination pickers and dense config text, maps-api already covers time-series visualizations (e.g. MSPT), and a chest renderer would require a parallel Fabric screen-handler implementation plus ownership of inventory-specific vulnerability surface (click races, item-dupe vectors, click-spam). Rather than ship and own an inventory GUI, this proposal exposes a small, safe GUI-author SPI so third-party GUI plugins/addons can build inventory (or any) GUIs against RTP. RTP owns validation and safety; the GUI author owns presentation and click handling. The surface is split between rtp-api (public, semver-stable, advertised to authors) and rtp-core (callable-but-unstable hooks for deeper introspection).

docs.title: 2. Decisions captured from the conversation
docs.text:
These are the answers the user gave during the design discussion. They are the contract this design is built against; do not silently change them in implementation.

  1. Do not ship a native inventory GUI. The remaining exclusive advantages (in-place toggle grids, slot/drag/quantity semantics, dashboard tile density) do not outweigh the cross-platform maintenance + security cost of RTP owning a chest renderer.
  2. MSPT (and any time series) is maps-api's job, fed by metrics-api (MetricsSnapshot.mspt, tickBudgetUtilisation = mspt/50; on Folia FoliaRegionSample.mspt is per-region). The SPI exposes this as a ChartSpec-style request, not raw item-drawing primitives.
  3. Security boundary is the whole point. The SPI exposes intent-level operations only (submit a validated teleport intent via the existing RTPAPI.teleport(...), read permission-gated data). It never exposes raw teleport primitives, item-stack mutation, inventory slot wiring, or click handlers. S-001..S-007 enforcement and permission gating stay inside RTP regardless of what the GUI does. A GUI author cannot, through this SPI, cause an unsafe teleport, bypass claims, or load chunks on the main thread.
  4. Two-tier surface. rtp-api carries the stable, advertised contract; rtp-core is a valid interface for non-topical / deeper hooks that RTP does not want to freeze into the public API. Both preserve the same safety boundary; only the stability guarantee differs.
  5. Books stay the default renderer for player-facing pickers and config text; chat renderer remains the universal fallback. The SPI is additive, not a replacement for the existing menu/ framework.

docs.title: 3.1 rtp-api (public, semver-stable, no platform imports)
docs.text:
Advertised to GUI authors. Everything returns immutable DTOs or accepts validated intents.

  • Teleport intent (the only mutating call) - ALREADY SHIPPED. 

    // io.github.dailystruggle.rtp.api.RTPAPI - present today.
// Permission, cooldown, cost, and S-001..S-007 safety are enforced inside this call.
// The future always completes with a success/failure RTPResult (S-004); never a silent no-op.
CompletableFuture<RTPResult> teleport(UUID player, RtpTarget target);
boolean cancel(UUID player);          // cancel a pending/in-flight teleport
int     queueDepth(RTPWorld<?> world);// pre-verified ready locations for a world
boolean isWarmingUp(UUID player);     // teleport requested but not yet completed
    No new teleport primitive is needed - this surface already exists and is tested (RtpApiTeleportSurfaceTest, TeleportDataTest). GUI authors call RTPAPI.teleport(...) directly. The RtpTarget selector (defaultRegion(), region(name), world(name), world(RTPWorld)) and RTPResult outcome type are likewise already public in rtp-api.

  • Permission-gated reads (for populating menu items). 

    // Targets this player is actually allowed to use (permission gates already applied).
// Keyed by UUID for consistency with the shipped teleport(UUID, RtpTarget) surface.
List<RtpTarget> getAllowedTargets(UUID player);
// Per-player status for a target: remaining cooldown, cost, availability reason.
RtpTargetStatus getTargetStatus(UUID player, RtpTarget target);
    RtpTargetStatus is a new immutable DTO (remaining-cooldown ms, cost, enum availability reason such as READY / ON_COOLDOWN / NO_PERMISSION / NO_FUNDS / DISABLED). Reuse MenuPermissionGates logic behind getAllowedTargets so the picker matches what the command would allow.

  • Runtime-health read (for dashboard tiles). 

    MetricsSnapshot getMetricsSnapshot();              // global
// (Folia) optional per-region samples for region-scoped tiles.
List<FoliaRegionSample> getRegionSamples();
    Returns sampled snapshots only - never computes on the caller's thread, so no chunk I/O and no main-thread cost is introduced (consistent with maps-api ReqRtpMap002NoChunkIoTest).

  • Chart request (delegates rendering to maps-api). Publish/confirm maps/ChartSpec as the supported way to ask for a rendered chart (MSPT sparkline, etc.) so authors do not draw pixels themselves. Authors hand a ChartSpec + a MetricsSnapshot-derived series to the maps pipeline; RTP/maps-api owns the MapBinding and render constraints.

  • Bring-your-own-renderer hook (already present). The existing menu/ SPI (MenuRenderer, MenuModel, MenuPage, MenuFragment, MenuLine, MenuAction, MenuOpenRequest, MenuConsumerProfile, MenuPlatformView) already lets an author register a renderer. An inventory GUI is simply another MenuRenderer the author supplies - RTP does not write it. Document this path explicitly in the author guide.

docs.title: 3.2 rtp-core (callable-but-unstable hooks)
docs.text:
For authors who want deeper access and accept breakage between minor versions. Documented as "callable but unstable; not covered by the rtp-api semver guarantee."

  • Live queue/cache introspection (read-only): kept/unkept/backlog/login buffer depths, per-player fast-cache presence - useful for "X locations ready" dashboard tiles. Read-only views, never mutators.
  • The concrete menu builders (FrontPageBuilder, AdminPanelBuilder, CommandTreeMenuBuilder, VisualizationsSubmenuBuilder) for authors who want to mirror RTP's own pages rather than author from scratch.
  • Region/pool metadata (names, distance ranges, biome filters) beyond what RtpTarget exposes.

Even at this tier, no mutator that could bypass safety/permission is exposed; introspection is read-only and teleport still routes through the existing RTPAPI.teleport(...).

docs.title: 4. Affected modules
docs.text:
• rtp-api - teleport intent (teleport/cancel/queueDepth/isWarmingUp), RtpTarget, and RTPResult already exist - no work. New work: getAllowedTargets/getTargetStatus reads (on RTPAPI or a new RtpMenuDataApi facade), new RtpTargetStatus DTO, metrics accessors, confirm maps/ChartSpec as public, document the menu/ BYO-renderer path. No platform imports.
  • rtp-core - implement the rtp-api methods (wire getAllowedTargets to MenuPermissionGates, getMetricsSnapshot to CoreMetrics), expose the read-only introspection hooks.
  • No platform-adapter changes required for the SPI itself; adapters already install MetricsBinding / MapBinding. A third-party GUI links rtp-api (and optionally rtp-core).
  • Docs - author guide (where to depend, the safety contract: "RTP owns validation; you own presentation + click handling"), and an ADR.

docs.title: 5. Requirements / ADR linkage
docs.text:
• Safety prohibitions preserved by construction: S-001 (no unsafe destination), S-003 (no claim-protected teleport), S-004 (no silently discarded failure - RTPAPI.teleport(...) completes its future with an RTPResult), S-005 (no main-thread chunk I/O - reads are sampled snapshots), S-006 (require-by-contract: rtp-api entry points throw IllegalStateException if called before core loads, never null/no-op; already enforced by the shipped teleport surface).
  • Builds on ADR-035 (interactive menus, book-first), ADR-044 (command-tree menu reflector), maps-api (ChartSpec, renderers), metrics-api (MetricsSnapshot).
  • New ADR required: "GUI-author SPI: menu-data + teleport-intent surface, split rtp-api (stable) / rtp-core (unstable hook)." Records the decision NOT to ship a native inventory GUI and the security rationale for the intent-only boundary.

docs.title: 6. Risks and trade-offs
docs.text:
• API-surface permanence. Anything in rtp-api is a semver commitment. Mitigation: keep the stable surface minimal (intent + permission-gated reads + ChartSpec); push everything speculative into the rtp-core unstable tier.
  • Author misuse outside the boundary. A GUI author can still write an unsafe inventory (dupe bug in their click handler) - but they cannot make RTP perform an unsafe teleport. That is the explicit point: RTP's liability stops at the validated intent. Must be stated plainly in the author guide.
  • Discoverability. An SPI nobody adopts adds maintenance for no usage. Mitigation: ship a tiny example addon under addons/ demonstrating an inventory picker built on the SPI (proves the surface is sufficient and doubles as documentation).
  • RtpTargetStatus shape churn. The availability-reason enum may grow. Keep it an enum with a documented "unknown reasons may be added" note.

docs.title: 7. Out of scope
docs.text:
• RTP shipping its own inventory/chest renderer.
  • A Fabric MapBinding (separate effort; until it exists, map-item tiles fall back to scalar items on Fabric).
  • Cross-server / network-mode menu data.
  • Any change to the existing book/chat renderers' behavior.

docs.title: 8. Remaining work (post prior-art reconciliation)
docs.text:
The teleport-intent surface is done (RTPAPI.teleport/cancel/queueDepth/isWarmingUp + RtpTarget + RTPResult). What this proposal still covers, if approved:

  1. ~~getAllowedTargets(UUID) (permission-gated) + RtpTargetStatus DTO (cooldown/cost/availability reason).~~ DONE 2026-05-30 (Phase 1).
  2. ~~getMetricsSnapshot() / getRegionSamples() accessors on rtp-api.~~ DONE 2026-05-30 (Phase 1).
  3. ~~Publish/confirm maps/ChartSpec as advertised-public.~~ CONFIRMED 2026-05-30 (Phase 2).
  4. ~~rtp-core unstable introspection hooks (cache/buffer depths beyond queueDepth).~~ DONE 2026-05-30 (Phase 2). (Concrete-menu-builder reuse left as future opt-in; the builders are already public in rtp-core.)

Phase 1 landed (approved 2026-05-30; user chose: extend RTPAPI directly, defer the example addon, phase the work):

  • New rtp-api DTO RtpTargetStatus (Availability enum: READY / ON_COOLDOWN / NO_PERMISSION / NO_FUNDS / DISABLED / UNKNOWN; remaining-cooldown ms; cost). Immutable, forward-compatible enum.
  • New RTPAPI reads: getAllowedTargets(UUID), getTargetStatus(UUID, RtpTarget), getMetricsSnapshot(), getRegionSamples() - all with REQ-RTP-S-006 pre-init IllegalStateException guards and null-arg validation; null delegate results degrade to a safe non-null value (empty list / UNKNOWN status), never a silent no-op.
  • Core wiring in RTP.java static block: permission-gated target list (region requirePermission + rtp.regions.<name> / rtp.worlds.<name>), per-target status (cooldown from latestTeleportData + player.cooldown(), cost from region price + EconomyKeys.price honouring rtp.free, funds vs balanceFloor), and metrics-api snapshot supplier from RTP.metrics.
  • Build edge: rtp-api now api project(':metrics-api') (acyclic; metrics-api is dependency-free).
  • Tests: RtpApiMenuDataSurfaceTest (13 cases, rtp-api/metrics-api imports only). Full multi-module build green.
  • Follow-up (not blocking): add RtpApiMenuDataSurfaceTest to the REQ-RTP-S-006 row in TRACEABILITY.md (the oversized row resisted in-place editing this session).

Phase 2 landed ("undefer", 2026-05-30):

  • maps/ChartSpec confirmed already public in rtp-api (io.github.dailystruggle.rtp.api.maps.ChartSpec, renderer-neutral record, REQ-RTP-MAP-006 / ADR-047) and tested (ChartSpecSurfaceTest). No new work was required to advertise it; item 3 is satisfied as-is.
  • New unstable rtp-core introspection hook: io.github.dailystruggle.rtp.common.api.RtpCoreIntrospection (static, read-only) + immutable RegionQueueDepths record. Reports per-region kept/unkept/backlog/login/networkKept/networkReserved buffer depths, waitlist size, open per-player-queue count, and hasFastLocation(region, uuid) presence.
  • Safety: strictly read-only, no mutator exposed; reads are instantaneous in-memory samples (no chunk I/O, S-005). Deliberately degrades to empty/null/false rather than throwing pre-init (the REQ-RTP-S-006 throw contract governs the rtp-api surface, not this unstable hook).
  • Widened RegionQueueManager.hasFastLocation(UUID) from package-private to public so the facade (different package) can read it.
  • Tests: RtpCoreIntrospectionTest (5 cases).

Phase 3 landed ("create the addon", 2026-05-30):

  • New reference addon addons/RTP_GuiAddon (Bukkit JavaPlugin, /rtpgui) - a chest-inventory destination picker built only on the stable rtp-api surface (compileOnly project(':rtp-api') + :metrics-api; deliberately does NOT link rtp-core, proving the public surface is sufficient for a full GUI).
  • Demonstrates the security boundary: one slot per getAllowedTargets(UUID) target, each decorated via getTargetStatus(UUID, RtpTarget) (availability / cooldown / cost icon + lore), a server-health tile from getMetricsSnapshot(), and click -> RTPAPI.teleport(UUID, RtpTarget). The addon owns presentation + click handling (custom InventoryHolder, cancel-every-click anti-dupe guard); RTP re-validates every teleport.
  • Files: RTPGuiAddon, DestinationPickerGui, DestinationPickerListener, plugin.yml, README.md. Registered as addons:RTP_GuiAddon in settings.gradle. Bukkit-family only (Fabric has no Bukkit inventory API; noted in README).

docs.title: 9. Open questions for the user
docs.text: All resolved. The user chose: extend RTPAPI directly, phase the work, then "undefer" the Phase 2 items (ChartSpec confirmation + rtp-core hooks), and finally "create the addon" (Phase 3, the RTP_GuiAddon example). All proposal items are now landed.

docs.title: PROPOSAL: /rtp info as a book GUI (with periodic refresh + text fallback)
docs.text: Status: Draft (D-005 design, pre-implementation) Date: 2026-05-18 Author: Junie (agent) Predecessors: - PROPOSAL-config-view-as-book.md v3.7.x (book renderer, MenuAction token model, MenuTokenRegistry TTL conventions) - PROPOSAL-admin-panel.md v2 (curated MenuModel builders; OpenAdminPanel / OpenFrontPage sealed-record variants; permission self-hide pattern) - METRICS_PLAN.md > /rtp info Surface (B11 / C3 / F7) — what gets rendered today Related ADRs: ADR-035 (book/menu architecture), ADR-045 (token registry + TTL), ADR-020 (locale baseline)

docs.title: 1. Problem statement
docs.text:
/rtp info (canonical: InfoCmd in rtp-core/.../commands/info/) currently emits ~20-40 lines of chat — header, per-world rows, per-region rows, Health — pipeline group, Health — cache (Folia), and the disclaimer block. This is functional for console operators but, in chat, it:

  1. Scrolls past quickly, especially mid-game with combat / world messages interleaved.
  2. Is non-interactive: world / region rows are click-to-suggest (/rtp info world:<x>) but the operator still has to re-type /rtp info to re-read the live numbers.
  3. Is a snapshot. Metrics that move tick-to-tick (TPS, MSPT, queue depth, pending teleports, avg pipeline ms, heap) are frozen at issue time.

The user (issue: "can we pull the 'info' into book form and later do periodic updates?") asks for a richer presentation: a book MenuModel with the same content, and a refresh affordance so the operator's open book stays current.

A follow-up update ("maintain optional fallback per book vs text gui choice") requires that the existing chat/text rendering remain selectable, with the choice configurable per-viewer (server default + per-player opt-out).

docs.title: 2. Goals
docs.text:
• G1. Render /rtp info (no args, world-scoped, and region-scoped) as a MenuModel consumable by the existing BookMenuRenderer.
  • G2. Provide a 🔄 Refresh row inside the book that re-renders the current scope with a fresh MetricsSnapshot.
  • G3. Optionally drive periodic background refreshes for a server-bounded set of open info books (operator dashboards), without re-sending a book every tick.
  • G4. Keep the existing chat/text rendering as a first-class fallback. The choice of book vs text is configurable per-viewer, with a server-wide default.
  • G5. Zero new platform code in rtp-core / rtp-api. All book / chat dispatch stays behind the existing MenuRenderer SPI.

docs.title: 3. Non-goals
docs.text:
• NG1. Redesigning the content of /rtp info. The metric set, ordering, and locale keys stay byte-identical to today; only the presentation changes.
  • NG2. Multi-page info books in v1. If 14 lines is exceeded, the existing chat block is the source of truth and the book renders a more in chat --> footer that runs /rtp info text-mode.
  • NG3. Console operators getting a book. Console always uses text mode (no Player object to send a book to).
  • NG4. A new permission node. rtp.info remains the only gate.

docs.title: 4.1 Per-viewer rendering preference
docs.text:
New config key under config.yml:

# How /rtp info renders to players. Console always gets text.
#   auto - book if the player's platform supports books (Paper/Folia
#          with BookMenuRenderer), else text.
#   book - book everywhere a renderer is available; text otherwise.
#   text - always text (legacy behaviour).
infoRenderMode: auto

Per-viewer override stored alongside other player prefs (same persistence layer used for rtp.personalqueue-style opt-ins; nullable infoRenderMode column in the existing player-prefs accessor — exact name Q1). A new player-facing toggle command /rtp info mode:<auto|book|text> flips the preference and persists it.

docs.title: 4.2 Dispatch path
docs.text:
InfoCmd.onCommandInner decides up-front:

mode = effectiveInfoMode(callerId)        // viewer pref -> server default -> auto
if (mode == TEXT || callerId == serverId || !MenuRendererRegistry.hasBookRenderer())
    -> existing text path (unchanged byte-for-byte)
else
    -> new InfoBookBuilder.build(callerId, scopeWorld, scopeRegion).render()

MenuRendererRegistry is the existing SPI lookup used by MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchOpenFrontPage. No new SPI is added.

docs.title: 4.3 InfoBookBuilder (new, rtp-core)
docs.text:
Sibling to AdminPanelBuilder and FrontPageBuilder. Pure model builder, no platform imports.

class InfoBookBuilder {
  static MenuModel build(UUID viewer, InfoScope scope, MetricsSnapshot snap, ...);
}

sealed interface InfoScope {
  record Global() implements InfoScope {}
  record OneWorld(String worldName) implements InfoScope {}
  record OneRegion(String regionName) implements InfoScope {}
}

Rendering rules (all rows self-hide on empty locale value, mirroring the existing text path's "skip if empty" pattern):

  • Title row — infoTitle (already exists).
  • Section: World(s) — infoWorldHeader; one infoWorld row per RTPWorld, click-to-open scope OneWorld. In OneWorld scope, render infoWorldDetail (existing world-info list).
  • Section: Region(s) — infoRegionHeader; one infoRegion row per region, click-to-open scope OneRegion. In OneRegion: region-info list.
  • Section: Health — pipeline — infoHealthPipelineHeader + infoTps, infoMSPTLive, infoSoftCap, infoQueueDepth, infoPendingTeleports, infoAvgPipelineMs, infoHeap, infoDatabaseLatencyMs. (Unchanged keys; just laid out as book rows.)
  • Section: Health — cache (Folia only) — infoFoliaRegionsHeader + repeated infoFoliaRegion rows (B11/C3 work).
  • Section: Footer — 🔄 Refresh row (new key infoBookRefreshRow / hover infoBookRefreshHover), 📜 Switch to chat row (new keys), ↩ Back (only if entered from OpenAdminPanel — uses existing OpenFrontPage semantics... Q2: is /rtp info reachable from the admin panel today, or only via the slash command? If only via slash, the Back row is omitted in v1).

docs.title: 4.4 Two new MenuAction variants (rtp-api)
docs.text:
Following the OpenAdminPanel / OpenFrontPage shape (no-payload or single-string-payload sealed records, no defensive copies, full equals/hashCode/toString):

  • MenuAction.OpenInfo(InfoScopeToken scope) — opens (or re-opens) the info book at a given scope.
  • InfoScopeToken is a small enum-or-record carrying kind ∈ {GLOBAL, WORLD, REGION} + optional String name.
  • Used by the in-book click rows (World X -->, Region Y -->, 🔄 Refresh).
  • MenuAction.SwitchInfoToText — runs the text path for the same scope and does not mint a new book token.
  • Used by the 📜 Switch to chat row.
  • Also flips the viewer's infoRenderMode to text for this session only (does not persist; persistence requires the explicit toggle command).

MenuModelSurfaceTest's permitted-types list grows by these two.

docs.title: 4.5 Redeem path (MenuRedeemSubcommand)
docs.text:
Two new arms:

  • dispatchOpenInfo(senderId, scope, messageMethod) — gated on rtp.info. Builds via InfoBookBuilder, mints token (TTL: 5 minutes — shorter than admin panel's 1h because the data is live and stale tokens would mislead), sends book.
  • dispatchSwitchInfoToText(senderId, scope, messageMethod) — gated on rtp.info. Calls the legacy text path directly with the captured scope; sets the in-memory session pref to text.

docs.title: 4.6 Periodic refresh (G3)
docs.text:
Two layers, both opt-in and bounded:

Layer A — manual refresh (always available). The 🔄 Refresh row in any open info book mints a new token at the same scope. Existing TTL semantics handle cleanup.

Layer B — background auto-refresh (opt-in, capped). New config block:

infoBookAutoRefresh:
  enabled: false                # default off; this is a dashboard affordance
  intervalSeconds: 10           # min 5, max 300
  maxConcurrentSubscribers: 8   # safety cap; LRU evicts older subscribers
  permission: rtp.info.autorefresh

When enabled and the viewer has rtp.info.autorefresh:

  • Opening an info book registers the viewer in InfoBookAutoRefreshRegistry (new, rtp-core, keyed by UUID + scope).
  • A single platform-async task (Folia: Global Region Scheduler async; Paper/Spigot: async scheduler; per S-005 hard rules) ticks every intervalSeconds and:
  • Captures one MetricsSnapshot (shared across all subscribers — not one per).
  • For each subscriber whose previous book token is still valid, mints a refreshed token at the same scope and re-sends the book.
  • Drops subscribers whose token has expired (operator closed the book), is offline, or has lost the permission.
  • Subscribers older than the LRU cap are evicted (with a one-time chat notice: "info book auto-refresh: capacity reached, evicting oldest viewer").
  • Logout closes the subscription via the existing player-quit hook.

Why not push-on-metric-change? That would create chat-spam under load (the entire point is to see movement under load). A bounded interval gives operators predictable refresh cadence without saturating the network.

S-rule compliance: - S-005: No chunk I/O. The refresh task only reads MetricsSnapshot (already non-blocking) and dispatches book sends through the existing async-safe BookMenuRenderer path. - S-004: A failed refresh (renderer absent, player offline, snapshot null) logs at WARN and silently drops the subscriber — not silently no-ops the whole task. - S-006: API entry points (InfoBookAutoRefreshRegistry.subscribe) throw IllegalStateException if called before core loads.

docs.title: 4.7 Locale impact
docs.text:
New baseline keys (all via the Locale Config TSV Pipeline):

  • infoBookRefreshRow / infoBookRefreshHover
  • infoBookSwitchToTextRow / infoBookSwitchToTextHover
  • infoBookAutoRefreshNotice (chat-side notice when subscription evicted)
  • infoRenderModeChanged (chat acknowledgement of /rtp info mode:<x>)
  • infoBookOverflowFooter (the more in chat --> row when content exceeds the book cap)

Total: 5 new key pairs (~9 keys). No removals. Reuses existing infoTitle, infoWorldHeader, infoRegionHeader, infoHealthPipelineHeader, infoFoliaRegionsHeader, and the per-row metric keys verbatim.

docs.title: 4.8 Affected modules
docs.text:
Module File(s) Change rtp-api menu/MenuAction.java (+ MenuModelSurfaceTest) Add OpenInfo, SwitchInfoToText sealed variants; add InfoScopeToken record. rtp-api configuration/enums/MessagesKeys.java Add ~9 new enum entries. rtp-core commands/info/InfoCmd.java Branch on effectiveInfoMode; preserve text path verbatim. rtp-core commands/menu/InfoBookBuilder.java (new) + InfoBookBuilderTest Pure model builder; permission self-hide for rtp.info (the parent command already enforces, so this is belt-and-braces). rtp-core commands/menu/MenuRedeemSubcommand.java Two new dispatch arms; wire a new MenuInfoPageBuilder SAM. rtp-core commands/info/InfoRenderMode.java (new enum) + viewer-pref accessor wiring Persistence behind existing player-prefs layer (Q1). rtp-core commands/info/InfoBookAutoRefreshRegistry.java (new) Bounded LRU subscriber map + scheduled task. Disabled by default. rtp-paper-common BookMenuRenderer.toClickEvent Switch arms for the two new MenuAction variants. BookMenuRendererTest round-trip rows. rtp-plugin RTPCmdBukkit Wire InfoBookBuilder + MenuInfoPageBuilder SAM into MenuRedeemSubcommand. messages.yml baseline + TSV pipeline. config.yml baseline for infoRenderMode + infoBookAutoRefresh.*. docs CHANGELOG.md One bullet (absolute terms). docs METRICS_PLAN.md > /rtp info Surface Cross-reference: rendering mode does not change the metric set.

No platform-specific code under rtp-bukkit / rtp-paper-v* / rtp-folia-v* / rtp-fabric-*. Fabric inherits the text path (no book renderer registered) automatically.

docs.title: 5. Risks and trade-offs
docs.text:
• R1. Snapshot semantics across refreshes. Each refresh captures one MetricsSnapshot, so a single book view is internally consistent (per PlaceholderProvider.withSnapshot). Across refreshes, numbers will jitter — that's the point, but the operator must understand the timestamp. Mitigation: include a last-refreshed: <hh:mm:ss> line in the book footer.
  • R2. Auto-refresh + crowded operator base. A 32-operator server with all subscribed at 5s would mint ~6 book tokens/s and re-send ~6 books/s. The LRU cap (maxConcurrentSubscribers: 8) bounds this. Default enabled: false makes it strictly opt-in.
  • R3. Locale drift. New baseline keys ship with English values across all 12 locales until translated. Per Locale Parity Maintenance rule 4, that's acceptable for v1 with # TODO(i18n): placeholders.
  • R4. Book-cap overflow on OneWorld / OneRegion scopes. A heavily-configured region's region-info list can exceed 14 lines. Fall back to infoBookOverflowFooter row that runs /rtp info region:<r> in text mode. No data loss.
  • R5. Persistence of infoRenderMode. Adding a column to the player-prefs accessor crosses a DB-migration boundary. Q1 below.

docs.title: 6. Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• A1. Always book, no text fallback. Rejected by the user's update ("optional fallback per book vs text gui choice").
  • A2. Server-wide mode only (no per-viewer override). Simpler, but operators on the same server have different preferences (some want chat for Ctrl+F history searches). Rejected.
  • A3. Push-based refresh on MetricsSnapshot mutation. Rejected per §4.6 (chat-spam under load).
  • A4. Generic "/menu info" entry from the admin panel. Possible later — depends on Q2. Not blocking for v1.

docs.title: 7. Open questions
docs.text:
• Q1. Persistence layer for infoRenderMode viewer pref: extend the existing player-prefs accessor (DB migration), or treat it as session-only (in-memory map, lost on restart, no DB cost)? I lean session-only for v1 + a roadmap note to promote to persistent if requested.
  • Q2. Should /rtp info be reachable from the admin panel (Diagnostics section), in addition to the slash command? If yes, the admin-panel row dispatches OpenInfo(Global) and the info book grows a Back -> OpenAdminPanel row (otherwise the Back row is omitted). I lean yes, add a Server info (book) row and supersede the existing admin-panel Server info row that currently runs the text command.
  • Q3. Auto-refresh cadence default: 10s, 15s, or 30s? I lean 15s — long enough that operators don't perceive churn, short enough that a TPS dip is visible.
  • Q4. Should the per-viewer toggle be /rtp info mode:<x> (parameter-style, current convention) or a dedicated /rtp prefs info <x> (gestures toward a future rtp.prefs umbrella)? I lean the former for v1 to avoid a new command tree.
  • Q5. When the auto-refresh task evicts a subscriber, should we also auto-resubscribe them next time they open /rtp info, or require them to re-opt-in? I lean auto-resubscribe (LRU-eviction is "you're not at the front of the queue", not "you opted out").
  • Q6. Should infoRenderMode: auto prompt the player the first time (chat hint: "tip: /rtp info now opens as a book; run /rtp info mode:text to keep chat"), or silently use the new default? I lean silent — chat hints become noise.
  • Q7. Token TTL for info-book tokens: 5 min (my draft), or shorter (e.g. 60s) given the data is live? I lean 5 min — refresh is a click, not a re-issue; expiring the click target faster doesn't help anyone.

docs.title: 8. Implementation order (on approval)
docs.text:
Mirrors PROPOSAL-admin-panel.md v2 §8 structure. Each step is independently verifiable; promote to docs/dev/scratch/CHECKLIST-info-as-book.md per Checklist-Based State Tracking.

  1. MenuAction.OpenInfo + SwitchInfoToText + InfoScopeToken (rtp-api) + MenuModelSurfaceTest rows.
  2. InfoBookBuilder + InfoBookBuilderTest (rtp-core, pure model assertions; no platform).
  3. InfoRenderMode enum + effectiveInfoMode(UUID) + session-pref store (rtp-core).
  4. InfoCmd branch — text path verbatim under mode == TEXT || console || no-renderer, book path otherwise. Tests assert the text path is byte-identical to today on mode=text.
  5. MenuRedeemSubcommand — dispatchOpenInfo, dispatchSwitchInfoToText, new SAM, permission gate on rtp.info.
  6. BookMenuRenderer.toClickEvent two new arms + BookMenuRendererTest round-trips.
  7. InfoBookAutoRefreshRegistry (rtp-core) + scheduled task wiring per platform; default disabled; LRU + permission gate. New ReqRtpInfoBookAutoRefreshBoundedTest covers the LRU cap and S-004 failure paths.
  8. Locale TSV pipeline pass: 5 new key pairs (~9 keys); no removals.
  9. /rtp info mode:<auto|book|text> parameter wiring under InfoCmd's existing parameter lookup; persistence per Q1 outcome.
  10. CHANGELOG.md bullet (absolute terms vs v3.0.0-beta.2).
  11. LocaleParityTest + scoped tests + .\gradlew build (mandatory final full build).

docs.title: 9. Notes
docs.text:
• Em / en dashes not introduced (per AGENTS.md Markdown Encoding Hygiene rule 7); ASCII punctuation throughout.
  • This proposal is purely additive within ADR-035 / ADR-045; no superseding ADR is anticipated.
  • Auto-refresh (G3) is the highest-risk piece. If Q3/Q5 reveal disagreement, ship v1 without auto-refresh — manual 🔄 Refresh alone covers the user's "later do periodic updates" intent at acceptable cost — and defer auto-refresh to v2.

docs.title: PROPOSAL — Metrics-to-Maps: declarative ChartSpec bridging MetricsSnapshot to MapBinding
docs.text: Status: Draft, awaiting D-005 approval. Authored: 2026-05-20. Mode at authorship: [CODE] (drafted as docs-only per D-005 — no source files touched). Effective Issue (latest, 2026-05-20): "great let's make it, first wiring in maps into our menu info system using a drawing of bad points in the region then move on to metrics integration."

docs.title: 1. Summary
docs.text:
Add a declarative bridge so RTP can:

  1. Build a ChartSpec from a typed admin request (kind + source + region/window/viewer/tile-grid).
  2. Resolve that spec against existing in-memory state (MemoryShape bad-locations, MetricsSnapshot, ADR-039 SurfaceModel data) on a worker thread, producing a sealed ChartModel (maps-api).
  3. Hand the ChartModel to the active ChartRenderer<M> and MapBinding to paint the result onto a cartography map.
  4. Surface the resulting map as a click-action from the existing /rtp info menu (ADR-035 / ADR-044), via a new MenuAction kind (e.g. OPEN_MAP).

The two halves already exist: - Data side — metrics-api MetricsSnapshot + MemoryShape.addBadLocation + ADR-039's planned DiagnosticSurface / SurfaceModel. - Pixel side — maps-api MapBinding SPI + sealed ChartModel permits + HeatmapRenderer + NoopMapBinding.

What does not exist: any orchestrator that names a chart declaratively and routes the result through the menu. This proposal adds exactly that, without widening any data contract and without introducing new I/O hotpaths.

This is the connector ADR-046 / ADR-039 / ADR-040 each implicitly assume but none authors.

docs.title: 2. Two-stage rollout (mirrors the Effective Issue)
docs.text: The user's update explicitly orders the work: first menu→map for "bad points in the region"; then broader metrics integration. Both stages share the same ChartSpec machinery so Stage 2 reduces to adding new spec kinds and new resolvers.

docs.title: Stage 1 — Bad-points heatmap from /rtp info (target)
docs.text:
• New menu entry under /rtp info (administrator subtree, gated on rtp.admin.diag or equivalent existing permission — to be confirmed against RtpAdminPermissions):
  • Label: configurable via messages.yml key menuInfoBadPointsLabel (REQ-RTP-F-013, S-007).
  • Click action: OPEN_MAP (new MenuAction.Kind), payload = serialized ChartSpec(kind=BAD_POINTS_HEATMAP, region=<active>, viewer=<player UUID>, tiles=1x1).
  • On click, rtp-core resolves the spec on the existing async scheduler:
  • Reads MemoryShape.badKeysCache (already populated and persisted; no new I/O).
  • Decodes each 1D spiral index via Shape.locationToXZ.
  • Buckets into a fixed-resolution grid (default 128×128 to match MapCanvas.VANILLA_WIDTH/HEIGHT; tileGrid may multiply).
  • Normalises to a Heatmap2D(width, height, double[] counts, 0, max).
  • Hands the model to the installed MapBinding.allocate(...) then renderEphemeral(handle, HeatmapRenderer, model). The map item is given to the requesting admin.
  • Configurable failure messages (S-007): mapBusy, mapUnavailable, mapBindingMissing keyed under messages.yml per REQ-RTP-F-013.

docs.title: Stage 2 — Broader metrics integration
docs.text:
Add resolvers and ChartSpec.Kind values for the remaining ADR-039 surfaces — each one is a single resolver class plus a MenuAction.OPEN_MAP entry in the existing diagnostic menu. No new platform code.

ChartSpec.Kind Resolver source ChartModel produced Renderer BAD_POINTS_HEATMAP MemoryShape.badKeysCache Heatmap2D HeatmapRenderer (exists) REGION_COVERAGE RegionQueueManager.keptLocations / unkeptLocations / backlogLocations RegionCoverage RegionCoverageRenderer (new, Stage 2) FAIL_RATE_HEATMAP ADR-039 FailHeatSnapshot ring buffer Heatmap2D HeatmapRenderer CACHE_OCCUPANCY RegionQueueManager size getters CategoryDistribution CategoryPieRenderer (new, Stage 2 — already in CHECKLIST-maps-api.md 4.1) METRIC_SPARKLINE ADR-039 in-memory ring on MetricsSnapshot keys TimeSeries SparklineRenderer (new, Stage 2 — already in CHECKLIST-maps-api.md 4.2)

Stage 2 is gated on ADR-039's SurfaceModel types actually being authored (currently paper) and maps-api Stage 2 (BukkitMapBinding + RTPHooks slot) landing.

docs.title: 3.1 New types
docs.text:
Module New file Purpose rtp-api menu/MenuAction.java (extend) Add Kind.OPEN_MAP and a chartSpecId(String) payload field. No new behaviour on existing kinds. rtp-api maps/ChartSpec.java Sealed record carrier: Kind, String regionName, @Nullable UUID viewer, int tilesRows, int tilesCols, optional String metricKey, int windowSeconds. Renderer-neutral. Pure data; no platform / maps-api imports. rtp-core commands/maps/ChartSpecResolver.java Interface: CompletableFuture<ChartModel> resolve(ChartSpec, RTPCtx ctx). Strict S-005 contract: must not call world.getChunkAt synchronously; must not block on Future#get/#join. rtp-core commands/maps/resolvers/BadPointsHeatmapResolver.java Reads MemoryShape.badKeysCache, decodes via Shape.locationToXZ, buckets to Heatmap2D. Pure CPU. rtp-core commands/maps/MapDispatch.java Single entry point invoked by the OPEN_MAP MenuAction handler in rtp-plugin. Selects resolver, awaits the model (off-thread), then calls MapBinding.allocate + renderEphemeral via the supplied HeatmapRenderer. Configurable failure messages route through RTP.log (S-004) and sendMessage keyed on messages.yml.

rtp-core depends on maps-api for the ChartModel / ChartRenderer / MapBinding types only. It does not depend on mapsapi.render.. (enforced by an ArchUnit rule added to the existing module-wide guard in ReqRtpMap002NoChunkIoTest — extended scope, no new test class).

docs.title: 3.2 Edited types (minimal)
docs.text:
Module File Edit rtp-api menu/MenuAction.java New enum constant + sealed-permits guard or constructor branch (preserves backwards compat). rtp-plugin bukkit/commands/info/InfoCmd*.java (or wherever the admin /rtp info page is composed) Append one MenuLine with MenuFragment(text=…, action=MenuAction.openMap(chartSpecId)). rtp-plugin bukkit/menu/<dispatch wiring>.java Map MenuAction.Kind.OPEN_MAP → MapDispatch.

No edits to MetricsSnapshot, Metrics, MetricsBinding, or any sampler. No edits to MemoryShape beyond exposing a read-only iterator of bad-location indices (it may already suffice via the existing public methods — confirm in Stage 1 step 1 before adding any accessor). No edits to maps-api SPI.

docs.title: 3.3 Not in scope of this proposal
docs.text:
• BukkitMapBinding / FoliaMapBinding / FabricMapBinding themselves. They are the parallel CHECKLIST-maps-api.md Stage 2 / Stage 3 work. This proposal assumes BukkitMapBinding lands first (or in lockstep); without it MapDispatch resolves to NoopMapBinding and surfaces the configurable mapBindingMissing message.
  • Live-streamed charts. MapBinding.bindLive is not used in Stage 1. renderEphemeral only. Live binding is a Stage 2+ option.
  • Persisting charts across restarts. Charts are one-shot per admin request.
  • Mermaid (MermaidChart / Stage 4.4 of CHECKLIST-maps-api.md). Unrelated.

docs.title: 4. Relevant REQs / ADRs
docs.text:
• REQ-RTP-MAP-001..005 — maps-api REQs already cover require-by-contract, no chunk I/O, lifecycle, Lite-only Noop, Mermaid subset. This proposal adds no new REQ unless approval includes a new REQ-RTP-OBS-N for "diagnostic surfaces shall be renderer-pluggable".
  • REQ-RTP-OBS-001 — non-blocking metrics snapshot. The resolver chain is strict consumer of MetricsSnapshot; no new writes, no new schema. Preserved.
  • REQ-RTP-F-013 / S-007 — every user-facing string (menuInfoBadPointsLabel, mapBusy, mapUnavailable, mapBindingMissing) is keyed in messages.yml (new locale rows mirrored per Locale Parity Maintenance — TSV pipeline).
  • REQ-RTP-S-004 — no silently-discarded failures. Every MapDispatch exit path either delivers the model, surfaces a configurable message, or RTP.log(Level.WARNING, …).
  • REQ-RTP-S-005 — no chunk I/O on the main thread. BadPointsHeatmapResolver reads only in-memory state (MemoryShape.badKeysCache). Resolver chain runs via RTP.scheduler.runTaskAsynchronously on Bukkit/Paper, runTaskTimerAsynchronously on Folia (per existing scheduler abstraction).
  • REQ-RTP-S-006 — MapBinding API throws IllegalStateException before core loads. Preserved by routing through the existing RTPHooks MapBinding slot (added in CHECKLIST-maps-api.md Stage 2.6).
  • ADR-035 — menu framework. This proposal extends MenuAction with a new kind; no other change.
  • ADR-039 — diagnostic surfaces. The Stage 2 resolvers consume the same SurfaceModel types ADR-039 plans (still paper). This proposal does not require ADR-039 to be amended; it positions MapBinding as a renderer peer to MenuRenderer for the same surfaces.
  • ADR-044 — command-tree menu reflector. The admin /rtp info page is already composed via the reflector; we add one curated fragment.
  • ADR-046 — maps-api module. This proposal is the natural next step after CHECKLIST-maps-api.md Stage 2. No amendment required unless approval wants a ChartSpec re-export under rtp-api/.../maps/.
  • D-005 — this document is the proposal.

A new ADR — call it ADR-047 — Declarative Chart Composition Bridge — is the proposed governance artifact. It can either land alongside this proposal's approval or be authored after Stage 1 ships, mirroring how ADR-035 followed CHECKLIST-generalized-menu.md Stage 1. Recommend authoring up-front since the surface touches three SPIs (menu, maps, metrics).

docs.title: 5. Risks and trade-offs
docs.text: Risk Mitigation MapBinding not yet installed on any platform → every OPEN_MAP click fails. Surface the configurable mapBindingMissing message; gate the menu entry on MapBinding != NoopMapBinding so admins don't see a dead link. Same pattern as the existing MenuRenderer selector in RTPCmdBukkit#selectMenuRenderer. MemoryShape.badKeysCache is large on long-running servers; bucketing 100k+ indices to a 128×128 grid is CPU-bound. Resolver runs off-thread; counts are accumulated in a primitive long[16384]. Worst case sub-10 ms on commodity hardware. Cap input read to Math.min(cache.length, BAD_POINTS_RESOLVER_CAP) with a configurable cap defaulting to 250k. Adding Kind.OPEN_MAP to MenuAction is a model-shape change visible to every MenuRenderer. BookMenuRenderer and the test renderers already iterate MenuAction defensively; new kinds without a handler fall back to inert text (verified by MenuStageTwoTest.openPageRejectsWithMenuInvalidWhenRendererThrows). Add one test asserting BookMenuRenderer does not throw on OPEN_MAP. Stage 2 metrics resolvers race the ADR-039 SurfaceModel work. Stage 2 is explicitly gated on ADR-039 surfaces being authored. Stage 1 only depends on MemoryShape and maps-api Stage 2 — both already on track. Locale parity drift when adding menuInfoBadPointsLabel, mapBusy, etc. Follow Locale Config TSV Pipeline: edit baseline messages.yml, locale-files-to-csv → reconcile-locale-csvs → translate → locale-files-from-csv → LocaleParityTest. rtp-core depending on maps-api types creates a new module edge. Already a one-way edge documented in CHECKLIST-maps-api.md row 129 ("RegionCoverage model wiring … is the only place where rtp-core reaches into maps-api"). This proposal extends that edge to include ChartModel, MapBinding, and ChartRenderer types only — no mapsapi.render.. import. ArchUnit rule extends to enforce.

docs.title: 6. Stage-1 acceptance criteria (for the Stage-1 PR alone)
docs.text:
1. Running .\gradlew :rtp-plugin:run (or equivalent dev server) and issuing /rtp info shows the new "Bad points map" line for an admin.
  2. Clicking it (or running the equivalent /rtp menu redeem <token> flow) emits a single 128×128 cartography map filled with the bad-points heatmap rendered via HeatmapRenderer. The map is given to the requesting player's inventory.
  3. With MapBinding == NoopMapBinding, clicking surfaces the configurable mapBindingMissing message; nothing is logged at SEVERE; one WARNING is logged via RTP.log per REQ-RTP-S-004.
  4. New tests green:
  5. BadPointsHeatmapResolverTest (pure unit; 4 cases: empty cache, single point, 4-quadrant spread, cap enforcement).
  6. MapDispatchTest (3 cases: happy / NoopMapBinding / resolver throws → routed through configurable message).
  7. MenuActionOpenMapBackcompatTest (asserts existing BookMenuRenderer ignores unknown action kinds without throwing — regression guard for the model-shape change).
  8. LocaleParityTest green after the TSV pipeline runs.
  9. .\gradlew build green (per Final Full Build rule).
  10. TRACEABILITY.md row(s) updated if any new REQ-* added (default: none).
  11. CHANGELOG.md bullet under the current unreleased version.

docs.title: 7. Out-of-scope follow-ups (Stage 2 onward — separate checklists / PRs)
docs.text:
• Stage 2 ChartSpec kinds (REGION_COVERAGE, FAIL_RATE_HEATMAP, CACHE_OCCUPANCY, METRIC_SPARKLINE) — each one is a single resolver class, a single test, and a MessagesKeys entry. Land in the same order ADR-039's surfaces land.
  • Live charts via MapBinding.bindLive — only after Stage 1 + Stage 2 prove the static path is correct on Bukkit/Paper/Folia.
  • Cross-backend --backend <id> on OPEN_MAP once ADR-040's network snapshot publishes the relevant rows. Out-of-scope here.
  • Fabric MapBinding (Stage 3 of CHECKLIST-maps-api.md). Gated on Fabric stabilising.

docs.title: 8. Requested approval (D-005)
docs.text:
Three explicit go/no-go items needing user sign-off before I write any source:

  1. Approve the scope of Stage 1 exactly as described in §2 (bad-points heatmap from /rtp info, single-tile, ephemeral, Bukkit/Paper first).
  2. Approve the ChartSpec placement in rtp-api/.../maps/ (vs. keeping it in rtp-core and re-exporting later). The proposal recommends rtp-api since addons may want to author specs.
  3. Approve authoring ADR-047 — Declarative Chart Composition Bridge up-front (before Stage 1 code), to lock the connector contract.

If any of the three should be different, say so in the next <issue_update> and I will revise this proposal before opening any code path.

docs.title: PROPOSAL: MultiConfig submenu (regions, worlds, future kinds) for the runtime book menu
docs.text:
Status: Proposal (this file). Author: Junie, 2026-05-22. Captures the design conversation between the user and Junie verbatim so the implementation can resume in a later session without re-deriving any decision. No code lands in the session that produced this file.

Companion files:

  • docs/dev/scratch/CHECKLIST-multiconfig-menu.md - the resumable step list that drives the implementation across sessions.
  • See "Mermaid chart" at the bottom of this file for the visual model of the new dispatch surface.

docs.title: 1. One-paragraph summary
docs.text: The runtime book menu currently lets an admin browse and stage edits to the global config files (config.yml, safety.yml, etc.) via MenuAction.OpenConfigSelector and MenuAction.OpenConfigFile. This proposal extends that pattern to the per-entry config files held by MultiConfigParser<E> (today: regions/*.yml and worlds/*.yml; tomorrow: effects/*.yml and any further kinds), and adds the ability to create new entries (Add) and delete existing entries (Remove). Add/Remove are gated by a pluggable per-kind "in-use" guard so that the default region and any world currently loaded on the server cannot be removed via the book.

docs.title: 2. Decisions captured from the user's review
docs.text:
