These are the answers the user gave during the proposal review on 2026-05-22. They are the contract this design is built against; do not silently change them in implementation.

  1. Region semantics. Local regions can be edited locally. Build on top of MultiConfigParser so the same menu pattern serves regions, worlds, effects, and any kind added later. Anything currently "in use" cannot be removed; the set of in-use predicates can grow arbitrarily as new kinds are added.
  2. World semantics. Worlds cannot be removed when the server reports the world by name (i.e. RTPServerAccessor.getRTPWorld(name) != null). Orphan world configs (server no longer reports the world) may be removed.
  3. API shape. Three new sealed MenuAction variants, all parameterized by a parserKind string that matches MultiConfigParser.name ("regions", "worlds", future "effects"). Not per-kind variants.
  4. Add UX. Add opens an anvil-text-input prompt (existing MenuAction.PromptAnvilInput + AnvilInputSession infrastructure from ADR-045). Prefill is default<N> where N increments until the candidate name is unique against the parser's existing entries. The user types over the prefill if they want a different name.
  5. Remove UX. Remove is a toggled mode on the selector page, not a per-row button. The viewer flips a toggle row at the top of the selector; while the toggle is ON, clicking any non-locked entry row dispatches a remove instead of an edit. The toggle is per-viewer, session-scoped, and resets on selector re-open.
  6. Locked row presentation. Locked entries (default region, live world) are shown as gray-disabled rows, not hidden. Hover text explains why they cannot be removed.
  7. Color scheme. Row labels are file names, not messages.yml strings, so they do not need per-locale color treatment. Hover text (and only hover text) is translated and lives in messages.yml.
  8. Seed for Add. Clone default. When the new entry's name (region kind) or world name (world kind) ends in _nether or _the_end, amend the cloned values the same way the existing SubConfigCmd region-update path does (LINEAR vert, direction=2, maxY=128, requireskylight=false for nether; requireskylight=false for the_end). The existing logic lives in SubConfigCmd.java lines 83 and 123; factor it into a reusable helper rather than duplicating it.
  9. Permission. Reuse rtp.config.edit for both Add and Remove. View gating uses the existing rtp.config.view. No new permission node.
  10. Out of scope. ADD does not create the server world (only the YAML config). No cross-server propagation. No new ADR for this slice (extends ADR-035 / config-view-as-book). A short subproject ADR is optional if implementation reveals an architectural decision worth capturing; default is no ADR.

docs.title: 3.1 New MenuAction sealed variants (in rtp-api)
docs.text:
All three follow the defensive-copy / equals / hashCode / toString discipline of the existing OpenConfigSelector / OpenConfigFile / OpenConfigKey records, and are routed through the same MenuTokenRegistry mint path (one token per row, ADR-035 §3).

/** List page for a MultiConfigParser kind (regions, worlds, effects, ...). */
record OpenMultiConfigSelector(String parserKind) implements MenuAction { ... }

/** Per-entry staging-cart page for one entry of a MultiConfigParser kind. */
record OpenMultiConfigEntry(String parserKind, String entryName) implements MenuAction { ... }

/** Server-resolved mutation against a MultiConfigParser kind. */
record MultiConfigMutate(String parserKind, String entryName, Op op) implements MenuAction {
    enum Op { ADD, REMOVE }
}

parserKind is normalized to lowercase on construction. entryName is trimmed and validated against a conservative [A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+ regex (rejects YAML path traversal, slashes, whitespace, etc.); construction throws IllegalArgumentException on violation so a malformed token cannot ever reach the dispatcher.

OpenMultiConfigSelector does not carry the remove-mode toggle state. The toggle is held by MenuRedeemSubcommand per-viewer (see §3.4); the selector builder reads the live toggle state when rendering and emits row actions accordingly. This keeps the action sealed-shape compact and avoids encoding ephemeral UI state into a token.

docs.title: 3.2 In-use removal guard SPI (new, in rtp-core)
docs.text:
package io.github.dailystruggle.rtp.common.commands.menu.multiconfig;

public interface MultiConfigRemovalGuard {
    /** Returns true when entryName must NOT be removed. */
    boolean isLocked(String entryName);

    /**
     * messages.yml key whose value is the hover-tooltip reason shown on the
     * locked, grayed-out row. Returning null means "no reason text".
     */
    @Nullable MessagesKeys reasonKey(String entryName);
}

MultiConfigRemovalGuards (new) is a process-wide registry of Map<String /*parserKind*/, MultiConfigRemovalGuard>. The Bukkit-family wiring (RTPCmdBukkit) and the Fabric wiring register two default guards on plugin enable, before the first MenuRedeemSubcommand is constructed:

  • regions → locks entryName.equalsIgnoreCase("default"). Reason key: messages.multiconfig.lock.regionDefault (new).
  • worlds → locks RTP.serverAccessor.getRTPWorld(entryName) != null. Reason key: messages.multiconfig.lock.worldLoaded (new).
  • Unknown kind → falls back to a no-op guard that locks nothing. (Defense-in-depth: a kind that has no row in the admin panel will not have a selector page either, so this branch is reachable only if a forged token names an unregistered kind, which the dispatcher rejects upstream.)

The dispatcher re-checks the guard server-side on every MultiConfigMutate(REMOVE, ...) dispatch. Row suppression in the builder is UX hygiene; the dispatch-side re-check is the actual invariant per the S-001 / D-005 pattern of "never trust the client".

docs.title: 3.3 New builder: MultiConfigMenuBuilder (in rtp-core)
docs.text:
Sibling to CommandTreeMenuBuilder (the existing OpenConfigSelector / OpenConfigFile builder), not folded into it. Three entry points:

  • buildSelector(UUID viewer, String parserKind, boolean removeMode) → the list page.
  • buildEntry(UUID viewer, String parserKind, String entryName, LinkedHashMap<String,String> cartSnap) → the per-entry staging-cart page. Cart snapshot keyed by (parserKind, entryName, fileName).
  • buildConfirmRemove(UUID viewer, String parserKind, String entryName) → tiny confirm page (single confirm button + cancel). Only used by Remove. Add does not need a confirm page because the anvil prompt itself is the confirmation step.

Selector page layout (top to bottom, every row a single line so the book stays short):

  1. Back row → OpenConfigSelector (the main config-files page) so the user can navigate back up the admin tree.
  2. Header (non-clickable): the kind name, e.g. "Regions" or "Worlds".
  3. Toggle row: "[ ] Remove mode" or "[x] Remove mode" → re-opens the selector with removeMode flipped.
  4. Add row: "+ Add new..." → PromptAnvilInput prefilled with default<N>, whose confirm token redeems to MultiConfigMutate(parserKind, <typed>, ADD).
  5. One row per entry (alphabetically sorted; default first if present):
  6. Normal mode + non-locked → OpenMultiConfigEntry(parserKind, name).
  7. Normal mode + locked → same as above (locked entries are still viewable; lock applies only to remove).
  8. Remove mode + non-locked → red label, action = MultiConfigMutate(parserKind, name, REMOVE). Click goes through the confirm page.
  9. Remove mode + locked → gray label, no action (non-clickable display row), hover text from reasonKey.

Entry page layout: mirrors the existing OpenConfigFile page (staging cart, Changeable list, Pending block, Apply, Discard). The only material difference: keys come from the per-entry ConfigParser<E> instead of a global parser. Apply still goes through the existing MenuRedeemSubcommand cart-apply machinery.

All hover text on this surface is resolved through messages.yml keys; row labels are file names (no message key needed). The "header" row's label is a translated string (kind name); its message key is messages.multiconfig.header.<parserKind> with a generic fallback messages.multiconfig.header.default = "[parserKind]".

docs.title: 3.4 Dispatch arms (in MenuRedeemSubcommand)
docs.text:
Three new arms, each mirroring the existing dispatchOpenConfigSelector shape (gate → builder → render → S-004 reject on every failure path):

  • dispatchOpenMultiConfigSelector(senderId, OpenMultiConfigSelector open, messageMethod).
  • dispatchOpenMultiConfigEntry(senderId, OpenMultiConfigEntry open, messageMethod).
  • dispatchMultiConfigMutate(senderId, MultiConfigMutate open, messageMethod).

Plus a new per-viewer state field Map<UUID, Set<String>> removeModeKinds holding the parserKinds for which the viewer currently has remove mode ON. The selector dispatch arm consults this map when building; the toggle row's action is a dedicated re-dispatch of OpenMultiConfigSelector after flipping the bit (no new sealed action variant for the toggle itself).

Permission gating:

  • dispatchOpenMultiConfigSelector / dispatchOpenMultiConfigEntry: rtp.config.view.
  • dispatchMultiConfigMutate: rtp.config.view and rtp.config.edit. On REMOVE, additionally re-check the guard for the named entry; on a locked entry, reject with menuInvalid and log WARN (this is the S-004 path for "forged token attempted protected mutation").

ADD path detail:

  1. The anvil-input prompt is opened by the row's PromptAnvilInput action (already platform-supported).
  2. The submit command in the anvil prompt is shaped to redeem a token that the renderer minted at selector-build time for MultiConfigMutate(parserKind, "", ADD). The dispatcher reads the typed text as the entry name (overriding the empty placeholder), validates it (regex, non-empty, not already present), then calls parser.addParser(name).
  3. After addParser returns, the dispatcher applies the nether/end amendment helper (extracted from SubConfigCmd lines 83/123 into a reusable NetherEndConfigAmender).
  4. The dispatcher re-renders the selector page so the new row is visible.

REMOVE path detail:

  1. Click in remove-mode dispatches MultiConfigMutate(parserKind, name, REMOVE).
  2. Dispatcher gates on rtp.config.edit, re-checks the guard, then opens the confirm page (the confirm button mints a fresh MultiConfigMutate token; the cancel button mints OpenMultiConfigSelector(parserKind) with the toggle preserved).
  3. On confirm-click, dispatcher removes the parser from the configParserFactory map and schedules the YAML file for delete (mirroring SubConfigCmd lines 287-288: deleteOnExit()).
  4. Dispatcher re-renders the selector.

docs.title: 3.5 Renderer (in rtp-paper-common BookMenuRenderer)
docs.text: Three new case arms in the action-to-token-mint switch, matching the existing config-subtree shape. No BookMenuRenderer logic changes beyond the three switch arms.

docs.title: 3.6 Admin panel rows (in AdminPanelBuilder)
docs.text:
Two new rows under the Configuration divider, both gated rtp.config.view:

  • "Regions" → OpenMultiConfigSelector("regions").
  • "Worlds" → OpenMultiConfigSelector("worlds").

Effects and future kinds are not added in this slice. Doing so is a one-line addition once their MultiConfigParser is the canonical config surface and a removal guard has been registered for the kind.

docs.title: 4. Locale strings (new messages.yml keys)
docs.text:
Authored under the project's TSV pipeline (scripts/locale-files-to-csv.ps1 → reconcile-locale-csvs.ps1 → translate → locale-files-from-csv.ps1 → LocaleParityTest). All keys live under a new top-level multiconfig block; identity-mapped first-pass translations are acceptable for locales other than en and es per the project's translation guide.

multiconfig:
  header:
    default: "[parserKind]"
    regions: "Regions"
    worlds: "Worlds"
  toggle:
    removeMode:
      off: "[ ] Remove mode"
      on:  "[x] Remove mode (click an entry to delete)"
  row:
    add: "+ Add new..."
    addHover: "Type a name in the anvil prompt. Prefilled: [name]"
    editHover: "Edit [name]"
    removeHover: "Delete [name]"
  confirm:
    title: "Delete [name]?"
    yes: "Confirm delete"
    no:  "Cancel"
  lock:
    regionDefault: "The default region cannot be removed."
    worldLoaded:   "World '[name]' is loaded on the server. Unload it before removing its config."
  result:
    added:   "Added '[name]'."
    removed: "Removed '[name]'."
    addFailed:    "Could not add '[name]': [reason]"
    removeFailed: "Could not remove '[name]': [reason]"
    nameInvalid:  "Name '[name]' is not allowed. Use letters, digits, '_', '-', '.'"
    nameTaken:    "An entry named '[name]' already exists."

The [parserKind] and [name] placeholders follow the project's existing [token] placeholder convention and must be masked through the TSV translation step per the encoding/translation guide.

docs.title: 5. Tests (planned, none authored in this session)
docs.text:

docs.title: 7. Risks / open notes for the implementation session
docs.text:
• Effects kind. EffectsGroupKeys is already a MultiConfigParser (see Configs.java line 280). Adding a third admin-panel row would require an in-use guard for effects (probably: "locked if any active player has the effect group attached"). Out of scope for this slice; flagged here so the next iteration can lift it in.
  • Confirm-page placement. The confirm page sits between the click and the actual mutation. If the user navigates away (back row or selector re-open) between click and confirm, the staged mutation is dropped silently (mirrors the existing staging-cart contract - see MenuRedeemSubcommand.clearCart).
  • Cart key collision. The existing staging cart is single-file scoped per viewer. For OpenMultiConfigEntry the scope becomes (parserKind, entryName, fileName). Keying must be updated everywhere the cart is read/written, but the cart's contract (one staged file per viewer) is preserved. This is the largest non-obvious risk in the implementation session; budget time accordingly.
  • Toggle persistence across navigation. Decision: the remove-mode toggle survives navigation to and from the entry page (so opening an entry to "double-check before removing" then going back leaves the mode ON). It resets when the viewer leaves the selector for a non-multiconfig page (back to OpenConfigSelector / admin panel / front page) or when the token TTL expires.
  • Folia / region thread. All file-system mutations (add/remove YAML files) must run on the async scheduler per S-005. Reuse RTP.scheduler.runTaskAsynchronously exactly as the existing SubConfigCmd.onCommand does.

docs.title: D-005 Proposal — NeoForge Adapter Bring-Up (rtp-neoforge)
docs.text:
Status: APPROVED 2026-06-01 (project lead). Both Phase N1 preconditions (proposal approval + named maintainer) are cleared. The Phase N1 module skeleton landed 2026-06-02 (see checklist N1); the implementation surfaces (RTPServerAccessor, command wiring, S-005/S-006 guards) remain open carry-over. This is a scratch working note per Checklist-Based State Tracking in .junie/AGENTS.md. Delete or fold into the plan/ADR set once Phase N1 fully lands.

Effective Issue: "let's get neoforge support going" -> "fabric is confirmed stable" -> "planning artifacts" -> "let's do the skeleton and docs now". Mode: [CODE].

docs.title: 0. Why this proposal exists
docs.text: NeoForge is already a documented in-scope target platform per ADR-033, but ADR-033 §2 hard-gated activation behind Fabric stabilization, and §3 requires this D-005 proposal + a subproject ADR + plan rows + TRACEABILITY rows before any code lands. With Fabric now confirmed stable, the gate is clear and the bring-up sequence is unblocked. This document is item §3.1 of that sequence.

docs.title: 1. Activation gate — confirmed clear
docs.text:
ADR-033 §2 gate criteria, each now satisfied:

  • No open S-005 violations in rtp-fabric — FabricRTPWorld.getChunkAt returns CompletableFuture on the async chunk-load path (resolved).
  • FabricServerAccessor.getLocationGenerator null stub resolved — wired; throws IllegalStateException pre-init per S-006.
  • Loom dependency resolved — per-MC carrier split (rtp-fabric-ADR-009) in place.
  • Green rtp test full on at least one shipped MC carrier — Phase 2 Step H dual-runtime smoke test passed; Fabric beta shipped (Phase 3, 2026-05-31).
  • Fabric confirmed stable by the project lead (2026-06-01).

docs.title: 2. Affected modules
docs.text:
New, sibling to rtp-fabric (do not nest under or share a tree with it — ADR-033 alternatives, NEOFORGE_NOTES.md §11):

platforms/rtp-neoforge/
  docs/adr/                      # subproject ADRs, restart at 001
  REQUIREMENTS.md                # mirrors platforms/rtp-fabric/REQUIREMENTS.md
  rtp-neoforge-common/           # Mojmap, version-agnostic; rtp-api / rtp-core / stable NeoForge API only
  rtp-neoforge-v1_21_R1/         # per-MC carrier (NeoForge 1.20.4+); NM-typed surfaces isolated here
  rtp-neoforge-v26_2_R1/         # current target carrier (year-based MC versioning)

Reused 1:1, unchanged (platform-neutral): rtp-core, rtp-api, rtp-anvil, commands-api, effects-api, metrics-api, maps-api.

Touched only at the entry/bootstrap seam: rtp-plugin iff a combined multi-loader artifact is pursued (distribution decision, Phase N1).

No changes to rtp-core / rtp-api — the April 2026 gap analysis (re-confirmed for Fabric) holds for NeoForge: gaps are implementation, not interface (NEOFORGE_NOTES.md, ADR-033 §Context).

docs.title: 3. Intended before/after structure
docs.text:
• Before: four platform families (Bukkit, Paper, Folia, Fabric); NeoForge documented in-scope but no module under version control.
  • After (Phase N1 target): a fifth sibling family rtp-neoforge with a @Mod entry point + META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml, a NeoForgeVersionAdapter classpath-probe dispatcher (mirrors RTPFabricMod / RTPBukkitPlugin), and per-MC carriers. A single /rtp round-trip on the default world is the Phase N1 exit gate; optimization/anvil/ticket parity follow in Phase N2.

docs.title: 4. Key build/design decisions to ratify in the subproject ADR
docs.text:
• Gradle toolchain: ModDevGradle (closer to Loom in spirit, newer official path) over NeoGradle — NEOFORGE_NOTES.md §8. Applied only under platforms/rtp-neoforge/**.
  • Obf/unobf carrier: NeoForge is Mojmap-at-runtime on 1.20.4+, so most likely no obf carrier, but the per-version structural split (NM-typed surfaces isolated from rtp-core/rtp-api) is still required — NEOFORGE_NOTES.md §5.
  • Command registration: reuse BrigadierCommandAdapter (commands-api-ADR-001); only the registration trampoline differs (RegisterCommandsEvent on the mod bus vs. Fabric's CommandRegistrationCallback).
  • Threading: single-main-thread vanilla; no Folia region-ownership analog. Back-to-main-thread sink is MinecraftServer#submit / the server-tick executor.
  • Claim mods (FTB Chunks, OpenPartiesAndClaims, Argonauts): reflection-gated soft hooks per ADR-026; no claim-mod code in the pipeline (S-003).

docs.title: 5. Requirements / ADRs referenced
docs.text: ADR-033 (scope), NEOFORGE_NOTES.md (landscape/reuse/risks), rtp-fabric-ADR-002 (precedent shape), rtp-fabric-ADR-001, rtp-fabric-ADR-007, rtp-fabric-ADR-009, ADR-010, ADR-024, ADR-026, commands-api-ADR-001. New: REQ-NEOFORGE-F-* / REQ-NEOFORGE-ARCH-* (to be authored in platforms/rtp-neoforge/REQUIREMENTS.md); S-005 / S-006 guards ReqRtpNeoforgeS005ChunkLoadingTest / ReqRtpNeoforgeS006EarlyApiTest.

docs.title: 6. Risks & trade-offs
docs.text:
• Platform matrix grows four → five families; release-test and lite-jar (ADR-024) surfaces expand. Bounded by per-version carriers.
  • Mappings drift across MC revs — absorbed by per-version carriers; must not leak into rtp-core.
  • NeoForge mod-loading phases — the S-006 fail-loud guarantee is friendly here.
  • AccessTransformers / Mixins are a red flag: re-examine whether the public API suffices first.
  • Ownership gate: ADR-033 / ADR-022 require a named maintainer owning the platform end-to-end before Phase N1. Owner: project lead (@leaf_26), assigned 2026-06-01.

docs.title: 7. Bring-up checklist (ADR-033 §3 / NEOFORGE_NOTES.md §10)
docs.text:
• [x] N0.1 — D-005 proposal (this document).
  • [x] N0.2 — Subproject ADR rtp-neoforge-ADR-001-platform-in-scope.md drafted; README catalog row added.
  • [x] N0.3 — MULTI_PLATFORM_PLAN.md Phase N0 rows updated; activation-gate note reflects Fabric-stable.
  • [x] N0.4 — TRACEABILITY.md placeholder rows for the planned S-005 / S-006 guards (unimplemented).
  • [x] N0.5 — platforms/rtp-neoforge/REQUIREMENTS.md authored (Phase N0).
  • [x] N0.6 — Named maintainer assigned (ownership gate): project lead (@leaf_26), 2026-06-01.
  • [~] N1 — Module skeleton landed 2026-06-02 (platforms/rtp-neoforge/): ModDevGradle build wiring (rtp-neoforge-common + rtp-neoforge-v1_21_R1), META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml, @Mod entry point RTPNeoForgeMod (lifecycle + tick + RegisterCommandsEvent trampoline), complete server-thread NeoForgeScheduler, NeoForgeCommandRegistrar + carrier version-adapter scaffolds, README, and an opt-in -PincludeNeoforge settings.gradle include (keeps the default offline build green). Still open (carry-over): NeoForgeServerAccessor (RTPServerAccessor impl) + RTPAPI.serverAccessor binding, event bridge, database handler, the S-005 async chunk path, anvil/ticket parity, the single /rtp round-trip exit gate, and a network-host -PincludeNeoforge build verification.
  • [ ] N1.x — S-005 / S-006 REQ-traceable guards (ReqRtpNeoforgeS005ChunkLoadingTest, ReqRtpNeoforgeS006EarlyApiTest); TRACEABILITY rows reserved (unimplemented).

docs.title: 8. Still NOT done (carry-over for the maintainer)
docs.text:
• No NeoForgeServerAccessor (RTPServerAccessor implementation) yet; RTPAPI.serverAccessor is not bound and RTP.scheduler is not installed — the mod is lifecycle-only until this lands.
  • No event bridge, database handler, S-005 async chunk path, anvil-prefilter parity, or non-persistent chunk tickets.
  • No /rtp round-trip (the Phase N1 exit gate) and no S-005/S-006 REQ-traceable tests.
  • No network-host -PincludeNeoforge build verification (NeoForge/ModDevGradle artifacts are unavailable offline; the modules are gated out of the default build).
  • No rtp-core / rtp-api edits (gaps remain implementation-only, per the gap analysis).

docs.title: PROPOSAL: Phase 2e (SQL slice) - SqlNetworkStateBinding + Backend-Side Network Wiring
docs.text: Status: Proposed (docs-only, D-005 gating turn) Author: Junie session 2026-05-18 Scope: the minimum cut to make a real cross-process runtime test possible: 1 Velocity proxy + 2 Paper backends + 1 shared SQL DB, all of them seeing each other's heartbeats in a shared table. Supersedes nothing. Folds the SQL slice of rtp-proxy-ADR-011-sql-network-state-binding (Proposed) into a concrete implementation plan and pairs it with the missing backend-side publisher.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
After this proposal lands as code, the following devstack smoke test passes:

  1. Start 1x Velocity 3.3 + 2x Paper 1.21 + 1x MySQL 8 (or Postgres 16).
  2. All three JVMs read the same network.yml template with enabled: true, transport.type: sql, identical secretEnv (unused for SQL - see Q1), distinct proxyId / serverId.
  3. Within 2 * heartbeat.intervalMs of the last JVM booting, SELECT * FROM rtp_network_proxies returns 1 row and SELECT * FROM rtp_network_backends returns 2 rows.
  4. Killing either backend causes its row's last_seen_ms to stop advancing; after 3 * heartbeat.intervalMs the proxy's NetworkSnapshot no longer lists it as fresh.

That is the only acceptance criterion for this phase. No /rtp cross-server teleport, no ServerPreConnectEvent, no Brigadier /network status - those are Phase 2c / 2d / 2g.

docs.title: 2. Non-goals (deferred)
docs.text:
• Reservation token claim contention testing (claim / release are implemented but not exercised end-to-end until Phase 2c lands ServerPreConnectEvent).
  • HMAC / kill-switch wire enforcement (ADR-010): the SQL binding leans on DB connection auth + TLS; HMAC fields stay zeroed. Documented as N/A per PROPOSAL-sql-binding-first.md rev 2.
  • Redis binding (Phase 2e-Redis): peer to this, separate D-005 turn.
  • network.yml ships shaped but without Redis stanzas wired - those are skeleton-only.
  • Metrics axis. No MetricsBinding taps yet.

docs.title: 3.1 Module placement
docs.text:
rtp-proxy-common/
  src/main/java/.../proxy/common/transport/sql/
    SqlNetworkStateBinding.java          (NEW; implements NetworkTransport)
    SqlNetworkStateBindingFactory.java   (NEW; opens from JDBC URL + creds)
    SqlNetworkStateSchema.java           (NEW; DDL bootstrap)
    SqlHeartbeatPoller.java              (NEW; periodic SELECT + fan-out)
  src/test/java/.../proxy/common/transport/sql/
    SqlNetworkStateBindingH2Test.java    (NEW; H2 in-memory, two-instance fan-out)

rtp-proxy-common already depends on rtp-api (no JDBC there) - we add org.xerial:sqlite-jdbc and com.h2database:h2 as testRuntimeOnly, real production JDBC drivers (MySQL / Postgres) stay the deployer's responsibility (matching AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor's philosophy in rtp-core).

Open question Q2: Do we share rtp-core's HikariCP-backed pool from AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor, or does the SQL binding own its own small pool? See §7.

docs.title: 3.2 Backend-side wiring (the other half)
docs.text:
rtp-core/
  src/main/java/.../common/network/
    BackendStatePublisher.java           (NEW; mirrors ProxyStatePublisher)
    BackendStateSampler.java             (NEW; interface: snapshot() -> BackendHeartbeat row data)
  src/test/java/.../common/network/
    BackendStatePublisherTest.java       (NEW; deterministic cadence test)

rtp-plugin/src/main/resources/
  network.yml                            (NEW template; shipped, defaults to enabled:false)

platforms/rtp-bukkit/rtp-bukkit-common/
  src/main/java/.../bukkit/common/network/
    BukkitBackendStateSampler.java       (NEW; reads TPS/MSPT/playerCount from Bukkit)

rtp-plugin/
  src/main/java/.../bukkit/RTPBukkitPlugin.java
    (EDIT) onEnable: if network.yml -> enabled:true, open binding,
                     setNetworkStateBinding on DB accessor, start BackendStatePublisher
    (EDIT) onDisable: stop publisher in reverse order, close binding

rtp-core's BackendStatePublisher is platform-agnostic - it takes a BackendStateSampler SPI that each adapter implements. Mirrors how RTP.serverAccessor works.

docs.title: 4. SqlNetworkStateBinding shape
docs.text:
Public surface is exactly NetworkTransport. No new SPI. Internal shape:

public final class SqlNetworkStateBinding implements NetworkTransport {
    private final DataSource ds;                     // Hikari, see Q2
    private final Supplier<Instant> clock;
    private final SqlHeartbeatPoller poller;         // owns 1 daemon thread
    private final CopyOnWriteArrayList<Sub> subs;
    private final AtomicBoolean closed;
    private final String dialect;                    // h2 | sqlite | mysql | postgresql

    @Override public CompletableFuture<NetworkSnapshot> readSnapshot();
    @Override public CompletableFuture<ReservationToken> claim(...);
    @Override public CompletableFuture<Void> release(...);
    @Override public CompletableFuture<Void> publishProxyHeartbeat(...);
    @Override public Subscription subscribeBackendHeartbeats(...);
    @Override public void close();
}

docs.title: 4.1 SPI -> SQL mapping
docs.text:
NetworkTransport method SQL action publishProxyHeartbeat(row) INSERT INTO rtp_network_proxies ... ON CONFLICT(proxy_id) DO UPDATE SET ... (UPSERT) readSnapshot() SELECT * FROM rtp_network_backends WHERE last_seen_ms > ? - ? (now - staleness budget); returns NetworkSnapshot(nowMs, backendsMap) claim(serverId, playerId, ttl) one of two strategies, see §4.3 release(tokenId, reason) UPDATE rtp_network_tokens SET state = ?, released_at_ms = ? WHERE token_id = ? (idempotent on missing row) subscribeBackendHeartbeats(sink) sink stored in subs; SqlHeartbeatPoller fires sink.accept(row) every poll cycle for newly observed or refreshed rows

Backend-side publish (the missing direction): SqlHeartbeatPoller.publishBackendHeartbeat(row) does the same UPSERT against rtp_network_backends. The SPI does not currently expose this method; we add it as default on NetworkTransport (additive, in-memory binding implements it identically via publishBackendHeartbeat which already exists as a test affordance). This is the one SPI tweak.

docs.title: 4.2 DDL bootstrap (SqlNetworkStateSchema)
docs.text:
Idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on binding.open(). Per-dialect tweaks via switch on dialect. Sketch:

-- rtp_network_proxies
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rtp_network_proxies (
    proxy_id        VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    last_seen_ms    BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    player_count    INT          NOT NULL,
    kill_switch     BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    schema_version  INT          NOT NULL,
    updated_at_ms   BIGINT       NOT NULL
);

-- rtp_network_backends
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rtp_network_backends (
    server_id       VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    last_seen_ms    BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    tps             DOUBLE       NOT NULL,
    mspt            DOUBLE       NOT NULL,
    player_count    INT          NOT NULL,
    queue_depth     INT          NOT NULL,
    kill_switch     BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    schema_version  INT          NOT NULL,
    updated_at_ms   BIGINT       NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_backends_last_seen ON rtp_network_backends(last_seen_ms);

-- rtp_network_tokens
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rtp_network_tokens (
    token_id        VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    server_id       VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    player_id       VARCHAR(36)  NOT NULL,
    expires_at_ms   BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    state           VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL,    -- PENDING | CLAIMED | CONSUMED | RELEASED | EXPIRED
    created_at_ms   BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    released_at_ms  BIGINT
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_tokens_active_player
    ON rtp_network_tokens(player_id) WHERE state IN ('PENDING','CLAIMED');
-- (the partial index is Postgres / SQLite; MySQL needs a trigger or active-only table)

schema_version is REQ-RTP-NET-010 propagation; mismatched versions are logged and ignored on read.

docs.title: 4.3 Atomic claim (two strategies, dialect-gated)
docs.text:
• Postgres / MySQL 8+ / H2: INSERT INTO rtp_network_tokens (...) VALUES (...). The partial unique index on player_id enforces per-player idempotency at the DB level. Catch SQLIntegrityConstraintViolationException -> throw IllegalStateException("Reservation race") matching in-memory semantics.
  • SQLite / older MySQL: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE then INSERT inside a single transaction. Slightly slower; acceptable since SQLite is dev-only.

The PENDING -> CLAIMED transition is collapsed into a single INSERT ... VALUES (..., 'CLAIMED', ...) in the SQL binding (the in-memory two-step exists for race-test scaffolding; SQL gets atomicity from the DB).

docs.title: 4.4 SqlHeartbeatPoller
docs.text:
Single daemon thread, name rtp-proxy-sql-poller. Loop:

loop:
    sleep(network.transport.sql.pollIntervalMs)    // default 1000
    if closed: break
    try:
        nowMs = clock()
        staleAfterMs = network.heartbeat.staleAfterMs   // default 5000
        rows = SELECT * FROM rtp_network_backends WHERE last_seen_ms > nowMs - staleAfterMs
        for each row not in lastSeenCache or with newer updated_at_ms:
            for each sub: sub.sink.accept(row)
        lastSeenCache = rows.indexBy(serverId)
    catch SQLException: log WARNING, continue (transient DB blip is not fatal)

Polling overhead at N backends: O(1) query/sec/JVM. At 1Hz poll on a LAN MySQL: ~5-30ms per poll, negligible. Open question Q3: does this scale past N=32 without LISTEN/NOTIFY?

docs.title: 5.1 BackendStatePublisher (in rtp-core)
docs.text:
Mirror of ProxyStatePublisher:

public final class BackendStatePublisher {
    private final NetworkTransport transport;
    private final BackendStateSampler sampler;
    private final ScheduledExecutorService scheduler;   // 1 daemon thread
    private final long intervalMs;
    private final AtomicBoolean running = new AtomicBoolean();

    public void start();    // idempotent
    public void stop();     // idempotent, joins with 2s deadline (ADR-006 parity)
}

Cadence: network.heartbeat.intervalMs (default 1000). On each tick:

row = sampler.sample(nowMs)
transport.publishBackendHeartbeat(row)    // new default method on NetworkTransport

docs.title: 5.2 BackendStateSampler (SPI in rtp-core)
docs.text:
public interface BackendStateSampler {
    BackendHeartbeat sample(long nowMs);
}

Adapter implementations (only one in this phase):

  • BukkitBackendStateSampler (in rtp-bukkit-common): pulls TPS / MSPT from existing metrics taps, Bukkit.getOnlinePlayers().size(), queue depth from RegionQueueManager.keptLocations.size() (or equivalent - see Q4).

Folia / Paper inherit Bukkit's. Fabric: deferred.

docs.title: 5.3 Boot wiring in RTPBukkitPlugin
docs.text:
Pseudocode (real PR will respect existing init order):

@Override
public void onEnable() {
    super.onEnable();
    // ... existing setup ...

    File networkYml = new File(getDataFolder(), "network.yml");
    if (!networkYml.exists()) saveResource("network.yml", false);
    NetworkConfig netCfg = NetworkConfig.fromMap(toNestedMap(RtpYamlConfig.load(networkYml)));
    if (!netCfg.enabled()) {
        // REQ-RTP-NET-002 byte-identical no-op: no binding, no publisher, no thread.
        return;
    }
    NetworkTransport binding = openBindingForType(netCfg);  // sql | inMemory | redis-later
    ((AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor) RTP.databaseAccessor).setNetworkStateBinding(binding);
    BukkitBackendStateSampler sampler = new BukkitBackendStateSampler(this, netCfg.serverId());
    BackendStatePublisher publisher = new BackendStatePublisher(binding, sampler,
            netCfg.heartbeatIntervalMs());
    publisher.start();
    // store handles for onDisable
}

network.yml template (new resource):

# Network mode. Disabled by default; flip to true on every backend AND every proxy.
network:
  enabled: false
  serverId: "backend-1"   # MUST be unique per backend
  transport:
    type: "sql"           # sql | inMemory | redis (Redis: Phase 2e-Redis)
    sql:
      # Defaults to sharing the main RTP database (see Q2).
      pollIntervalMs: 1000
  heartbeat:
    intervalMs: 1000
    staleAfterMs: 5000
  schemaVersion: 1

(On the proxy side, the existing template adds proxyId and secretEnv; we keep them divergent for now - proxies don't need serverId, backends don't need proxyId.)

docs.title: 6.1 Unit (this turn's [CODE] follow-up)
docs.text:
1. SqlNetworkStateBindingH2Test:
  2. Boots H2 in-memory.
  3. Opens two SqlNetworkStateBinding instances against the same JDBC URL.
  4. Instance A: publishProxyHeartbeat(...); instance B: readSnapshot() -> sees the row (well, proxy heartbeat doesn't appear in NetworkSnapshot which only carries backends - tested separately via dumpProxies()-equivalent SELECT).
  5. Instance A: publishBackendHeartbeat(...); instance B's subscriber fires within 2 * pollIntervalMs.
  6. Instance A: claim(...); instance B's claim(...) for same player throws IllegalStateException.

  7. DDL is idempotent across open() calls.

  8. BackendStatePublisherTest:

  9. Deterministic clock; assert sampler called every intervalMs (+/- jitter budget).
  10. stop() joins within deadline.
  11. stop() is idempotent.

docs.title: 6.2 Integration smoke (manual, post-code)
docs.text: The Goal block at the top of this doc. Runs against a real docker-compose; not automated this turn.

docs.title: 6.3 No-op parity (regression guard)
docs.text: Extend ReqRtpNet002NetworkDisabledNoOpTest (in rtp-core) with one new assertion: when network.enabled:false, RTPBukkitPlugin.onEnable does not call setNetworkStateBinding(...) on the DB accessor. Currently it can't call it because the field is null; we lock that in.

docs.title: 7. Open questions
docs.text:
Q1. secretEnv semantics for the SQL binding. ADR-010 requires HMAC over wire envelopes; SQL has no envelope, just rows. Recommendation: secretEnv is read but unused when transport.type: sql (logged as INFO at boot: "transport=sql; HMAC verification N/A, relying on DB transport auth"). Same env var is required by the Redis binding so a network can switch without re-configuring backends. Confirm.

Q2. HikariCP pool sharing. Two options: - A. SqlNetworkStateBinding owns its own small pool (2-4 conns), independent of AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor's. Pro: zero interference with main DB workload. Con: doubles connection footprint. - B. Share AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor's DataSource; bump maximumPoolSize documentation guidance by +2. Pro: half the connection count. Con: a slow network poll could starve the main RTP workload. Recommendation: B, with maximumPoolSize docs bump. Confirm or override.

Q3. Polling beyond N=32. At 1Hz poll, N=32 backends * 2 proxies = 64 reads/sec - still trivial for MySQL. At N=128 (rare but possible), it's 256 reads/sec, also fine. Recommendation: ship polling as-is; defer LISTEN/NOTIFY (Postgres) / Debezium-style streaming to a follow-up ADR. Confirm.

Q4. Backend queueDepth field source. BackendHeartbeat has a queueDepth field. Most natural source is RegionQueueManager.keptLocations.size() + unkeptLocations.size(). But that's a region pool count, not a teleport-waitlist count. Recommendation: queueDepth = playerQueue.size() (the teleport waitlist), matching the REQ-RTP-NET-008 fairness metric. Confirm.

Q5. Where does openBindingForType live? Either rtp-proxy-common exposes a static factory (NetworkBindings.open(NetworkConfig, DataSource)) consumed by both proxy adapter and RTPBukkitPlugin, OR each side wires its own. Recommendation: static factory in rtp-proxy-common - keeps the transport.type switch in one place.

Q6. Module dependency direction. Backend-side wiring requires rtp-plugin to depend on rtp-proxy-common. Currently rtp-plugin -> rtp-core, and rtp-proxy-common -> rtp-api. Adding rtp-plugin -> rtp-proxy-common is acceptable (the dep is type-only - NetworkTransport, NetworkConfig, etc.). Alternative: move the SPI types into rtp-api and let both consume. Recommendation: add the dep - moving SPI to rtp-api exposes addon authors to proxy-shaped surfaces they don't need. Confirm.

docs.title: 8. Risk surface
docs.text:
• Moderate. New transport binding, new backend publisher, new resource file, new SPI default method (additive), modest edit to RTPBukkitPlugin. ~700-900 LOC across both modules.
  • Reversible. The default for network.enabled stays false; existing deployments see byte-identical behavior. REQ-RTP-NET-002 guard test is the safety net.
  • No S-00x exposure. No new chunk I/O, no main-thread blocking (BackendStatePublisher lives on its own daemon thread), no claim-plugin interactions.

docs.title: 9. Verdict step list (for the implementing turn that follows this proposal)
docs.text:
Assuming user approves Q1-Q6 as recommended:

  1. Add default method publishBackendHeartbeat(BackendHeartbeat) to NetworkTransport (in-memory binding already has it as test affordance - promote to override).
  2. Create SqlNetworkStateSchema (DDL string constants + idempotent bootstrap).
  3. Create SqlNetworkStateBinding + SqlHeartbeatPoller + SqlNetworkStateBindingFactory.
  4. Create NetworkBindings.open(NetworkConfig, DataSource) static factory in rtp-proxy-common.
  5. Create BackendStatePublisher + BackendStateSampler SPI in rtp-core.
  6. Create BukkitBackendStateSampler in rtp-bukkit-common.
  7. Ship network.yml template under rtp-plugin/src/main/resources/ (backend-shaped, defaults disabled).
  8. Wire RTPBukkitPlugin.onEnable / onDisable (gated on network.enabled).
  9. Update rtp-plugin/build.gradle: add implementation project(':rtp-proxy:rtp-proxy-common').
  10. Tests: SqlNetworkStateBindingH2Test, BackendStatePublisherTest, extend ReqRtpNet002NetworkDisabledNoOpTest.
  11. Update docs/dev/MULTI_SERVER_PLAN.md: tick Phase 2e-SQL items, add "Phase 2e-SQL slice landed" callout.
  12. Update docs/dev/TRACEABILITY.md: REQ-RTP-NET-005, REQ-RTP-NET-007, REQ-RTP-NET-008 partial implementations.
  13. Flip rtp-proxy-ADR-011 from Proposed to Accepted (date 2026-05-18 or following).
  14. Full .\gradlew build -> must be green.
  15. Mojibake / em-dash sweep on every touched file.

docs.title: 10. Not in this proposal (will be follow-up D-005 turns)
docs.text:
• Redis binding (Phase 2e-Redis): ADR-005, ADR-010 already Accepted; needs Lettuce wiring, Lua script SHA verify, HMAC verifier, pub/sub subscriber.
  • ServerPreConnectEvent interception + reservation redemption on Velocity (Phase 2c).
  • Brigadier /rtp on proxy + /network status (Phase 2d).
  • Devstack docker-compose.yml (ops, not code).
  • BungeeCord adapter (rtp-proxy-bungee): still scaffolding-only, out of scope until Velocity Phase 2 stabilizes.
  • Metrics axis taps.

docs.title: 11. Confirmation needed before any code lands
docs.text: Answers to Q1-Q6. The recommendations above are my defaults; any override is fine and will be reflected in the implementing turn.

docs.title: PROPOSAL - Plugin-Message Network Transport as the Default Tier (DB-free cross-server RTP, proxy auto-detect, lite-shipped)
docs.text: Status: Approved (design-only; no code in scope; D-005 gate cleared 2026-06-12 by repo owner leaf) Date: 2026-06-12 Owner: leaf (repo owner) Effective Issue: give the free/lite edition a competitive cross-server RTP story against EzRTP without sacrificing the large-network optimizations (durable reservation tokens, atomic claims, load-balanced selection) that justify the Pro Redis/SQL tiers. Make a plugin-messaging transport the default so that a database is not required for most operators, and auto-detect the proxy so the operator config shrinks to near-nothing. Refines: MULTI_SERVER_PLAN.md (plugin-message transport currently "dev-only", D2); ADR-024 (lite assembly scope); ADR-036 (network-mode umbrella); rtp-proxy-ADR-* transport-binding family. Reuses (no SPI changes): NetworkTransport, BackendHeartbeat, NetworkSnapshot, BackendSelector in rtp-proxy-common.

docs.title: 1. Thesis
docs.text:
EzRTP's "network" feature is a backend-only server selector: a static, hand-maintained servers: list per backend, online/offline detected by direct host:port server-list pings, and player movement performed by speaking the proxy's built-in plugin-messaging vocabulary (Connect) over the issuing player's connection. It needs no proxy plugin and no database. Its ceiling: it transmits only server up/down, never which regions/worlds are servable, and the server list drifts because every backend is configured by hand.

We can match its zero-infra baseline and beat its capability by shipping a PluginMessageNetworkBinding that implements the existing NetworkTransport SPI over the proxy's plugin-messaging channel, carrying our richer BackendHeartbeat (region availability, warm-cache counts, load) instead of a bare ping. Backends self-advertise, so the network assembles itself with no hand-typed server list.

This is purely an additive transport tier. The durable Pro tiers (RedisNetworkStateBinding, SqlNetworkStateBinding) remain unchanged behind the same SPI; the dispatcher, selector, and command/tab-complete layer do not know which transport is underneath.

docs.title: 2. Transport tiers (one SPI, four implementations)
docs.text:
Tier NetworkTransport impl Availability source Reservation / atomic claim Durable Edition 0 InMemoryNetworkStateBinding (existing) in-JVM yes (in-JVM) no dev/test 1 (new default) PluginMessageNetworkBinding BackendHeartbeat relayed via proxy Forward sub-channel best-effort / none (player re-issues on miss) no lite + Pro 2 SqlNetworkStateBinding (existing) DB UPSERT + poll (Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY) yes yes Pro 3 RedisNetworkStateBinding (existing) pub/sub yes (atomic Lua + HMAC token) yes Pro

MySQL is the free durable tier (tier 2); Postgres is the higher-performance tier-2 variant via LISTEN/NOTIFY. Redis (tier 3) is the lowest-latency, atomic-claim tier.

Selection precedence in network.yml: explicit transport.type wins; transport.type: auto (the lite default) resolves to tier 1 when a proxy is detected and to "disabled" when standalone.

docs.title: 3. PluginMessageNetworkBinding shape
docs.text:
Keep as much as possible in rtp-core behind a thin NetworkBridge seam, and only drop down to a platform/proxy adapter at the exact points where the platform plugin-messaging API must be called. This is not Bukkit-specific: a Fabric (or NeoForge) backend fronted by Velocity must reach the same binding, so the message framing, heartbeat assembly, TTL expiry, snapshot maintenance, and the auto state machine all live in rtp-core; only the raw "send these bytes on bungeecord:main over player P's connection" / "receive bytes" primitive is delegated to the adapter (Bukkit#sendPluginMessage, Fabric custom-payload, etc.).

Backend-side binding (rtp-core NetworkBridge + a small per-platform send/receive shim). Implements NetworkTransport:

  • publishBackendHeartbeat(BackendHeartbeat row) -> serialize the record (already carries serverId, regionsAvailable, worldsLoaded, regions, regionKeptCounts, acceptingRequests, pluginState, killSwitch, keptCount) and emit it on the proxy Forward (or ForwardToPlayer) sub-channel of bungeecord:main, throttled to a heartbeat interval (default 200 ticks, the EzRTP ping-interval-ticks analogue).
  • subscribeBackendHeartbeats(sink) / readSnapshot() -> maintain the last-seen BackendHeartbeat per serverId; expire entries on a TTL (the plugin-message analogue of ping-timeout-millis); invoke sink on change. readSnapshot() returns the assembled NetworkSnapshot.
  • Move: the dispatcher's connect step emits Connect <serverId> (or ConnectOther <player> <serverId>) on the issuing player's connection. The destination backend detects the join and runs a normal local /rtp.
  • claim / redeem / release / reapExpired / findReservation -> best-effort / no-op. There is no durable token store. On a miss (region drained, world unloaded, backend gone), the destination's local pipeline bounces with an S-007 configurable "busy / no such region" message and the player re-issues. This is the same correctness posture EzRTP lives with, but with real region data.

No rtp-proxy-common SPI surface changes: this is a peer of InMemoryNetworkStateBinding.

docs.title: 4. Proxy auto-detection (transport.type: auto)
docs.text:
Two layers:

Layer 1 - passive probe (gate, not source of truth). Read whether proxy forwarding is enabled: - Spigot: settings.bungeecord: true in spigot.yml. - Paper: proxies.bungee-cord / proxies.velocity in paper-global.yml. This arms network mode but supplies neither this backend's proxy name nor the sibling list.

Layer 2 - active handshake (the real detect + topology learn). Register bungeecord:main always; on the first player join, send: - GetServer -> proxy replies with this backend's own proxy name (operator never hand-types it). - GetServers -> proxy replies with the full backend-name list.

State machine: UNKNOWN -> (passive probe true) ARMED -> (first join: send handshake) PROBING -> (reply within timeout, default ping-timeout-millis: 1500) ENABLED; else DISABLED (standalone). Heartbeat gossip begins only in ENABLED. Re-probe on proxy reconnect.

Result: drop the jar on every backend, the network assembles itself - strictly better than EzRTP's static per-server servers: list.

docs.title: 5. network.yml (lite) shape
docs.text:
Minimal; mirrors EzRTP's servers.<name> vocabulary only where an operator must still express policy a backend cannot self-discover.

network:
  transport:
    type: auto        # auto | plugin-message | sql | redis | inMemory | disabled
    heartbeatTicks: 200
    staleTimeoutMillis: 1500
  # Optional per-server policy overlay; absent => discovered server is offered with defaults.
  servers:
    skyblock:
      permission: ""           # gate visibility/use of this destination
      display-name: "Skyblock"
      hide-when-unavailable: false
      allow-when-unavailable: false

There is no hand-typed server list required in auto mode: servers: is an optional policy overlay keyed by the discovered names. host/port are gone (availability is the heartbeat, not a socket ping).

docs.title: 6. Honest limitations (document loudly; they define the Pro upgrade boundary)
docs.text:
1. Everything rides a player connection. GetServers, Forward, and Connect require an online player on the sending backend. Auto-detect completes only on first join (acceptable). A player-empty backend cannot broadcast its heartbeat, so its availability goes stale/unknown.
  2. Unknown -> accept. isRelevant (execute-time region validation) must accept when the snapshot is unknown/stale and let the destination decide; suggestion filtering may stay strict. Otherwise transport lag becomes user-visible command failures.
  3. Single-proxy fan-out. Forward only reaches backends visible to one proxy. Multi-proxy (RedisBungee-style) networks need tier 2/3 - the clean, honest upgrade boundary.
  4. Non-durable. No reservation survives a proxy restart (D2). Worst case is a re-issued /rtp. Operators needing atomic, durable, load-balanced cross-server reservation move to MySQL/Postgres/Redis.
  5. Optional proxy companion (future). The existing rtp-proxy-velocity / rtp-proxy-bungee plugins can hold the channel open independent of player presence and relay heartbeats reliably - an enhancement, not a baseline requirement.

docs.title: 7. Tab-completion / validation (cross-server region parameter)
docs.text: A NetworkRegionParameter whose values() returns the cached availability snapshot for the chosen target server and whose isRelevant validates against the same snapshot with the §6.2 "unknown -> accept" grace. The snapshot provider is pluggable (config overlay / plugin-message / SQL / Redis) so the command layer is transport-agnostic. Pure-config operators (no transport) get a static declared list (EzRTP parity); the heartbeat tiers eliminate the drift.

docs.title: 8. What this does NOT change
docs.text:
• rtp-proxy-common SPI: zero changes. Tier 1 is a peer implementation.
  • Pro selector / claim / token logic: reused unchanged behind the SPI.
  • ADR-024 lite excludes (SQL drivers, Redis, Folia adapter classes): unchanged. Tier 1 adds no driver; the binding lives in a backend-reachable module and ships in lite. liteJarStructureCheck extended only to assert no Redis/SQL transport class leaks while permitting PluginMessageNetworkBinding.
  • S-00x: the destination always runs the normal local pipeline (spiral -> chunk -> safety), so S-001/S-004/S-005 hold; tier 1 transports intent, not a coordinate. Move failures are logged, never swallowed (S-004); busy/invalid messages are configurable (S-007).

docs.title: 9. Resolved decisions (formerly open questions)
docs.text:
1. Heartbeat serialization format - RESOLVED: reuse. Forward payloads reuse the existing Redis flat-field encoder (encodeBackend/decodeBackend) over the proxy channel, so tier 1/2/3 share one decoder and the BackendHeartbeat field set is identical across transports. No new wire format.
  2. Module ownership - RESOLVED: maximise rtp-core. The binding lives in rtp-core behind a NetworkBridge seam; only the raw platform plugin-messaging send/receive primitive is delegated to a per-platform shim (see §3). This is deliberately not a Bukkit-only adapter because Fabric/NeoForge backends can also sit behind Velocity. Backend-specific code appears only if/when we depend on the Bungee API directly; BungeeCord support is layered on top of the existing Velocity support later and is not required for this tier.
  3. Heartbeat delivery / cost - RESOLVED: use the proxy as the store. Rather than treating availability as a per-backend database status, the proxy itself is the rendezvous point - backends gossip BackendHeartbeat through it and origins read the last-seen snapshot from it. This is the DB-free analogue of the tier-2/3 status table; throttle stays at the default 200-tick heartbeat interval and is revisited only if chatty at large N.
  4. Velocity channel handling - DECISION: implement if absent. Confirm GetServer/GetServers/Connect/Forward are honored on current Velocity; we do not appear to exercise all of these yet, so any missing piece (notably the modern namespaced-channel registration and the GetServers/topology handshake) is in scope to add.
  5. auto re-probe - RESOLVED: re-probe. A standalone server that later joins a proxy must re-probe live (on first join and on proxy reconnect) rather than requiring a restart.

docs.title: 9a. Self-pausing backends (Fabric / NeoForge)
docs.text:
Fabric and NeoForge backends are valid proxy targets but self-pause after ~60 s of no player activity (Minecraft's idle-tick pause). Consequences for tier 1:

  • A paused backend stops ticking, so it cannot emit heartbeats and its auto handshake/gossip stalls - its snapshot entry goes stale exactly as the §6.1 player-presence limitation predicts. Treat "stale/unknown" the same as player-empty: unknown -> accept (§6.2), let the move + destination decide.
  • The Connect move still wakes a paused backend (the proxy transfer resumes ticking on player arrival), so cross-server RTP into a paused Fabric/NeoForge backend works; only its advertised availability is unreliable while paused.
  • Do not rely on a paused backend to answer a synchronous availability query. The staleTimeout must tolerate the idle-pause window (default 1500 ms is far shorter than 60 s, so a paused backend is correctly shown stale). Operators wanting always-fresh availability for idle backends are pointed at the durable tier-2/3 store (which survives independent of backend ticking) or the optional proxy companion (§6.5).

docs.title: 10. Verdict (ratification status)
docs.text:
Approved by repo owner leaf 2026-06-12; the docs-only ratification (steps 1-4) is done this turn.

  1. [DONE] Amended MULTI_SERVER_PLAN.md: plugin-message promoted from "dev-only" to tier-1 default (non-durable) per §2-§6 (new Amendment: Plugin-Message Default Tier section; D2, reservation, transport-order, config, and risk lines updated); player-presence limitation and tier-2/3 upgrade boundary documented.
  2. [DONE] Amended ADR-036 (network-mode umbrella): D2 reframed, transport tiers updated, new Amendment: Plugin-Message Promoted to Tier-1 Default section recording the default tier and the auto detection mode.
  3. [DONE] Amended ADR-024 (lite assembly): new 2026-06-12 amendment — lite ships PluginMessageNetworkBinding + the trimmed network.yml; liteJarStructureCheck extension scoped (Redis/SQL transport classes stay forbidden, plugin-message binding permitted).
  4. [DONE] Authored subproject ADR platforms/rtp-proxy/docs/adr/rtp-proxy-ADR-016-plugin-message-default-transport.md (Accepted) holding the binding contract (§3) and the auto state machine (§4); added rows to both ADR README tables.
  5. [PENDING] Land code in a follow-up D-005 turn (still gated): PluginMessageNetworkBinding, auto resolver, NetworkRegionParameter, network.yml schema, lite bootstrap wiring, audit extension, tests.

No source changes in this turn (docs-only ratification).

docs.title: PROPOSAL: rtp-proxy as the cross-server availability store (DB-free, lite-capable)
docs.text: Status: Approved (owner: leaf) - implementation in progress (Slice 1 landed 2026-06-13) Date: 2026-06-13 Author/Owner: leaf (repo owner) Supersedes/amends: ADR-036 (transport tiers), platforms/rtp-proxy/docs/adr/rtp-proxy-ADR-016-plugin-message-default-transport.md, ADR-024 (lite assembly) Builds on: approved PROPOSAL-plugin-message-network-default.md, the landed plugin-message tier (PluginMessageNetworkBinding, ProxyAutoDetector, NetworkBridge, PeerRegionRegistry topology seeding)

docs.title: 1. Motivation
docs.text:
Runtime testing of the lite/plugin-message tier surfaced two facts:

  1. Backend-to-backend heartbeat gossip does not converge. A Forward heartbeat must ride a player connection on both ends: the sending backend needs an online player to emit it, and the proxy only relays it to backends that also have an online player. On any quiet network (and on the test stack with a single player) backends are player-empty, so availability gossip never reaches a lobby. This is structural to backend-to-backend plugin messaging, not tunable. The plugin-message tier therefore remains viable only for the Connect move + GetServers topology (which need only the originating player's own connection), not as an availability model.

  2. Network mode is never booted on the lite assembly. RTPBukkitLitePlugin.onEnable (the lite-only bootstrap) does not call NetworkModeBootstrap.readLobbyModeEarly(...) and does not call networkBootstrap.boot(...). BootstrapSupport has no network hook either. Consequences observed on lite:

  3. RTP.lobbyMode stays false, so lite "lobby" servers run the normal local region processing (ScanTask pre-fill, DB hydrate, Region.execute() pulse) and initialise their default regions - the regression the operator reported versus the Pro jar (where RTPBukkitPlugin performs the early-read).
  4. No transport is opened, no ProxyAutoDetector runs, no heartbeat is ever published, and the topology seeding (Option 1) never fires - so the entire tier-1 plugin-message implementation already landed is inert under the lite jar.

Decision (owner, this session): pivot the availability model to use the proxy itself as the store ("use rtp-proxy as a database mechanism"). The proxy is the one process that is always present and never player-empty, so it is the natural authority for the network snapshot - with no Redis/MySQL dependency, preserving the DB-free promise.

docs.title: 2. Goals / Non-goals
docs.text:
Goals - Make cross-server region availability converge reliably without a database, by caching each backend's BackendHeartbeat in the proxy companion (rtp-proxy-velocity) and serving it back to lobbies. - Fix the two lite-bootstrap prerequisite bugs so the feature actually runs under the lite jar: early lobbyMode read + network boot. - Reuse the existing NetworkTransport SPI and BackendHeartbeat record; leave the dispatcher / BackendSelector / PeerRegionRegistry / NetworkRegionParameter read paths unchanged.

Non-goals - No durable persistence (proxy restart loses the in-memory cache; it re-warms as backends re-push). Durability stays the Pro Redis/SQL tier. - No atomic claim / reservation tokens on this tier (best-effort, same posture as plugin-message). - No multi-proxy fan-out beyond a single proxy's view (RedisBungee-class topologies remain the Redis/SQL upgrade boundary). - No BungeeCord companion in this slice (Velocity first; Bungee layered later).

docs.title: 3.1 Transport tier table (after this proposal)
docs.text:
Tier Transport Availability store Reservation Edition 0 plugin-message Connect move + GetServers topology proxy topology only (server list) none lite + Pro 1 (new default with companion) proxy availability cache BackendHeartbeat cached in the proxy companion, served to lobbies best-effort lite + Pro 2 SQL (MySQL free / Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY) DB rows durable Pro 3 Redis pub/sub atomic Lua claim + HMAC tokens Pro

Tier 0 (topology seeding) stays the zero-companion fallback for default-region routing. Tier 1 supersedes the non-viable backend-to-backend gossip as the real availability path.

docs.title: 3.2 Backend -> proxy push
docs.text:
• Each backend publishes its BackendHeartbeat (existing 14-field record, encoded via the shared BackendHeartbeatCodec) to the proxy companion over bungeecord:main whenever it has at least one online player and on the existing heartbeat.intervalMs cadence.
  • This needs only a player on the sending backend (not on a peer), so a backend with any traffic keeps the proxy's view fresh. A fully idle backend's entry simply ages out (TTL) - acceptable, and the documented limitation.

docs.title: 3.3 Proxy caches it ("the proxy is the database")
docs.text:
• rtp-proxy-velocity keeps a ConcurrentHashMap<serverId, BackendHeartbeat> with a last-seen timestamp; entries older than heartbeat.staleAfterMs are treated as stale/evicted.
  • The companion already holds the channel open independent of player presence, so the cache survives the contributing player leaving (within the stale window) - this is what the pure gossip tier could not do.
  • Direction B (operator-declared servers map, landed): to cover the all-backends-empty case (no live push ever arrives), the companion also reads an optional servers.<id>.regions map from the proxy network.yml and emits a synthetic READY row per declared server. A fresh live push always supersedes the declared row for the same server; a stale/absent push falls back to it. This is what makes cross-server tab-completion converge with zero players on the backends.

docs.title: 3.4 Lobby <- proxy query/push
docs.text:
• On a lobby's player connection, the lobby requests the snapshot (a new RTPNet-subchannel verb, e.g. SNAPSHOT_REQ); the companion replies with the cached heartbeats (SNAPSHOT_RSP). Optionally the companion pushes deltas to lobbies that have a player online.
  • The lobby feeds these into the same cachedSnapshot that PeerRegionRegistry/NetworkRegionParameter already read - so the command layer, suggestions, and validation are unchanged and now see real per-region availability even when the backend is currently empty.

docs.title: 3.5 SPI reuse
docs.text:
• New backend-side NetworkTransport impl (working name ProxyCacheNetworkBinding) whose readSnapshot()/subscribeBackendHeartbeats() are satisfied by the proxy query/push, and whose publishBackendHeartbeat() is the backend->proxy push. Reservation methods best-effort/no-op (D2 non-durable), mirroring PluginMessageNetworkBinding.
  • NetworkBridge gains the two snapshot verbs as default methods (so existing shims/test doubles compile unchanged), implemented concretely in BukkitNetworkBridge and mirrored on the Velocity companion.

docs.title: 3.6 Lite-bootstrap prerequisite fixes (in scope)
docs.text:
• Fix A (lobbyMode regression): RTPBukkitLitePlugin.onEnable must perform the same early RTP.lobbyMode = NetworkModeBootstrap.readLobbyModeEarly(ensureNetworkYml(...)) before region hydrate that RTPBukkitPlugin does. Best-effort, defaults to false. Confirming test: a lite lobby seed with routing.lobbyMode: true must not hydrate regions.
  • Fix B (network never boots on lite): wire networkBootstrap.boot(networkYml) into the lite bootstrap (shared helper in BootstrapSupport is the cleanest place so both editions call one path), so the transport/ProxyAutoDetector/heartbeat machinery actually starts under lite. Without this, every network feature is inert on the lite jar regardless of transport choice.
  • These two are prerequisites: the proxy-as-store work is unobservable on lite until network mode boots there.

docs.title: 4. network.yml
docs.text:
• transport.type gains proxy-cache (and auto resolves to it when a companion is detected, falling back to topology-only tier 0 when not).
  • No new operator-required keys: cadence/staleness reuse the existing heartbeat.intervalMs / heartbeat.staleAfterMs. Channel reuses bungeecord:main.
  • All changes shipped through the locale TSV pipeline per AGENTS.md.

docs.title: 5. Risks / limitations (document loudly)
docs.text:
• Idle backend ages out. A backend with zero players stops pushing; its availability goes stale and is treated as UNKNOWN -> accept (destination decides on arrival). Fabric/NeoForge self-pause (~60 s) makes this more frequent on those backends.
  • Proxy restart = cold cache. Re-warms as backends re-push; no durability. Pro Redis/SQL for always-fresh.
  • Single-proxy scope. Multi-proxy networks need the Redis/SQL tier; documented as the upgrade boundary.
  • Companion required for tier 1. Without the proxy companion installed, the system degrades to tier 0 (topology-only default-region routing) - still functional, just coarser.

docs.title: 6. Proposed build order (separate approved coding turns)
docs.text:
1. [DONE 2026-06-13] Lite-bootstrap Fix A + Fix B - unblocks everything on lite, fixes the reported regression. RTPBukkitLitePlugin.onEnable now performs the early readLobbyModeEarly (before region load) and calls networkBootstrap.boot(networkYml), registers the cross-server JoinTriggerSource + waitlist wiring, and onDisable calls networkBootstrap.shutdown(). Full multi-module build green. (No lite-bootstrap unit test added: the glue requires MockBukkit; readLobbyModeEarly itself is already covered by LobbyModeEarlyReadTest.)
  2. [DONE 2026-06-13] ProxyCacheNetworkBinding + NetworkBridge snapshot verbs + BukkitNetworkBridge impl. Added ProxyCacheNetworkBinding (rtp-core) reusing the snapshot/TTL/subscriber machinery, with publishBackendHeartbeat -> pushHeartbeatToProxy + requestSnapshot (self-pumped by the existing BackendStatePublisher cadence). Added pushHeartbeatToProxy/requestSnapshot default verbs to NetworkBridge. Implemented both in BukkitNetworkBridge over a dedicated rtp:net companion channel (PROXY_PUSH/PROXY_SNAPSHOT_REQ/PROXY_SNAPSHOT_RSP framing), separate from bungeecord:main. Wired proxy-cache case into NetworkModeBootstrap.openTransport and switched auto (when armed) to prefer ProxyCacheNetworkBinding (Q2: prefer when armed; degrades to tier-0 topology routing when no companion answers). ProxyCacheNetworkBindingTest 5/5 green.
  3. [DONE 2026-06-13] Velocity companion availability cache + SNAPSHOT_REQ/RSP handling. Added VelocityProxyAvailabilityCache (pure logic: merges operator-declared servers.<id>.regions synthetic READY rows with live backend pushes, live-wins-while-fresh, TTL = heartbeat.staleAfterMs) and VelocityProxyCacheListener (registers the rtp:net companion channel, caches PROXY_PUSH payloads via BackendHeartbeatCodec, answers PROXY_SNAPSHOT_REQ with one PROXY_SNAPSHOT_RSP frame per known server). Wired into RtpVelocityPlugin.onProxyInitialize (parse servers: block + register channel/event listener) with shutdown deregistration; added the documented servers: block to network-proxy.yml. The operator-declared map (direction B) lets a lobby populate cross-server /rtp region= tab-completion even when every backend is player-empty. VelocityProxyAvailabilityCacheTest 5/5 green; full multi-module build green.
  4. network.yml proxy-cache/auto schema + locale pipeline.
  5. Lite-jar audit (assert binding present, no Redis/SQL leak) + docs/ADR amendments + devstack -Lite acceptance.

docs.title: 7. Open questions for owner
docs.text:
• Q1: Companion verb naming/wire layout under the RTPNet subchannel - reuse the codec framing 1:1? (default: yes)
  • Q2: Should auto prefer proxy-cache over tier-0 topology whenever any companion reply is seen, or require a config opt-in? (default: prefer when detected)
  • Q3: Put the shared lite/full network-boot call in BootstrapSupport (one path) vs duplicating in each bootstrap? (default: BootstrapSupport)

docs.title: PROPOSAL: proxy-direct = a simple, redis-equivalent data-management transport
docs.text: Status: DRAFT (design-first; awaiting user approval before implementation) Supersedes (on acceptance): the bespoke teleport leg of rtp-proxy-ADR-018 (OP_ENROL / OP_REDEEM_QUERY + ProxyDirectRedeemListener). Keeps: rtp-proxy-ADR-017 (the player-independent backend->proxy TCP socket).

docs.title: 1. Goal (the one-sentence contract)
docs.text:
proxy-direct shall be exactly what redis and sql already are -- a NetworkTransport + NetworkRequestQueue binding pair backed by a single shared store -- except the shared store is the proxy's own in-memory maps, reached over the existing proxy-direct TCP socket instead of a Redis/JDBC server.

Litmus test for "simple option other than redis for data management": every cross-server behaviour (region discovery, enrolment, dispatch, reservation, arrival redeem) must run through the same SPI calls and the same proxy-side code that the Redis tier uses. The only thing that changes between transport.type: redis and transport.type: proxy-direct is where the bytes land. No teleport-specific opcodes, no parallel arrival listener.

docs.title: 2. The mental model (who is the "redis server")
docs.text:
Role Redis tier proxy-direct tier The shared store external Redis the proxy JVM's InMemoryNetworkStateBinding + InMemoryNetworkRequestQueue (already constructed today, RtpVelocityPlugin lines 197/213/278) Backend transport RedisNetworkStateBinding (client) ProxyDirectNetworkBinding (RPC client) Backend queue RedisNetworkRequestQueue (client) ProxyDirectNetworkRequestQueue (RPC client, new) The wire RESP over TCP to Redis length-prefixed HMAC frames over TCP to the proxy listener (already exists)

The proxy is the always-on process, so it plays the part Redis plays: it owns the data; backends are stateless clients that read/write it. This is precisely the user's "the proxy server takes the role of the redis server."

docs.title: 3. What already works and is REUSED unchanged
docs.text:
On the proxy, in proxy-direct mode, these are already constructed and running (verified in RtpVelocityPlugin.onProxyInitialize):

  • transport = InMemoryNetworkStateBinding (the store for heartbeats + reservations).
  • requestQueue = in-memory NetworkRequestQueue (the enrolment FIFO).
  • DefaultRtpDispatcher (selector + transport.claim + sender.createConnectionRequest).
  • TransportRequestTriggerSource (drains the queue, feeds the dispatcher).
  • ReservationTokenReaper, the ServerPreConnectEvent redeem listener, the waitlist drainer.

None of this changes. Today it operates on an empty store because backends write to their own separate in-memory instances. The whole fix is: point the backends' SPI calls at the proxy's instances.

docs.title: 4.1 Wire (ProxyDirectWire) -- generic RPC, not teleport verbs
docs.text:
Replace OP_PUSH / OP_ENROL / OP_REDEEM_QUERY with one opcode per SPI method actually invoked from a backend (the only RPC direction; the proxy never dials a backend):

OP_HEARTBEAT_AND_SNAPSHOT  // publishBackendHeartbeat(row) -> readSnapshot rows   (= today's PUSH)
OP_FLUSH_PENDING           // NetworkRequestQueue.flushPending(batch) -> EnrolOutcome
OP_POLL_STATUS             // NetworkRequestQueue.pollStatus(ids)     -> List<QueueStatus>
OP_CANCEL                  // NetworkRequestQueue.cancel(id, reason)  -> ack
OP_FIND_RESERVATION        // NetworkTransport.findReservation(id)    -> Optional<ReservationToken>
OP_REDEEM                  // NetworkTransport.redeem(tok,id,server)  -> RedeemOutcome
OP_LIST_ACTIVE_FOR_SERVER  // NetworkTransport.listActiveForServer(s) -> List<ReservationToken>

Each frame: byte opcode, one signed request payload (delimited fields), one signed response payload (or count+rows for list returns). HMAC + framing helpers are reused verbatim. Request fields are simple strings (UUIDs, server ids, region keys, enum names); ReservationToken serialises its 6 fields (tokenId, serverId, playerId, expiresEpochMs, state, regionKey).

Methods that are proxy-local only are never RPC'd: claim, dequeueReady, transition, release, reapExpired, publishProxyHeartbeat, subscribeBackendHeartbeats. They run on the proxy against its own store, as today.

docs.title: 4.2 Backend client (rtp-core)
docs.text:
• ProxyDirectNetworkBinding (existing) becomes a full RPC NetworkTransport: publishBackendHeartbeat, readSnapshot (as today), plus findReservation, redeem, listActiveForServer via RPC. claim throws UnsupportedOperationException (a backend never claims; the proxy does). release/publishProxyHeartbeat stay no-ops (proxy-side concerns).
  • ProxyDirectNetworkRequestQueue (new, rtp-core) implements NetworkRequestQueue: enrol/flushPending/pollStatus/cancel via RPC; dequeueReady returns empty and transition returns empty (backends never drain -- those are proxy-local).

docs.title: 4.3 NetworkModeBootstrap (rtp-core)
docs.text:
• openRequestQueue("proxy-direct") returns the new remote queue instead of null. The existing flush-sink wiring (NetworkEnrolmentBuffer -> requestQueue.flushPending) then lights up with no special-casing -- the same code path the SQL/Redis tiers use.
  • Delete the proxyDirectRedeemListener field + its registration. Arrival redeem returns to the standard JoinTriggerSource (it already calls transport.findReservation + transport.redeem, which now RPC to the proxy).

docs.title: 4.4 Proxy listener (rtp-proxy-velocity)
docs.text:
• ProxyDirectListener gains an RPC dispatch switch that calls the already- built transport and requestQueue instances (passed in from RtpVelocityPlugin, replacing the current onPush/snapshotRows/onEnrol/ onRedeemQuery lambdas). OP_HEARTBEAT_AND_SNAPSHOT keeps feeding the availability cache for tab-completion.
  • Delete onProxyDirectEnrol / onProxyDirectRedeemQuery / the proxyDirectPending TTL map. The dispatcher's createConnectionRequest (driven by the trigger source) now performs the move, and claim records the reservation the arriving backend redeems.

docs.title: 5. End-to-end flow after the change (identical to Redis, different bytes)
docs.text:
1. Backend boot: publishBackendHeartbeat (RPC) -> proxy store has its regions -> lobby readSnapshot (RPC) -> /rtp region= tab-completion populated. (Zero players; unchanged from today.)
  2. Lobby /rtp region=backend-a:default: router enrols -> NetworkEnrolmentBuffer flush -> flushPending (RPC) -> proxy's in-memory queue.
  3. Proxy TransportRequestTriggerSource dequeues -> dispatcher selects backend -> transport.claim writes a reservation into the proxy store -> sender.createConnectionRequest moves the player. (All existing proxy code.)
  4. Player lands on backend-a: standard JoinTriggerSource -> findReservation (RPC) -> redeem (RPC) -> local /rtp region=default. (All existing code.)

docs.title: 6. Reservations: kept this pass (explicit)
docs.text: Per the user's note, "no per-player reservations" is a future cleanup about an already-implemented concept, not a constraint on this refactor. This proposal keeps reservation tokens so the arrival path reuses JoinTriggerSource verbatim. A later, separate change may slim the proxy-direct store to a region-only pending map if desired; it is out of scope here.

docs.title: 7. Why this is "simple" (and not more than needed)
docs.text:
• Net new types: one (ProxyDirectNetworkRequestQueue). Everything else is edits to existing files.
  • Net deleted surface: the three bespoke teleport opcodes, ProxyDirectRedeemListener, and the proxy-side pending-map + enrol/redeem lambdas.
  • Zero new concepts on the proxy: the dispatcher, trigger source, reaper, and preconnect redeem are untouched.
  • transport.type switches a backend between redis, sql, and proxy-direct with no behavioural branches anywhere except the binding factory -- the definition of a drop-in data-management option.

docs.title: 8. Risks / decisions for sign-off
docs.text:
1. Blocking RPC on backend threads. Each RPC opens a short-lived socket. publishBackendHeartbeat/readSnapshot already do this on the scheduler tick. findReservation/redeem run from JoinTriggerSource; they must be dispatched on RTP.scheduler's async tier (as the retired redeem listener already did) so no join/tick thread blocks. flushPending/pollStatus run from the existing buffer/status-cache timers (already async).
  2. One socket per RPC vs. pooling. Simplest correct choice is one connect-per-call (matches today's heartbeat exchange). Acceptable for lite scale; a keep-alive pool is a later optimisation, not needed for correctness.
  3. Multi-proxy. A backend dials every configured proxy. For reservations the first definite answer wins (as the snapshot read already does). Cross-proxy ownership is a durable-tier concern; proxy-direct remains single-proxy-simple and is documented as such.
  4. ADR. On approval, supersede the teleport portion of rtp-proxy-ADR-018 with a new rtp-proxy-ADR (or a revision) recording "proxy-direct = remote in-memory store across the full SPI."

docs.title: 9. Out of scope
docs.text:
• The region-publish limiter (deferred earlier by the user).
  • Reservation removal (section 6).
  • Keep-alive/pooled sockets, Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY, BungeeCord.

docs.title: PROPOSAL: rtp menu config search
docs.text: Status: DRAFT, awaiting explicit user approval (Rule D-005). Author: Junie session 2026-05-19. Effective Issue: "A user had difficulty tracing a specific message. We should add a search option to our config stuff in rtp menu ... start with the rtp menu command ... cast off color for the text search otherwise it will be unusable with gradients."

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Add a first-class search entry to the rtp menu config flow that lets an operator find any config key or value across every loaded config file by typing a free-form substring, and jumps from each hit to the existing per-key config menu page.

The motivating use case: an admin sees a message in chat (e.g. "You are not allowed to RTP here.") and wants to know which messages.yml key produced it without grepping the jar.

docs.title: 2. User-confirmed constraints (this session)
docs.text:
1. Search spans all config files at once (not a single file).
  2. Search matches both keys and values (comments excluded; the user explicitly noted "if we ignore comment lines" the corpus is small).
  3. Case-insensitive substring match.
  4. No result cap ("the sum of config files aren't that big").
  5. Render hits as a multi-page book, one row per hit, clickable to open the existing config-key page that manages that file/key (reuses MenuAction.OpenConfigKey).
  6. Visual: gray base text with off-blue highlight on the matched substring.
  7. Search must operate on color-stripped text for both the haystack and the needle. Legacy &/§ codes, modern hex (&#rrggbb) and gradient spans must NOT break substring matching. Highlight runs are computed against the stripped form and projected back onto raw offsets.
  8. Display the raw (un-rendered) text in each result row, not the colorized rendering (user update 2026-05-19: "we can display the raw text to the user so they know they can add or remove colors"). Operators must be able to see every &a, §l, &#rrggbb, gradient tag, etc. that is actually present in the config so they know what color codes exist and can decide to add or remove them. The off-blue highlight is overlaid on top of that raw text at the projected raw-offset ranges from §2.7. This is a deliberate departure from the file-view page (which renders colors) — search results are an editing aid, not a preview.
  9. Entry point: a search button on the config selector page plus an anvil-input prompt for the query string (same mechanism PromptAnvilInput already uses for param pickers).

docs.title: 3. Affected modules / classes
docs.text:
Module Class Change rtp-api MenuAction (sealed interface) Add 2 records: OpenConfigSearchPrompt, OpenConfigSearchResults(String query, int page). rtp-api tests MenuModelSurfaceTest.menuActionSealedShape Bump permitted-subclasses count from 13 -> 15; add the 2 new names to the expected set. rtp-api MessagesKeys Add keys: menuConfigSearchButton, menuConfigSearchPromptTitle, menuConfigSearchEmpty, menuConfigSearchResultsHeader, menuConfigSearchResultRow, menuConfigSearchTooShort. rtp-core new ConfigSearchResultsBuilder Walks every ConfigParser + MultiConfigParser, color-strips keys+values, case-insensitive substring match, returns ordered List<Hit> with raw value, stripped value, and match offsets in stripped space. rtp-core new helper ColorStrip (or reuse existing — see §6 open question) Strips legacy &x/§x, hex &#rrggbb, and any MiniMessage-style <gradient:..>...</gradient> / <color:..> runs.
