Returns the stripped string + an int[] offset map so highlight ranges can be projected back to raw offsets. rtp-core MenuRedeemSubcommand Two new dispatch arms: dispatchOpenConfigSearchPrompt (mints anvil-input action with continuation = OpenConfigSearchResults(query, 0)), dispatchOpenConfigSearchResults (builds page via ConfigSearchResultsBuilder, hands to MenuRenderer). rtp-core ConfigMenuConsumerProfile (or its selector builder) Adds a "Search" button row on the config selector page emitting OpenConfigSearchPrompt. rtp-core page builder new ConfigSearchResultsPageBuilder Renders one MenuRow per hit: &7[file] key.path = <raw literal value with off-blue highlight on the matched substring>; row click action = OpenConfigKey(file, keyPath). Pagination via existing book-pagination machinery (same as the file view builder). Raw value is emitted as literal text — no legacy/hex code translation pass before the gray-base + off-blue-highlight component is built (constraint §2.8). rtp-plugin (Bukkit family) AnvilInputOpener wiring Already exists; the new prompt re-uses it. No new platform code, just a new continuation tag understood by the existing redeem path. rtp-plugin/src/main/resources/messages.yml + every lang/<locale>/messages.yml via TSV pipeline Locale entries for the new MessagesKeys. Per the Locale Config TSV Pipeline section of AGENTS.md: edit baseline, run locale-files-to-csv -> reconcile-locale-csvs -> translate -> locale-files-from-csv -> LocaleParityTest.

No platform adapters beyond the Bukkit family need changes; Fabric and Folia inherit through rtp-core and the existing AnvilInputOpener abstraction (Fabric falls back to chat-prompt today, which is acceptable for a v1).

docs.title: 4. Before / after
docs.text:
Before: /rtp menu config opens a selector page. Each row is a config file; clicking opens that file's keys. To find the source of a specific message, the operator must page through messages.yml manually or grep the jar.

After: /rtp menu config selector gains a "Search" button at the top. Clicking it opens an anvil input prompt titled "Search all configs". On submit, OpenConfigSearchResults(query, 0) is redeemed; the renderer shows a paginated book of all hits across every loaded config. Each row shows the raw, literal text of the value (color codes visible as-is) so the operator can see what formatting is in place and decide whether to add or remove codes — the off-blue highlight overlays the matched substring at its projected raw offsets:

[messages.yml] notPermitted           = &7You are not allowed to RTP &9&lhere&7.
[messages.yml] menuInvalid            = &7Unknown menu command: &9&lsearch&7
[regions/default.yml] biome.whitelist  = &#7f7f7fplains, &9&lforest&7, jungle

The literal &7, &9&l, &#7f7f7f, etc. are displayed as text, not interpreted as color. The substring here / search / forest is rendered in the off-blue accent color (on top of the raw text); everything else in the row is the menu's gray base color. Each row is clickable; clicking jumps straight to the existing per-key config menu page (the same page /rtp config <file> view -> click-on-row already opens). Back button returns to the search-results page; another Back returns to the selector.

docs.title: 5. Threading / safety
docs.text:
• All config reads happen on the dispatching thread inside the existing MenuRedeemSubcommand async pipeline (no main-thread chunk I/O — S-005 unaffected).
  • The new dispatch arms gate on permission rtp.config and on senderId != null (consistent with the other OpenConfig* arms).
  • Token registry: each result page render mints a fresh OpenConfigSearchResults(query, page) token for prev/next, and one OpenConfigKey(file, key) token per result row. Existing TTL / per-player isolation rules apply; no new registry primitives.
  • No DB or chunk allocations; MemoryTracker unaffected.

docs.title: 6. Open questions / verification needed before writing code
docs.text:
1. Color-strip helper reuse: ~~does SendMessage or the MiniMessage renderer already expose a "strip every formatting code, return stripped string + offset map" helper?~~ Investigated 2026-05-19: there is no canonical platform-agnostic strip helper in rtp-api or rtp-core today. The existing strip implementations are:
  2. org.bukkit.ChatColor.stripColor(...) — direct Bukkit call, used in rtp-bukkit-common/SendMessage.java:428 and rtp-paper-common/AnvilInputSession.java:148. Bukkit-only, handles §x but not &x legacy codes nor &#rrggbb hex.
  3. FabricLegacyText.stripColor(String) and FabricAnsiText.stripColor(String) (rtp-fabric-common/tools/) and FabricLegacyText.stripColor(String) in rtp-fabric-common-unobf/tools/ — Fabric-side, handles §x, &x, and &#RRGGBB hex (via normalise -> HEX_PATTERN). Not callable from rtp-core (Fabric module).
  4. No helper anywhere in the codebase returns a stripped-string-plus-offset-map.

Gap surfaced by user (Effective Issue 2026-05-19): "I don't think we have a canonical way to strip without a direct call to bukkit yet. We should add that for multiple reasons if we're missing it." Confirmed; we don't.

Proposed resolution (part of this proposal, not a separate one): add a new utility class io.github.dailystruggle.rtp.common.text.LegacyColorStrip in rtp-core (platform-agnostic, no Bukkit/Fabric imports) that: - ports the strip logic from FabricLegacyText.stripColor + normalise (which already covers &x, §x, and &#rrggbb hex — the union we need), - exposes two surfaces: String strip(String) (drop-in replacement for ChatColor.stripColor) and StripResult strip2(String) returning { String stripped, int[] strippedToRaw } for the search-highlight projection, - has a unit test (LegacyColorStripTest) covering each color syntax including a gradient-flavored input. Once landed, follow-ups (recorded in POTENTIAL_BUGS.md if not done in-scope): migrate the Bukkit ChatColor.stripColor call sites in SendMessage.java:428 and AnvilInputSession.java:148 to the canonical helper; Fabric's three callers can stay (they're already in Fabric-internal code and the Fabric helper would just delegate).

This is what the user's question in the Effective Issue is asking us to do, and it is the prerequisite for the search feature's color-stripped matching (constraint §2.7). Treat the strip helper as a checklist item ahead of ConfigSearchResultsBuilder, not a separate proposal. 2. Sealed-shape test location: ~~confirm exact test path.~~ Investigated 2026-05-19: confirmed rtp-api/src/test/java/io/github/dailystruggle/rtp/api/menu/MenuModelSurfaceTest.java, method menuActionSealedShape (lines 41-59). It asserts assertEquals(13, permitted.length) and a sorted List.of(...) of simple class names. Bump to 15 and insert "OpenConfigSearchPrompt" and "OpenConfigSearchResults" in sorted position (between OpenConfigSelector / OpenConfigSubParamPage and OpenExternalUrl). 3. OpenConfigKey argument shape: ~~confirm it already accepts (fileName, keyPath) and resolves the key path~~ Investigated 2026-05-19: confirmed record OpenConfigKey(String fileName, String paramName) at MenuAction.java:310. Server-resolved by MenuRedeemSubcommand.dispatchOpenConfigKey against the live CommandParameter for paramName on the file. Search result rows can construct OpenConfigKey(file, paramName) directly and let the existing dispatch arm route to the same page that /rtp config <file> view -> row-click opens. Caveat: paramName is the typed enum key name (e.g. RegionKeys.shape), not a free-form YAML path; the builder must look up matches against the parser's enum keys and yield the enum name. Values that live under nested YAML sections inside a single enum key (e.g. vert.minY under RegionKeys.vert) will still resolve at the enum-key level (one result row per enum key, not per nested sub-path) — acceptable for v1 (the key page already surfaces the nested form). 4. PromptAnvilInput continuation contract: ~~confirm the existing prompt action supports a typed continuation~~ Investigated 2026-05-19: confirmed it does not. record PromptAnvilInput(String[] parentPath, String paramName, String prefill) at MenuAction.java:226 is resolved entirely renderer-side (per Javadoc: "Resolved entirely on the renderer side (Paper/Folia); never enters the MenuRedeemSubcommand dispatch path"); on submit the platform synthesizes /rtp <parentPath...> <paramName>:<typed> and runs it through the normal command pipeline. There is no carried next-action descriptor.

Implication for this feature: the proposed OpenConfigSearchPrompt action cannot reuse PromptAnvilInput as-is. Two viable shapes: - (A) Mint the prompt as PromptAnvilInput(parentPath=["menu","config","search"], paramName="query", prefill="") and have the menu config search subcommand (a thin new TreeCommand leaf under MenuRedeemSubcommand) accept query:<text>, build the results model itself, and hand it to the renderer. This piggybacks on the existing pipeline (/rtp menu config search query:foo) and adds zero new menu-action variants on the prompt side — only OpenConfigSearchResults(query, page) remains needed for pagination + the selector-button entry. Preferred. - (B) Add a small extension to PromptAnvilInput (or a sibling variant PromptAnvilInputThen(parentPath, paramName, prefill, MenuAction continuation)) so the post-submit action is carried by the prompt itself. Cleaner long-term but a wider API surface change; defer unless (A) hits a blocker.

Decision (this proposal): adopt (A). The OpenConfigSearchPrompt record becomes a thin pointer that the renderer translates to PromptAnvilInput(["menu","config","search"], "query", "") client-side; the actual submit goes through the command pipeline, parses query:<text>, and routes to the same builder used by dispatchOpenConfigSearchResults. This keeps sealed-shape additions at 2 (prompt + results) and avoids extending PromptAnvilInput. The thin menu config search TreeCommand leaf is in scope for this proposal; add it to §3 and checklist item 5. 5. MultiConfigParser iteration: ~~confirm the public surface for "give me every (key, raw value)" pair~~ Investigated 2026-05-19: confirmed listParsers(): Set<String> + getParser(name): ConfigParser<E> at MultiConfigParser.java:150-174. Walk: for each MultiConfigParser in RTP.configs.multiConfigParserMap, call listParsers(), then for each name getParser(name) and enumerate that parser's enum keys + getConfigValue(key, null). Each sub-parser carries its own file/name, so per-world overrides (regions/<world>.yml, worlds/<world>.yml) surface as distinct hit-source labels naturally.

All §6 items now verified. Proposal is ready for implementation modulo Q4's Decision (A) above, which adds a TreeCommand leaf to the affected-classes list — apply when implementing.

docs.title: 7. Risks and trade-offs
docs.text:
• Sealed MenuAction churn: every addition to MenuAction is an API event for addons that pattern-match on it. The two new records are additive and the existing sealed-shape test exists precisely to flag this; addons that use exhaustive switch on MenuAction will get an unhandled-arm warning. Acceptable; document in CHANGELOG.md under the next unreleased version.
  • Color-strip correctness: gradient/hex codes have several syntaxes in this codebase (legacy &x, §x, &#rrggbb, and the MiniMessage carry-over). Getting the strip wrong silently breaks highlight projection (highlight appears on the wrong characters). Mitigation: dedicated unit tests for the strip helper covering each syntax, plus a test that feeds a known gradient-wrapped value through ConfigSearchResultsBuilder and asserts the highlight offsets land on the correct raw characters.
  • Very short queries: a 1-char query would match almost everything. Mitigate with a minimum-length guard (proposed: >= 2 chars) backed by menuConfigSearchTooShort locale string. If the user disagrees, drop the guard.
  • Per-world regions.yml duplication: a value present in 10 region overrides will produce 10 hits. Acceptable for v1 (the operator wants to know all the places); revisit if it becomes noisy.
  • No result cap: the user explicitly waived the cap. A pathological config (huge worlds.yml with thousands of override values) could produce a multi-hundred-page book. Acceptable; the book renderer already paginates and the cost is bounded by total config size which is small.

docs.title: 8. Tests
docs.text:
Test module placement (user direction, 2026-05-19): new unit tests for this feature may live in rtp-plugin/src/test/... provisionally until the right canonical home is identified. Rationale: rtp-plugin already has the test infrastructure (LocaleParityTest, ReqRtpF013SpanishLocaleContentTest) and dependencies wired against rtp-core and rtp-api, so new tests can be authored there without spinning up additional test classpaths in lower modules. Once the feature lands and the right module home is clear (likely rtp-core for the builder tests, rtp-api for the sealed-shape bump), tests should be relocated in a follow-up. Until then, do not treat the Eventual module column below as final placement — the landing zone for v1 is rtp-plugin for any test marked (new) unless otherwise noted.

Test Eventual module Land in (v1) What it asserts MenuModelSurfaceTest.menuActionSealedShape (existing, bump) rtp-api rtp-api (in place) Permitted-subclasses set now includes OpenConfigSearchPrompt and OpenConfigSearchResults; size = 15. ConfigSearchResultsBuilderTest (new) rtp-core rtp-plugin Substring match is case-insensitive; matches across keys and values; gradient/hex/& codes do not break matching; offsets project back to the correct raw characters; empty query and too-short query return empty result + correct sentinel. ColorStripTest (new, only if a new helper is introduced per §6 Q1) rtp-core rtp-core (already landed as LegacyColorStripTest) Each color syntax strips to the expected plain text and the offset map round-trips. MenuRedeemSubcommandConfigSearchDispatchTest (new) rtp-core rtp-plugin The two new dispatch arms (a) reject when senderId == null, (b) reject when permission missing, (c) on prompt success mint a token whose redeem produces OpenConfigSearchResults, (d) on results success hand a MenuModel to the renderer with at least one row. LocaleParityTest (existing) rtp-plugin All new MessagesKeys entries present in every shipped locale per AGENTS.md Locale Parity Maintenance. ReqRtpF013SpanishLocaleContentTest (existing, untouched) rtp-plugin Sanity-check Spanish coverage still passes after baseline additions.

docs.title: 9. Locale strings (English baseline values, draft)
docs.text:
Key English baseline menuConfigSearchButton &9Search all configs menuConfigSearchPromptTitle Search configs menuConfigSearchEmpty &7No matches for &f[query]&7. menuConfigSearchResultsHeader &7Results for &f[query]&7 ([count] hits) menuConfigSearchResultRow &7[[file]] [key] = [value] menuConfigSearchTooShort &7Query must be at least 2 characters.

Highlight is applied by the renderer post-format, not encoded in the locale string (so translators don't have to think about color spans). The off-blue color used for the highlight is the existing menu accent color (resolve from the menu theme; do not hardcode a hex).

docs.title: 10. Implementation checklist (post-approval)
docs.text:
• [x] 1. Verify §6 open questions; record answers inline in this proposal before writing code. — done; §6 closing note confirms all 5 questions resolved (Q4 adopts Decision (A)).
  • [x] 2. Add 2 records to MenuAction; bump and update MenuModelSurfaceTest; run that test only. — landed: OpenConfigSearchPrompt + OpenConfigSearchResults(query,page) in rtp-api, sealed-shape bumped 13->15, BookMenuRenderer arms wired, MenuModelSurfaceTest 15/15 PASSED.
  • [x] 3. Implement ColorStrip helper (or reuse) + ColorStripTest. — landed: rtp-core/.../common/text/LegacyColorStrip.java (strip + strip2 with offset map); LegacyColorStripTest 11/11 PASSED.
  • [x] 4. docs.title: PROPOSAL: rtp test network (Shape A) + NetworkTransport composes RTPServerAccessor primitives
docs.text: Status: Proposed, docs-only, awaiting D-005 approval. Author: Junie session 2026-05-18. Scope: two coupled deliverables, see §1.

docs.title: 1. Why two deliverables in one proposal
docs.text:
The user asked for an automated integration test (rtp test network, Shape A "inject synthetic peers into the live binding"). Standing that up surfaced a question about how a test job in rtp-core reaches the live NetworkTransport on the current JVM, when network mode is enabled.

Direct answers (RTP.networkTransport static slot, RTPServerAccessor.networkTransport() getter, etc.) were each rejected by the user. The user's chosen direction is:

"RTPServerAccessor should implement methods that NetworkTransport would rely on instead of NetworkTransport needing multiple implementations" - "if anything is worth doing eventually it's best done immediately here."

That is a larger architectural reframe of the proxy SPI than what "register a new test subcommand" normally implies. Per Rule D-005 (Propose Before Implementation), the two deliverables are bundled into one proposal so the test job is designed against the same SPI shape we land for production use, not against today's shape that is about to change.

Deliverables:

  1. Architectural reframe. NetworkTransport becomes one shared implementation per transport type (in-memory, SQL, future Redis), but stops growing per-platform variants. Platform primitives the transport needs (logger, async executor, server id, current monotonic clock) are pulled from RTPServerAccessor (rtp-api) instead of being baked into the transport class.
  2. rtp test network Shape A. A new platform-agnostic test job in rtp-core that publishes N synthetic BackendHeartbeats through the already-live transport, asserts they appear in the local snapshot, asserts subscriber fan-out fires, and cleans up. Registered in TestCmd base so Bukkit + Fabric both get it.

Both land in one implementing turn, against the new SPI shape from item 1.

docs.title: 2. What is wrong with the current shape
docs.text:
SqlNetworkStateBinding (Phase 2e-SQL, shipped) is ~475 LOC and contains:

  • JDBC plumbing (UPSERT, atomic claim, snapshot SELECT, poll loop).
  • A self-managed ScheduledExecutorService for the 1s poll loop.
  • A self-managed CopyOnWriteArrayList of subscribers.
  • Hand-rolled clock reads (System.currentTimeMillis()).
  • Hand-rolled logging (uses RTP.log via a static accessor).

InMemoryNetworkStateBinding separately implements its own:

  • ConcurrentHashMap-backed snapshot.
  • Its own CopyOnWriteArrayList of subscribers.
  • Its own clock reads.
  • Same logging path.

The two share none of this scaffolding even though it is identical in shape. Adding RedisNetworkStateBinding would duplicate it a third time. Each new platform that wants to host the transport (e.g. eventually Fabric needing its own scheduler hand-off) is forced to either:

  • Subclass / replicate the binding per platform (the current trajectory, explicitly rejected by the user), or
  • Have the binding learn each platform's primitives inline (forbidden by Architecture Boundaries; rtp-proxy-common may not import platform types).

The user's correction is the natural way out: factor the scaffolding into platform primitives exposed on RTPServerAccessor. The transport calls them; the platform supplies them.

docs.title: 3. New primitives on RTPServerAccessor
docs.text:
Additive only. All defaulted to the current single-platform behaviour, so existing platform ServerAccessor implementations remain valid until they opt in.

package io.github.dailystruggle.rtp.api.server;

public interface RTPServerAccessor {

    // ... existing methods (sendMessage, getPlayer, scheduler, log, etc.)

    /**
     * Schedule a periodic task. The transport uses this for its poll loop
     * (SQL) or its TTL reaper (in-memory / Redis). Returns a handle the
     * transport calls to cancel the task on close.
     *
     * Default implementation delegates to the platform's RTPScheduler. Platforms
     * that already expose scheduling (Bukkit, Folia, Paper, Fabric) need not
     * override.
     */
    default RTPScheduledHandle schedulePeriodic(String taskLabel, long initialDelayMs,
                                                long periodMs, Runnable task) {
        // default delegates to RTP.scheduler (rtp-api already references it
        // via the existing RTPScheduler abstraction).
        return DefaultSchedulingBridge.schedulePeriodic(this, taskLabel,
                initialDelayMs, periodMs, task);
    }

    /**
     * Monotonic millisecond clock. Defaulted to System.currentTimeMillis().
     * Overridable for deterministic tests (an existing rtp-api convention -
     * MetricsBinding already uses Clock injection).
     */
    default long currentTimeMillis() {
        return System.currentTimeMillis();
    }

    /**
     * Stable identifier for this physical server within the network. Sourced
     * from network.yml network.serverId. Returns null when network mode is
     * disabled.
     */
    default String networkServerId() {
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Log routed through the platform's logger. Existing rtp-api convention
     * already exposes log(Level, String, Throwable); this primitive is named
     * for clarity from inside transport code.
     */
    default void networkLog(java.util.logging.Level lvl, String msg, Throwable t) {
        log(lvl, msg, t); // default to existing log() method
    }
}

RTPScheduledHandle is a tiny new rtp-api interface:

public interface RTPScheduledHandle extends AutoCloseable {
    boolean isCancelled();
    @Override void close(); // idempotent cancel
}

That is the full additive surface on RTPServerAccessor. No proxy-shaped types leak into rtp-api. No new static slots.

docs.title: 4. NetworkTransport after the refactor
docs.text:
The interface stays the same (existing public methods retained). What changes is the abstract base class that bindings extend.

package io.github.dailystruggle.rtp.proxy.common.spi;

public abstract class AbstractNetworkTransport implements NetworkTransport {

    protected final RTPServerAccessor host;
    protected final List<Consumer<BackendHeartbeat>> backendSinks =
            new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
    protected final List<Consumer<ProxyHeartbeat>> proxySinks =
            new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
    protected volatile RTPScheduledHandle pollHandle;

    protected AbstractNetworkTransport(RTPServerAccessor host) { this.host = host; }

    // Shared poll-loop scaffolding. Bindings override doPollOnce() with the
    // transport-specific read (JDBC SELECT for SQL; ConcurrentHashMap copy for
    // in-memory; Redis SCAN for future Redis).
    protected final void startPolling(String label, long intervalMs) {
        pollHandle = host.schedulePeriodic(label, intervalMs, intervalMs, () -> {
            try { doPollOnce(); }
            catch (Throwable t) {
                host.networkLog(Level.WARNING, label + " poll failed: " + t, t);
            }
        });
    }

    protected abstract void doPollOnce();

    // Shared subscriber-fanout. Bindings just call fanOutBackend(row) once
    // they have determined a heartbeat is new / changed.
    protected final void fanOutBackend(BackendHeartbeat row) {
        for (Consumer<BackendHeartbeat> s : backendSinks) {
            try { s.accept(row); }
            catch (Throwable t) { host.networkLog(Level.WARNING, "backend sink threw", t); }
        }
    }
    protected final void fanOutProxy(ProxyHeartbeat row) { /* mirror */ }

    @Override
    public final Subscription subscribeBackendHeartbeats(Consumer<BackendHeartbeat> sink) {
        backendSinks.add(sink);
        return () -> backendSinks.remove(sink);
    }

    @Override
    public void close() {
        if (pollHandle != null) pollHandle.close();
        backendSinks.clear();
        proxySinks.clear();
    }
}

After the refactor:

  • InMemoryNetworkStateBinding extends AbstractNetworkTransport - drops its own subscriber list, its own clock reads, its own scheduling. Shrinks from ~150 LOC to ~80.
  • SqlNetworkStateBinding extends AbstractNetworkTransport - drops its own poll loop, its own subscriber list, its own clock reads. Shrinks from ~475 LOC to ~320.
  • Future RedisNetworkStateBinding plugs straight into the same scaffolding; ~250 LOC instead of starting from scratch.
  • No per-platform subclass. Each transport type is one class, period.

AbstractNetworkTransport lives in rtp-proxy-common. It depends on RTPServerAccessor from rtp-api, which is already the case (rtp-proxy-common -> rtp-api).

docs.title: 5. How the test job reaches the live transport
docs.text:
The refactor does not, by itself, solve "how does NetworkSimulationTestJob in rtp-core find the live transport on this JVM?". Two cheap options remain; neither is RTP.networkTransport and neither is RTPServerAccessor.networkTransport().

Both options are platform-agnostic. Pick one:

docs.title: Option P (recommended). Bridge through the existing D3 slot.
docs.text:
AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor.setNetworkStateBinding(...) is already called by NetworkModeBootstrap.boot() (Phase 2e-SQL slice, line 104). The slot today holds a SqlBindingAdapter whose transport() accessor is package-private.

Action:

  • Promote the NetworkStateBinding interface (rtp-core) to expose a default NetworkTransport transport() { return null; } method.
  • SqlBindingAdapter.transport() becomes the override.
  • InMemoryNetworkStateBinding does NOT implement NetworkStateBinding - but the in-memory case in NetworkModeBootstrap wraps it in a tiny InMemoryBindingAdapter implements NetworkStateBinding the same way SQL does.
  • Test job: RTP.serverAccessor.databaseAccessor() instanceof AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor sql -> sql.getNetworkStateBinding() -> transport(). Any null link = skip with NOT-CONFIGURED.

Pro: no new types in rtp-api. Pro: Fabric route is the same code path - NetworkStateBinding is already in rtp-core. Con: leaks NetworkTransport type onto NetworkStateBinding (was opaque marker). But: rtp-core already has an api dep on rtp-proxy-common since the Phase 2e-SQL turn, so the import is mechanical, not architectural.

docs.title: Option Q. Visitor on RTPServerAccessor.
docs.text:
RTPServerAccessor gains default <T> T queryNetworkPrimitive(Class<T> kind) { return null; }. Platform ServerAccessor impls override to return the live transport when asked for NetworkTransport.class. Generic, future-proof for other "what platform has X" queries, but more ceremony for the single use site we have today.

Recommendation: P, with Q kept as a fallback if it turns out Fabric needs a different lookup path.

docs.title: 6.1 Placement
docs.text:
rtp-core/src/main/java/io/github/dailystruggle/rtp/common/commands/test/NetworkSimulationTestJob.java.

Registered in the TestCmd base class (not BukkitTestCmd), so the subcommand rtp test network is available on every platform that ships rtp test.

docs.title: 6.2 Command shape
docs.text:
/rtp test network            (default: simulate 3 peers, 5s observation window)
/rtp test network <N>        (override peer count, clamped 1..16)
/rtp test network <N> <ms>   (override observation-window ms, clamped 250..30_000)

Permission: rtp.test (mirrors siblings).

docs.title: 6.3 Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Resolve transport. Reach the live transport via Option P (§5). If null, emit network: NOT-CONFIGURED and return PASS-with-skip (consistent with REQ-RTP-NET-002 - disabled mode means the test is not applicable, not failed).
  2. Register with ActiveTestJobs. Mirrors EconomyIsolationTestJob pattern so rtp test full blocks on us if invoked from the umbrella.
  3. Deterministic synthetic peers. Seed = callerId.getMostSignificantBits() ^ jobId.hashCode(). Generate N BackendHeartbeats with synthesised UUIDs UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(("rtp-sim-" + seed + "-" + i).getBytes(UTF_8)), pluginState=READY, randomised TPS (16..20), MSPT (10..40), load (0..0.8).
  4. Subscribe to the transport. Capture a thread-safe set of UUIDs the subscriber observes (used in step 7).
  5. Publish. Call transport.publishBackendHeartbeat(row) for each synthetic peer. Await all futures with a 2s aggregate timeout (PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, mirroring EconomyIsolationTestJob).
  6. Wait one observation window. Default 5s. Lets the poll loop on SQL bindings pick up the rows; in-memory bindings fan out synchronously on publish so this window is a forgiving cushion, not a requirement.
  7. Assert.
  8. Local transport.readSnapshot() contains all N synthetic UUIDs.
  9. The subscriber observed exactly N fan-out events for those UUIDs (or >= N if the binding republishes on poll, with the SQL-side caveat called out below).
  10. WeightedAverageBackendSelector.select(snapshot, deterministicSeed) produces the same winner across three repeated calls (REQ-RTP-NET-013).
  11. Cleanup. Always - normal exit, exception, or command-source disconnect. Publish a "leave" heartbeat for each synthetic UUID (pluginState=STOPPING) AND immediately call transport.publishBackendHeartbeat(row) with the row's lastHeartbeatAt set to 0 / a far-past value so the binding's TTL reaper drops it within the next poll cycle. For SQL specifically, also issue a direct DELETE on the synthetic UUIDs through the same RTPServerAccessor primitive (added in §3 if not already present, but ideally NOT - cleanup should ride the existing transport API; see open question Q1).
  12. Audit. Emit one network: PASS / FAIL <reason> / NOT-CONFIGURED line via SendMessage, so rtp test full's FullAudit captures the row.

docs.title: 6.4 What it does NOT do
docs.text:
• Does not test HMAC reject paths (Phase 4 / ADR-010 territory).
  • Does not test multi-JVM agreement (requires real devstack).
  • Does not test churn or partition (Shape B territory).
  • Does not test reservation-token claim races (single-JVM only - both claimants are the same transport instance, so the race is trivial).

These are deliberately deferred per the original Shape A scope.

docs.title: 6.5 REQ-RTP-NET-002 parity
docs.text: Disabled mode must be byte-identical no-op. Test job preconditions check RTP.serverAccessor.networkServerId() == null (§3 primitive); if null, do not touch the transport at all, do not subscribe, do not allocate a ScheduledExecutor. Emit NOT-CONFIGURED and return.

docs.title: 7. Implementing turn worklist (after this proposal is approved)
docs.text:
1. rtp-api: add RTPScheduledHandle, the four default methods on RTPServerAccessor (§3). DefaultSchedulingBridge helper in rtp-api or rtp-core depending on dep direction.
  2. rtp-proxy-common: introduce AbstractNetworkTransport; refactor InMemoryNetworkStateBinding and SqlNetworkStateBinding to extend it; delete duplicated scaffolding. Update tests (existing 6+3 should still pass without semantic changes; if they don't, that is a bug in the refactor, not the tests).
  3. rtp-core: amend NetworkStateBinding to expose default NetworkTransport transport() { return null; }. Add InMemoryBindingAdapter for symmetry with SqlBindingAdapter.
  4. rtp-plugin: NetworkModeBootstrap populates the D3 slot for both SQL and in-memory paths.
  5. Each platform ServerAccessor (Bukkit, Folia, Paper, Fabric): override networkServerId() to return the value pulled from NetworkModeBootstrap (or null on Fabric until network bootstrap lands there). No other overrides required; defaults cover the rest.
  6. rtp-core: write NetworkSimulationTestJob per §6. Register in TestCmd base.
  7. TRACEABILITY.md: row for the new REQ (proposed: REQ-RTP-NET-015 - Simulated Peer Diagnostic).
  8. MULTI_SERVER_PLAN.md: tick H3 ("rtp test full network aggregator") partially (single-JVM half landed; cross-process half deferred to Phase 2f). Add Shape A landing callout.
  9. LESSONS_LEARNED.md: row explaining what Shape A does NOT cover so operators don't get false confidence.
  10. Tests: NetworkSimulationTestJob unit test using InMemoryNetworkStateBinding; refactor regression tests for the two existing bindings.
  11. Full gradlew build.

Estimated LOC: ~500 LOC code (mostly refactor; net new is ~200 LOC for the test job + ~80 LOC for the rtp-api primitives + ~50 LOC for the D3-slot plumbing). ~250 LOC of test code.

docs.title: Q1. Synthetic peer cleanup primitive.
docs.text:
Step 6.3.8 wants the test to be able to delete a row immediately, not wait for TTL. Options:

  • (a) Extend NetworkTransport with removeBackendHeartbeat(UUID). Cleanest. Every binding can implement it trivially.
  • (b) Publish a STOPPING-state heartbeat and let the binding's reaper drop it on the next poll. Lower API surface but means the test sleeps one poll interval during cleanup.

Default recommendation: (a). Symmetric with existing publish/snapshot surface, cleaner test exit, useful beyond this test job (admin tooling for evicting ghost backends).

docs.title: Q2. Should the test job run on the in-memory binding at all?
docs.text:
If transport.type: in-memory on a single JVM, the test is essentially a self-check (no real cross-process state to assert against). Still useful as a smoke test (proves the transport plumbing, subscribe/fan-out, selector determinism) but easy to misread as a multi-server-readiness check.

Default recommendation: run unconditionally; emit a NETWORK: PASS (in-memory; single-JVM only) suffix in the audit row to make the limitation explicit.

docs.title: Q3. Scheduling-bridge dep direction.
docs.text:
DefaultSchedulingBridge (§3) needs to call RTP.scheduler. RTP is in rtp-core. RTPServerAccessor is in rtp-api. If the bridge lives in rtp-api, it cannot reach RTP.scheduler. If it lives in rtp-core, then the default method on RTPServerAccessor calls into rtp-core - which rtp-api also cannot do.

Resolution: the default method delegates to an existing rtp-api primitive (RTPScheduler is already in rtp-api per the existing scheduling abstraction; RTPServerAccessor already has access to one via the existing scheduler() or equivalent). Verify during implementation; if not, the cleaner fix is for each platform's concrete ServerAccessor to override schedulePeriodic directly.

docs.title: Q4. Is RTPServerAccessor the right home for networkServerId()?
docs.text:
It is tied to network mode, not the server-platform abstraction. An argument exists for putting it on a separate RTPNetworkAccessor interface in rtp-api. Counter-argument: it is fundamentally "what is this server's identity in the network" which is server-shaped data, and putting it on RTPServerAccessor keeps the platform-abstraction surface unified.

Default recommendation: leave it on RTPServerAccessor with a clear Javadoc that it returns null when network mode is disabled. Re-home later if a richer RTPNetworkAccessor surface emerges.

docs.title: Q5. Refactor scope: now vs. incrementally.
docs.text:
The proposal lands the refactor and the test job in the same turn (~500 LOC code change + tests). An alternative is to land Shape A first using Option P (D3 slot + transport accessor) against today's binding shape, then do the AbstractNetworkTransport refactor as a follow-up turn.

Default recommendation: per user direction ("worth doing eventually is best done immediately here"), land both in one turn.

docs.title: 9. What this proposal explicitly does NOT change
docs.text:
• network.yml schema (ADR-002 stable).
  • NetworkConfig SPI in rtp-proxy-common.
  • ReservationToken SPI (ADR-005 already Accepted).
  • BackendSelector / WeightedAverageBackendSelector (the test uses them read-only).
  • The Phase 2e-SQL slice's external behaviour - bindings continue to produce the same SQL DDL, same UPSERT semantics, same atomic-claim contract. Only the internal scaffolding moves.
  • ADR statuses. rtp-proxy-ADR-005, -010, -011 all remain as-is.
  • Velocity-side wiring. rtp-proxy-velocity does not need changes; the Velocity adapter already constructs its transport via NetworkBindings.open().

docs.title: 10. Decision needed
docs.text:
• Approve §3 primitives (schedulePeriodic, currentTimeMillis, networkServerId, networkLog) on RTPServerAccessor. Override or add others.
  • Approve §4 AbstractNetworkTransport shape. Or push back if you'd rather keep each binding standalone.
  • Approve §5 Option P (D3-slot bridge with promoted transport() accessor on NetworkStateBinding). Or pick Q.
  • Approve §6 NetworkSimulationTestJob design.
  • Answer Q1-Q5 in §8 (defaults documented; saying "all defaults" is fine).

Once approved, the implementing turn is one D-005-compliant pass covering §7's 11 steps, ending with a full multi-module build.

InfoCmd (rtp-core) Add a verbose path (gated on a new /rtp info verbose argument or -v flag) that, when MetricsSnapshot.foliaRegions() is non-empty, renders the per-region table behind a new MessagesKeys.infoHealthCacheFoliaRegionRow template. Non-Folia platforms render nothing extra — existing behaviour preserved. RTPCostMetricsCharts (already landed) Add the Phase M2 Runtime health chart group: region_count, cache_pool_health, tps_buckets, mspt_buckets, pipeline_latency_buckets, memory_tracker_pressure, chunk_load_backlog_pressure, s005_violations_recent. Bucketisation runs once per Metrics.snapshot() and is cached for the chart fetch tick.

docs.title: 1.6 Cross-platform metrics consolidation (parity, added 2026-05-17)
docs.text:
User direction: "if we organize metrics we should organize metrics." The M1 bindings cover the MetricsSnapshot surface on every platform, but several metric-shaped reads still bypass the binding. Section C is the right moment to consolidate so all four platforms (Paper / Bukkit / Folia / Fabric) read every metric through the same boundary.

Audit findings (2026-05-17):

  • TPS: three independent readers. MetricsBinding#tps*m (real, per-platform sampled), RTPServerAccessor#getTPS(int) (Folia returns a hard-coded constant at AbstractFoliaServerAccessor.java:468; Fabric returns nominal 20.0 at FabricServerAccessor.java:1673 pending MULTI_PLATFORM_PLAN.md > Step C), and a redundant reflective probe in RTPCostMetricsCharts#register line 358.
  • Player count: five readers across PaperMetricsBinding:126, BukkitTpsSampler:104, RTPBukkitPlugin#onEnable:275, AbstractServerAccessor:365, AbstractFoliaServerAccessor:297. The latter two are legitimate iterator reads (need Player instances); the first three are size-only reads.
  • Soft cap / max players: four readers across PaperMetricsBinding:136, BukkitTpsSampler:114, RTPBukkitPlugin:249, FabricEventBridge:477-484 (reflective getMaxPlayers / intermediary method_3802). Folia inherits AbstractServerAccessor.
  • Heap: already consolidated via HeapSampler in rtp-core. No work.
  • MSPT: no outside-the-binding reader exists. No work.

Sub-proposal:

  • 1.6.1 Route RTPServerAccessor#getTPS(int) through Metrics.snapshot(). Per-platform getTPS(int) implementations (AbstractServerAccessor, AbstractFoliaServerAccessor, FabricServerAccessor) delegate to RTP.metrics.snapshot().tps*m when the binding is non-NOOP; keep the existing body as a fallback when Metrics.NOOP is active (e.g. pre-onEnable callers). Closes the throttle-vs-metrics divergence: rtp-core/.../tasks/TPS.java and MetricsSnapshot will now read the same value on every platform.
  • 1.6.2 Replace size-only player-count read at RTPBukkitPlugin.java:275 with RTP.metrics.snapshot().playerCount. Iterator reads at AbstractServerAccessor:365 and AbstractFoliaServerAccessor:297 stay (they need Player instances). One-line edit; snapshot field already exists.
  • 1.6.3 Reconcile soft-cap reads. Replace Bukkit.getMaxPlayers() fallback at RTPBukkitPlugin.java:249 with RTP.metrics.snapshot().softCap. Pull the reflective MinecraftServer.getMaxPlayers() block at FabricEventBridge.java:477-484 into FabricMetricsBinding#softCap() so the reflective probe lives at the binding boundary, not in event-bridge code. Login-reserve cache initialisation (the consumer in both sites) reads the snapshot.
  • 1.6.4 Delete redundant reflective getTPS() fallback at RTPCostMetricsCharts#register line 358. The MetricsBindingDispatcher.install() call site (B9) runs before bStats submission; the fallback is dead code now that PaperMetricsBinding is provably installed when the chart fetches.
  • 1.6.5 ArchUnit drift guard. Forbid the following raw calls outside the listed allow-list, in modules rtp-core + rtp-bukkit + rtp-paper + rtp-folia + rtp-fabric + rtp-plugin:
  • Bukkit.getOnlinePlayers().size() - allowed only inside *MetricsBinding, *TpsSampler.
  • Bukkit.getMaxPlayers() / Server#getMaxPlayers() - allowed only inside *MetricsBinding, *TpsSampler.
  • Bukkit.getServer().getTPS() / Server#getTPS() - allowed only inside *MetricsBinding; RTPCostMetricsCharts is removed from this list once 1.6.4 lands.
  • MinecraftServer.getMaxPlayers() reflective probe - allowed only inside FabricMetricsBinding.
  • Iterator reads (for (Player p : Bukkit.getOnlinePlayers())) are out of scope for the guard; they are a legitimate access pattern.
  • Exempt modules: helpers/ (test harness), commands-api/ (tab-complete reads via OnlinePlayerParameter are intentional), addons/ (third-party scope).

Tests for 1.6:

  • RTPServerAccessorTpsParityTest (new, in rtp-core test fixtures or rtp-plugin): synthetic non-NOOP binding produces a TPS value T; RTPServerAccessor#getTPS(1) returns T (not the platform fallback constant). Fallback path covered separately with Metrics.NOOP installed.
  • MetricsConsolidationArchTest (new ArchUnit test in rtp-core's arch-guard suite): asserts 1.6.5 allow-list rules.
  • No new REQ-* row needed - these are implementation rearrangements under the existing REQ-RTP-OBS-001/002/003 contracts.

docs.title: 1.7 Docs / traceability
docs.text:
• docs/dev/TRACEABILITY.md — rows for new tests under REQ-RTP-OBS-001 (snapshot non-blocking) and REQ-RTP-OBS-003 (bounded sampler cost). No new REQ ID needed — Folia/Fabric are platform implementations of the obs-001/002/003 contracts.
  • docs/dev/METRICS_PLAN.md > Phase M2 — tick C1/C2/C3/C4 items.
  • CHECKLIST-metrics-and-multiserver.md — tick C1–C5 as each lands.

docs.title: 2.1 MetricsSnapshot constructor — additive, single migration
docs.text:
Before (current, 15 args): 

new MetricsSnapshot(tps1m, tps5m, tps15m, mspt, playerCount, softCap,
    heapUsed, heapMax, queueDepth, pendingTeleports, memoryTrackerEntries,
    chunkLoadBacklog, avgPipelineMs, databaseLatencyMs, takenAtEpochMs);

After (16 args, append-only): 

new MetricsSnapshot(tps1m, tps5m, tps15m, mspt, playerCount, softCap,
    heapUsed, heapMax, queueDepth, pendingTeleports, memoryTrackerEntries,
    chunkLoadBacklog, avgPipelineMs, databaseLatencyMs, takenAtEpochMs,
    foliaRegions);

Per the A5 D-005 ratification: "Later phases extend via additive constructor changes contained to the single binding constructor." Single call site (CoreMetrics.snapshot()) updates; all reflection-free downstream consumers (InfoCmd, TestFullCmd, RTPCostMetricsCharts, tests) read the new field through the accessor and tolerate emptyList().

docs.title: 2.2 Push-binding lifecycle (unchanged from B6/B9)
docs.text:
server start →
  MetricsBindingDispatcher.install():
    if Folia detected   → CoreMetrics.setBinding(new FoliaMetricsBinding(...))
    elif Paper detected → CoreMetrics.setBinding(new PaperMetricsBinding())
    else                → CoreMetrics.setBinding(new BukkitTpsSampler(...))
server stop →
  MetricsBindingDispatcher.uninstall() → CoreMetrics.setBinding(MetricsBinding.NOOP)

Fabric uses its own bootstrap path (no Bukkit.*), invoking CoreMetrics.setBinding(new FabricMetricsBinding(...)) from the mod entry point. No interface change required.

docs.title: 2.3 MetricsKeys shape (mirrors EconomyKeys precedent)
docs.text:
# metrics.yml (auto-generated defaults)
foliaIncludeRegions: true        # A4-resolved; per-region detail in MetricsSnapshot.foliaRegions()
foliaAggregationTps: mean        # mean | max
foliaAggregationMspt: max        # mean | max
foliaAggregationTickBudget: max  # mean | max
version: "1.0"

docs.title: 3. Open questions for D-005 approval
docs.text:
1. Constructor breakage tolerance. The current MetricsSnapshot ctor is called from CoreMetrics, PaperMetricsBinding test fixtures, and MetricsSnapshotTest. Adding a 16th arg breaks all of them at compile time. Two options:
  2. (a) Append the 16th param; fix the 3 call sites. Single atomic commit. Recommended.

  3. (b) Add an overload MetricsSnapshot(... 15 args ...) that delegates with Collections.emptyList(). Avoids touching tests but locks a second public constructor signature. Default chosen unless overridden: (a).

  4. Shared TPS EMA helper. Folia per-region sampler and Fabric sampler both want the EMA math already present in BukkitTpsSampler. Two options:

  5. (a) Extract TpsEmaSampler into rtp-core/.../metrics/ (no platform imports — it's pure math). Recommended.

  6. (b) Duplicate the math per platform. Default chosen unless overridden: (a), with BukkitTpsSampler refactored to delegate (still trivial; existing tests stay green).

  7. /rtp info verbose invocation surface. Two options:

  8. (a) New subcommand verbose (/rtp info verbose) — Brigadier-friendly, tab-completable.

  9. (b) New flag -v parsed inside InfoCmd — terser but inconsistent with the rest of the command surface. Default chosen unless overridden: (a).

  10. FoliaRegionSample.regionId stability. Per METRICS_PLAN.md > regionQueueStatus redaction in network mode, region ids should be "stable opaque ids (region-0, region-1, …) assigned at startup, never crosses the wire as the human name." I'll mint ids from a per-FoliaMetricsBinding AtomicInteger keyed off the Folia RegionKey. Confirm this is acceptable for the M2 console / /rtp info verbose audience (the network-mode redaction concern is M3 and downstream).

  11. C4 chart-group landing reconciliation. The B-section closing note in the checklist says RTPCostMetricsCharts runtime-cost charts already landed ahead of the gate. Confirm the M2 Runtime health chart group is additive (new chart IDs in BStatsChartIds, new helper methods), not a rewrite of the cost charts.

docs.title: 4. Relevant REQs / ADRs
docs.text:
• REQ-RTP-OBS-001 / 002 / 003 (REQUIREMENTS.md §1.8) — non-blocking snapshot, single-sample pipeline recording, bounded sampler cost. C1/C2 must respect all three on every platform.
  • REQ-RTP-F-013 — all user-facing messages configurable. The new MessagesKeys.infoHealthCacheFoliaRegionRow row template must ship EN+ES defaults and survive LocaleResourceParityTest.
  • REQ-RTP-S-005 — no main-thread chunk I/O. Folia binding's per-region sampler runs on the region scheduler (already region-owned); no chunk access required.
  • ADR-032 — pipeline histogram never-resets. Unaffected (C-section doesn't touch the histogram).
  • AGENTS.md > Architecture Boundaries — MetricsKeys and FoliaRegionSample land in rtp-core (no platform imports); FoliaMetricsBinding lands in rtp-folia-common (platform-specific); ArchUnit guard continues to pass.
  • METRICS_PLAN.md > Folia Aggregation — max for mspt/tickBudget, mean for tps*. Operator-overridable via metrics.folia.aggregation.*.
  • METRICS_PLAN.md > Module Placement — module destinations match exactly.

docs.title: 5. Risks and trade-offs
docs.text:
• Risk: per-region sampler count on extreme-region-count Folia deployments. Mitigation: foliaIncludeRegions: false flips off the per-region rendering (A4 carve-out); the aggregation itself remains O(regions) per snapshot read, which is acceptable at the documented 1Hz snapshot cadence.
  • Risk: Folia API surface drift across MC versions (1.20.x / 1.21.x / 26.x). Mitigation: the platform-specific scheduling lives in rtp-folia-common only, behind the existing Folia version-shim modules (rtp-folia-v1_20_R1, rtp-folia-v1_21_R1, rtp-folia-v26_1_R1). If a per-version shim is needed for RegionScheduler.runAtFixedRate signature changes, it lands in the per-version module.
  • Risk: Fabric tick-callback wiring not yet ratified. Per MULTI_PLATFORM_PLAN.md > Step E2. If E2 lands after C2, C2 ships as a stub returning UNSAMPLED sentinels and is finalised when E2 is approved. The interface/binding registration stays correct.
  • Trade-off: separate metrics.yml vs. folding into performance.yml. Chose separate file: keeps reporting knobs (metrics.*) cleanly separated from throttle/tuning knobs (performance.*). One-time /rtp reload cost on first launch (file generation) is negligible.
  • No ADR supersession. No existing ADR contradicted; no superseding ADR required.

docs.title: 6. Out of scope (deferred or already done)
docs.text:
• Real-time per-tick CPU budget (tickCpuBudgetMsAnalytical, tickCpuMsP99, tickCpuMsP999, tickCpuOvershoots) — deferred per METRICS_PLAN.md Phase M2 last bullet, gated on a dedicated ADR not yet drafted.
  • /rtp info json — deferred to a follow-up; verbose human-readable rendering is enough for the M2 gate.
  • Multi-server network telemetry consumers — Phase M3, not Section C.
  • RTPCostMetricsCharts runtime-cost group — already landed ahead of the gate per the B-section closing note; C4 only adds the Runtime health group beside it.

docs.title: 7. Verification gate (matches checklist row C "Gate")
docs.text:
dual-runtime smoke test — one JAR loads on Paper and Fabric, /rtp info verbose prints sane health on both. Coordinates with MULTI_PLATFORM_PLAN.md > Phase 2 acceptance gate.

Per-row verification commands:

  • C1: .\gradlew :rtp-folia:rtp-folia-common:test --tests "*FoliaMetricsBinding*" green; MetricsSnapshot.foliaRegions() populated on a Folia devstack; metrics.folia.includeRegions: false empties the list without breaking the snapshot.
  • C2: .\gradlew :rtp-fabric:rtp-fabric-common:test --tests "*FabricMetricsBinding*" green; Fabric dev-server /rtp info shows non-zero TPS.
  • C3: .\gradlew :rtp-core:test --tests "*InfoCmd*" green; new test asserts the per-region rows are emitted exactly when verbose is the trailing arg and foliaRegions() is non-empty.
  • C4: new BStatsChartIdsTest rows confirming the Runtime health chart IDs are present, non-fingerprinting (UUID/IPv4/hostname regex still clean), and that bucketisation runs exactly once per snapshot fetch.
  • C5: .\check_traceability.sh clean.
  • Section gate: .\gradlew build green (the Final Full Build rule); dual-runtime smoke transcript captured in the checklist's section-C gate note.

docs.title: 8. Implementation order (once approved)
docs.text:
1. SPI change first (lowest risk, highest blast radius): FoliaRegionSample + MetricsSnapshot 16-arg ctor + MetricsBinding.foliaRegions() default + CoreMetrics wire-up. Update MetricsSnapshotTest / CoreMetricsTest / PaperMetricsBindingTest for the new arg. Run :rtp-core:test.
  2. MetricsKeys + metrics.yml registration in Configs. Run :rtp-core:test.
  3. (Optional from §3 Q2): extract TpsEmaSampler shared helper; refactor BukkitTpsSampler to delegate; re-run its 7 tests.
  4. FoliaMetricsBinding + FoliaRegionTpsSampler + test. Run :rtp-folia:rtp-folia-common:test.
  5. FabricMetricsBinding + test (stub if E2 not yet ratified). Run :rtp-fabric:rtp-fabric-common:test.
  6. MetricsBindingDispatcher Folia branch + fabric-bootstrap call. Run :rtp-plugin:test --tests "*MetricsBindingDispatcher*".
  7. Cross-platform consolidation (§1.6). Apply 1.6.1 → 1.6.4 in order; land MetricsConsolidationArchTest (1.6.5) last so the guard catches any residual stray reads. Run :rtp-core:test, :rtp-paper:rtp-paper-common:test, :rtp-folia:rtp-folia-common:test, :rtp-fabric:rtp-fabric-common:test, :rtp-plugin:test.
  8. InfoCmd verbose path + EN/ES message templates + InfoCmdTest row. Run :rtp-core:test --tests "*InfoCmd*".
  9. RTPCostMetricsCharts Runtime health additions + BStatsChartIds constants + anti-fingerprinting test rows.
  10. TRACEABILITY.md rows + METRICS_PLAN.md Phase M2 boxes + checklist C1–C5 ticks (plus a new C6 row capturing §1.6 — see C-section checklist amendment below).
  11. .\gradlew build (Final Full Build gate).

Approval status (2026-05-17): §1.6 Cross-platform metrics consolidation approved in-session ("go") with ArchUnit guard scope confirmed: rtp-core + rtp-bukkit + rtp-paper + rtp-folia + rtp-fabric + rtp-plugin in scope; helpers/, commands-api/, addons/ exempt. §1.1–§1.5 and §3 open questions still awaiting explicit approval before code lands; defaults (constructor option (a), TpsEmaSampler extraction option (a), /rtp info verbose subcommand option (a), opaque region-N ids, additive C4 chart group) stand unless overridden.

docs.title: Proposal: Source RTP runtime metrics from spark when present (D-005)
docs.text: Status: APPROVED + IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-12). Decisions: per-field merge (Q1), keep Folia native (Q2), CPU/GC out of scope (Q3). Shipped as SparkMetricsBinding + ReflectiveSparkStats (rtp-bukkit-common), wired via MetricsBindingDispatcher#wrapWithSparkIfPresent, softdepend: [spark], and an EXTERNAL_HOOKS row.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
When the spark plugin (me.lucko:spark) is installed on a Bukkit-family backend, prefer spark's measured statistics for the metric fields RTP surfaces in /rtp info / CoreMetrics, instead of the coarser native server calls. spark exposes richer, cross-platform-consistent data (TPS windows, MSPT mean/percentiles, CPU, GC) than Server#getTPS() / Server#getAverageTickTime().

This is a true soft-dependency: zero behavioral change when spark is absent.

docs.title: 2. Affected classes / modules
docs.text:
• platforms/rtp-bukkit/rtp-bukkit-common — NEW SparkMetricsBinding (implements metrics-api/MetricsBinding), accessing spark reflectively.
  • rtp-plugin — bukkit/metrics/MetricsBindingDispatcher gains a spark probe
  • install branch, chosen ahead of the Folia/Paper/Spigot bindings when spark is present.
  • docs/dev/EXTERNAL_HOOKS.md — new catalog row + RTPHooks entry (ADR-026).
  • rtp-plugin plugin.yml — add softdepend: [spark] (load-order only; see section 3a). Does NOT make spark mandatory.
  • Tests: SparkMetricsBindingTest (test-seam supplier ctor, like PaperMetricsBinding) + a dispatcher selection test.

No change to rtp-core / rtp-api. Fabric/NeoForge unaffected (spark's Bukkit API is Bukkit-family only).

docs.title: 3. Before / after structure
docs.text:
Before: MetricsBindingDispatcher.install() selects Folia -> Paper -> Spigot sampler, each reading native server values.

After: install() first probes for spark; if present and SparkProvider.get() succeeds, installs SparkMetricsBinding. Otherwise unchanged.

Field mapping (proposed): - tps1m/5m/15m() <- spark tps() DoubleStatistic windows. - mspt() <- spark mspt() mean (GenericStatistic last-1m mean). - playerCount() / softCap() <- still native (Bukkit), spark does not own these. - chunkLoadBacklog() / databaseLatencyMs() <- unchanged, folded by CoreMetrics. - foliaRegions() <- inherited empty (Folia per-region detail stays with FoliaMetricsBinding; see open question Q2).

Access strategy: reflection against me.lucko.spark.api.* (no compile dep), mirroring the presence-detection pattern already in SparkHook. All getters non-blocking; return documented sentinels (UNSAMPLED / 0 / -1) on any Throwable or before spark has sampled.

docs.title: 3a. Soft-dependency + disabled state (two complementary mechanisms)
docs.text:
These do different jobs and both belong in the design:

  • softdepend: [spark] in plugin.yml — constrains LOAD ORDER only: if spark is installed it is enabled before RTP, so SparkProvider.get() is ready when the binding first queries it. If spark is absent, no effect and no hard requirement. This is the sole purpose of a softdepend, and it removes the "present but not yet initialized" transient window at enable time. Caveat: softdepend only orders plugins present at load time; a later hot-load of spark is not ordered for that session, which is why the sentinel fallback below still earns its keep.
  • ClassNotFoundException / NoClassDefFoundError catch — handles the ABSENT case at class-linkage level (and trimmed/lite-jar classpaths). Probe once at construction; on linkage failure set a permanent enabled = false and never touch spark again (every getter then returns its sentinel). NoClassDefFoundError must be caught alongside the checked exception because a partial classpath surfaces as an Error.

Two disabled states: 1. Permanent (spark/API absent): enabled = false, always sentinel. The dispatcher's existing tryInstallBinding already swallows ClassNotFoundException | NoClassDefFoundError and falls through to the native binding, so this composes cleanly. 2. Transient (spark present but not yet sampling, or SparkProvider.get() throws IllegalStateException): per-getter catch (Throwable) returns the sentinel, self-healing once spark warms up. Never throw on the calling thread (binding contract).

docs.title: 4. Relevant requirements / ADRs
docs.text:
• Metrics SPI: metrics-api-ADR-001; METRICS_PLAN.md.
  • External hook contract: ADR-026 (EXTERNAL_HOOKS.md + RTPHooks).
  • S-006: API entry points throw, but a best-effort observability binding degrades to sentinels (consistent with existing dispatcher's graceful-degrade policy).

docs.title: 5. Risks / trade-offs
docs.text:
• spark API surface differs across spark versions; reflection must tolerate missing methods (degrade to sentinel) rather than hard-fail.
  • Folia: spark coexists with FoliaMetricsBinding's per-region sampling. Picking spark would drop foliaRegions() detail (Q2). Likely keep Folia on its native binding and only prefer spark on Paper/Spigot.
  • New reflective hook = new EXTERNAL_HOOKS maintenance surface.

docs.title: 6. Open questions for maintainer
docs.text:
• Q1: prefer-spark-when-present, or per-field merge (spark TPS/MSPT + native player/cap)? Per-field merge is recommended.
  • Q2: on Folia, keep FoliaMetricsBinding (per-region) and ignore spark, or compose? Recommend keep native on Folia for now.
  • Q3: expose spark-only CPU/GC? Requires additive MetricsBinding/MetricsSnapshot fields — out of scope unless requested (separate decision).

docs.title: PROPOSAL - SQL-First Network Binding (Phase 2b reframe; Redis becomes Phase 2e optimisation; proxy-as-participant is the default role)
docs.text: Status: Draft (design-only; no code in scope) Date: 2026-05-18 (rev 2 - participant default re-elevated per user direction "we designed both options to toggle between. Our first choice is proxy as a participant") Owner: session author Effective Issue: flip the architectural default back to proxy-as-participant (proxy holds a live NetworkStateBinding, publishes a heartbeat, can run the selector locally) while keeping proxy-as-router (thin: redeem-token-and-forward only) as a supported toggle. Both transport.type: sql and transport.type: redis remain peer bindings under the toggle. Supersedes (partial): docs/dev/scratch/PROPOSAL-velocity-redis-startup.md §11 (Phase 2b cut) and §1 framing of Lua scripts as Velocity-scoped. Refines: MULTI_SERVER_PLAN.md Phase 2 ordering; rtp-proxy-ADR-005 scope; rtp-proxy-ADR-006 boot-order step 10.

docs.title: 1. Thesis
docs.text: Two orthogonal axes; v1 ships both as toggles and picks one as the default in each.

docs.title: Axis A - Transport binding (transport.type)
docs.text:
• inMemory (dev/test only).
  • sql - shared SQL database that every backend already talks to (reuses AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor).
  • redis - Lettuce-backed pub/sub + Lua atomic-claim. Lower latency; opt-in.

Default for v1: sql. Redis is a latency optimisation, not a requirement. (See §3 for the SQL binding's shape; §4 for why Lua is scoped to the Redis binding only.)

docs.title: Axis B - Proxy role (proxy.role)
docs.text:
• participant (default). The proxy holds a live NetworkStateBinding open just like any backend does. It publishes a ProxyHeartbeat via ProxyStatePublisher, can run BackendSelector#choose(...) locally against the current NetworkSnapshot, participates in network-wait-queue fairness, and originates /rtp requests as a first-class actor when a player is on the proxy with no current backend. Plan line 73 already names proxies as "ordinary participants" of the shared store - this default makes that explicit.
  • router. The proxy intercepts ServerPreConnectEvent, redeems a reservation token that some backend (or a hub backend running /rtp) already produced, mutates the connect target, and forwards. No selector on the proxy, no ProxyStatePublisher, no live subscriber thread. Lighter footprint; appropriate when a hub backend is doing all the heavy lifting.

The toggle is implicit via wiring in the Velocity adapter, not a separate config knob: under participant the adapter registers ProxyStatePublisher + BackendSelector + transport subscriber; under router it skips those and only wires ServerPreConnectEvent. Both modes consume the same NetworkStateBinding SPI - the binding has no idea which role its caller is playing.

docs.title: What is shared state regardless of role
docs.text:
The following live in the binding's authoritative store (DB tables for sql, Redis keys for redis) - never proxy-local memory, never proxy-to-proxy chatter (plan §Design rules line 77, hub-and-spokes star topology):

  • Region registry
  • Tokenized available-coordinate pool (the cross-network analogue of keptLocations/unkeptLocations)
  • Network wait queue (REQ-RTP-NET-008)
  • Backend heartbeats / load advertisement
  • Proxy heartbeats (proxy_state table, sketched in plan line 750) - written by participants, ignored by routers
  • Kill switch + schemaVersion gate (ADR-010)

This means: switching proxy.role at runtime changes what the local proxy does, but does not change what other network members observe in the shared store - a router-mode proxy simply contributes less to the heartbeat table. Mixed-mode networks (one participant proxy + one router proxy) are well-defined.

docs.title: 2. Phase 2 reordering
docs.text: Phase Was Becomes 2b Velocity adapter + sender + publisher + Brigadier on InMemoryNetworkStateBinding Velocity adapter + sender + publisher + Brigadier + SqlNetworkStateBinding as the default production transport 2c ServerPreConnectEvent + token redemption unchanged (still consumes NetworkStateBinding opaquely) 2d Brigadier /rtp on proxy folded into 2b 2e Redis transport adapter unchanged in scope, demoted in priority: opt-in performance binding, not the recommended default 2f Regression + lite-jar exclusion lite-jar default transport.type: sql (closes open Q5)

docs.title: 3. SqlNetworkStateBinding shape
docs.text:
Implements NetworkTransport + acts as the network-state member on AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor (the slot landed in Phase 1). Tables (one per concern, names indicative, all carry schemaVersion):

  • rtp_network_backends(backend_id PK, world_set, last_heartbeat_at, mspt_p95, tps_1m, load_score, capacity, alive)
  • rtp_network_locations(token PK, backend_id FK, world, x, y, z, produced_at, claimed_at NULL, claimed_by NULL, expires_at)
  • rtp_network_wait_queue(seq PK auto, player_uuid UNIQUE, enqueued_at, network_id)
  • rtp_network_control(network_id PK, kill_switch BOOL, min_schema_version INT, updated_at)

Operations map 1:1 to existing NetworkTransport SPI methods:

  • publishBackendHeartbeat(...) -> UPSERT rtp_network_backends.
  • subscribeBackendHeartbeats(sink) -> polled SELECT on a scheduler tick (configurable interval, default 1s), diffed against last snapshot; sink invoked on change.
  • claimReservationToken(...) -> single-statement UPDATE rtp_network_locations SET claimed_at=..., claimed_by=... WHERE token=? AND claimed_at IS NULL RETURNING .... Atomic on every backend (MySQL 8.0+, Postgres, SQLite via BEGIN IMMEDIATE, H2 via MERGE).
  • releaseReservationToken(...) -> UPDATE ... SET claimed_at=NULL WHERE token=? AND claimed_by=?.
  • Orphan reanimation -> a scheduled sweep on every binding: UPDATE ... SET claimed_at=NULL, claimed_by=NULL WHERE claimed_at IS NOT NULL AND claimed_at + ttl < now(). Identical semantics to ADR-005's Lua sweeper; just slower and bus-friendly.

Determinism guarantee for REQ-RTP-NET-013: every backend reads the same rtp_network_backends snapshot at the same heartbeat tick (within polling skew). WeightedAverageBackendSelector is already deterministic over a snapshot, so the same input -> same decision on every JVM.

docs.title: 4. Lua scripts: scoped to RedisNetworkStateBinding, not Velocity
docs.text:
Correction to PROPOSAL-velocity-redis-startup.md §1 step 10d:

  • SCRIPT LOAD for atomic claim + sweeper-reanimate moves from "Velocity startup step 10d" to "RedisNetworkStateBinding.open() lifecycle step". Velocity's boot calls transport.open(); whatever the transport needs to do internally is opaque to Velocity.
  • The same Lua scripts (and the same EVALSHA invocations) are reused by backend-side callers when a Bukkit/Paper/Folia plugin holds the binding for a backend-originated claim. There is nothing proxy-specific about them.
  • Structural fix in the original proposal: split §1 into two tables - (i) Velocity bootstrap steps (transport-agnostic: 1-9, 11-19), (ii) RedisNetworkStateBinding.open() steps (10a-10e). The Redis table is then reused verbatim by any backend-side caller.

Do we need Lua at all? Yes, but only for RedisNetworkStateBinding. Both scripts (atomic claim, orphan sweep) collapse 2-3 round-trips into one and give strict atomicity that vanilla WATCH/MULTI/EXEC can't match cleanly on Dragonfly/KeyDB. Cost: one SCRIPT LOAD per open(), one EVALSHA per claim. Negligible.

SqlNetworkStateBinding does not use Lua - it uses the database's native atomic-update semantics.

docs.title: 5. Config implications (network.yml, ADR-002)
docs.text:
• transport.type enum gains sql (existing: inMemory, redis).
  • transport.sql.dataSource -> name of an existing entry under the plugin's database config (we reuse AbstractSQLDatabaseAccessor's connection pool; no new HikariCP setup).
  • transport.sql.heartbeatPollMs -> default 1000.
  • transport.sql.tableNamePrefix -> default rtp_network_.
  • Lite-jar default: transport.type: sql (was open Q5 in the original proposal).

ADR-002 is Accepted. Adding the sql enum value is a forward-compatible schema bump (covered by schemaVersion negotiation); not a re-acceptance event.

docs.title: 6. What this does NOT change
docs.text:
• rtp-proxy-common SPI surface: zero changes. SqlNetworkStateBinding is just another implementation, peer to InMemoryNetworkStateBinding. proxy.role is an adapter-side wiring decision, not an SPI concept - the binding has no role parameter.
  • rtp-proxy-velocity Phase 2a (already shipped): unchanged. The no-op shell is still correct under both roles (network.enabled:false short-circuits before role resolution).
  • ADR-005 / ADR-010: still Proposed. This proposal does not flip either. ADR-005 stays scoped to the Redis binding (good as written); ADR-010's HMAC discussion applies to any wire transport (Redis), not to the SQL binding (where the DB connection's own auth and TLS replace HMAC). The participant/router distinction is orthogonal to both ADRs.

docs.title: 7. Open questions
docs.text:
1. Heartbeat polling overhead. A 1s poll on rtp_network_backends from N backends is N SELECTs/sec network-wide. Acceptable for N <= 32; needs LISTEN/NOTIFY (Postgres) or trigger-based fan-out for larger. Defer to ADR if it becomes a problem.
  2. SqlNetworkStateBinding on SQLite. Single-writer; works for tiny networks (1-2 backends sharing a file) but not realistic for proxy-fronted networks. Document as "MySQL/Postgres recommended; SQLite for dev/test only".
  3. HikariCP pool sizing. Network-mode traffic is additive to existing plugin DB traffic. Should the binding own its own small pool, or share the accessor's pool? Recommended: share (one less moving part), but raise maximumPoolSize documentation guidance by +2.
  4. Replay resistance without HMAC. SQL binding leans on DB connection auth + TLS; ADR-010's replay-nonce discussion is N/A. Document this explicitly so ops don't expect the same wire-level protections.

docs.title: 8. Verdict
docs.text:
Adopt this reordering. Concretely:

  1. Amend MULTI_SERVER_PLAN.md Phase 2 ordering per §2 above; add a one-paragraph Proxy roles subsection naming participant as the default and router as the lightweight toggle, citing §1 Axis B of this proposal.
  2. Amend PROPOSAL-velocity-redis-startup.md §1 to split the table per §4 above (Velocity steps vs RedisNetworkStateBinding.open() steps), and §11 to point Phase 2b at SqlNetworkStateBinding with proxy.role: participant as the default wiring path.
  3. Author a new subproject ADR rtp-proxy-ADR-011-sql-network-state-binding.md (Proposed) holding §3 + §5 + §7 of this proposal. ADR-005 stays untouched.
  4. Author a second subproject ADR rtp-proxy-ADR-012-proxy-role-participant-default.md (Proposed) holding §1 Axis B of this proposal: the participant/router toggle, the default selection, the implicit-via-wiring implementation, and the mixed-mode-network well-definedness claim.
  5. Land code in a follow-up D-005 turn (still gated).

No source changes in this turn. Recommended next D-005 turn: ratify steps 1-4 above (still docs-only), then schedule the Phase 2b code cut.

docs.title: AI Translation Plan - Locale TSV Backfill
docs.text:
Scope: backfill untranslated rows in scripts/out/locale-<lang>.tsv for every shipped locale, prioritising German. Source of truth for the pipeline: AGENTS.md > Locale Config TSV Pipeline. Translation conventions: docs/dev/TRANSLATION_GUIDE.md. Parity guard: LocaleParityTest.

Generated: 2026-05-29. Data source: scripts/out/untranslated.tsv (537,879 bytes, 7,836 rows).

Delete this file once the German pass (P1+P2) is submitted and the wider locale sweep has its own checklist.

docs.title: 1. Scan Summary
docs.text:
untranslated.tsv is produced by the locale-CSV pipeline and rows are categorised as:

  • SAME_KEY - the locale TSV's key column equals base_key (no per-locale rename applied).
  • SAME_VALUE - the locale TSV's value column is byte-identical to the English baseline value.
  • SAME_COMMENT - the locale TSV's preceding_comment column is byte-identical to the English comment block.

A row may appear in more than one category (e.g. a single English-as-placeholder string typically triggers all three). The category is informational; the translation work is per (locale, relpath, base_key).

Note: cat is the Internet Cat dialect (see AGENTS.md > Domain Analogies), not Catalan. Treat its rows as creative rewrites, not translations.

docs.title: 3. Execution Workflow (per locale, per file)
docs.text:
Follows AGENTS.md > Locale Config TSV Pipeline verbatim. Per-locale, per-file slice:

  1. Confirm baseline is current: .\scripts\locale-files-to-csv.ps1 (refreshes scripts/out/*.tsv from on-disk YAML; preserves existing translations).
  2. Reconcile structural parity: .\scripts\reconcile-locale-csvs.ps1 (heals stale placeholders; seeds new rows from English).
  3. Translate scripts/out/locale-<lang>.tsv for the target file slice (filter by relpath):
  4. Mask [placeholders], &a/#hex colour codes, Section markers (section U+00A7), and @type / @range / @unit / @default / @options doc tags to sentinels before machine-translating; unmask after.
  5. Translate value first, then key, then preceding_comment. Leading # on every comment line.
  6. Embed newlines as \n and tabs as \t (same escape rules as baseline.tsv).
  7. Translate from English baseline (base_key / baseline value / baseline preceding_comment) - do not pivot through another locale's translated key, that is a double-translation hazard.
  8. Empty cells fall through to baseline English on regen, so partial passes are safe.
  9. Per AGENTS.md > Markdown Encoding Hygiene: UTF-8 only, no BOM, no Windows-1252 double-encoded mojibake (AeUR", AcoeY..., A..., etc.). For German specifically: emit real ae oe ue ss AE OE UE, never the Windows-1252-misread form.
  10. Mark known-stale rows with # TODO(i18n): comment if a confident translation is not possible.
  11. Regenerate: .\scripts\locale-files-from-csv.ps1 rewrites lang/<locale>/<file>.yml and synthesises <file>.lang.yml. Never hand-edit either.
  12. Verify:
  13. .\gradlew :rtp-plugin:test --tests "*LocaleParityTest*" (must stay green).
  14. .\gradlew build (full build per AGENTS.md > Final Full Build).
  15. Commit the regenerated YAML tree + the edited TSV slice + this checklist update in one commit per slice.

docs.title: 3.1 AI translation prompt template (per slice)
docs.text:
You are translating Minecraft plugin strings from English to <Target Language>.
Constraints:
  - Preserve all [placeholders] (square-bracketed tokens) and color codes (&a, &7, #2636ef, section-markers) byte-for-byte.
  - Preserve YAML escape sequences (\n, \t) and the leading "# " of every comment line.
  - Preserve @type, @range, @unit, @default, @options doc tags verbatim.
  - Translate only natural-language prose. Do not translate code identifiers, version strings, URLs.
  - Target audience for messages.yml: a player in chat. Use the informal "du" register for German.
  - Target audience for *.yml comments and operator-facing strings: a server administrator. Use the neutral / polite register.
  - Use ASCII hyphen ("-"), colon (":") or parentheses instead of em/en dashes (per AGENTS.md > Markdown Encoding Hygiene rule 7).
  - Output must be UTF-8, no BOM. Emit real "ae oe ue ss" - never Windows-1252 misreads.
Input rows (TSV slice): <paste>
Output: same TSV row layout, only the value / key / preceding_comment columns changed.

Run one file per slice. After each slice, run step 5 before moving to the next slice. Do not batch multiple locales through the same prompt - the German pass is the model for the others and validates the workflow.

docs.title: 4. Verification Strategy
docs.text:
• Parity (structural): LocaleParityTest - already green; must remain green after every slice.
  • Spanish content guard: ReqRtpF013SpanishLocaleContentTest - do not edit. If the es pass later trips it, the translation is wrong, not the test.
  • Mojibake sweep: per AGENTS.md > Markdown Encoding Hygiene rule 5, search_project for AeUR, Ac, AcoY, ? (U+FFFD) inside the regenerated lang/<locale>/ tree before commit. Any hit in your diff is a defect.
  • Visual sanity check (German): on a Paper devstack, run /rtp and confirm at least the rotating quick-win strings render in German: alreadyTeleporting, teleportCancel, unsafe, cooldownMessage, queueUpdate.
  • Final full build: .\gradlew build after each locale pass.

docs.title: 5. Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Adding new baseline keys (that is a separate baseline-edit pass; this plan only translates existing rows).
  • Hand-editing any lang/<locale>/*.yml or *.lang.yml. All edits go through the TSV pipeline.
  • Forge / NeoForge locales (out of project scope, per AGENTS.md > Current Development Focus).
  • Catalan (ca) - not shipped; do not confuse with cat Internet-Cat dialect.
